review_body: We are using this as a baby monitor. We first got the older version of this because it was $20 cheaper. It took 2 hours to figure out how to hook it up to the wifi. Then, when we tried to download the app on our phones, it said it didn't work with the older model. We returned it for this plug and play. You literally just scan the QR Code and within 5 minutes the whole thing is set up and works with the app. Image is fantastic and night vision looks great too. Tons of features that we probably won't even use, but good to have. Also has a mic and speaker so you can hear your baby and talk to them. You can set the volume in the app so that the alarm is more or less sensitive to sound. Highly recommend, especially for under $80!  Update: Feb 2017: Camera has had a lot of glitches over the 1.5yrs we've had it, including disconnecting from the wifi on a regular basis. It freezes when watching on your phone, so you have to close out and go back in. Now, after 1.5yrs, it has completely stopped working.

review_headline: Perfection, thy name is QKOO. These are absolutely amazing.
review_body:
You know, you should probably just buy these and then finish reading the reviews, on the off chance that you're near the deadline for shipping. Why? Because you want these ASAP.

Here's why:

(1) They're a perfect size for most uses - big enough for glasses, screens, phone displays, watches... anything. Not too big, not too small. Awesome all around size.

(2) They work *beautifully*. Obviously, that's the most important requirement, and these deliver in spades. They clean well, they wash up nicely for reuse, and they work use after use after use eve when not washed in between.

(3) They are individually packaged. This is fantastic - buy a bunch, toss some into glove boxes, suitcases, briefcases, purses, backpacks... you'll have a fresh, clean, unused microfiber cloth when you need it, and the price per cloth is crazy low, so there's no issue with getting extras.

(4) They are thin enough to keep one in all your laptops - keep one on the keys, and it's always there to clean your screen. You can buy sizes that are better for this purpose, but these do the trick and are very inexpensive.

Get whatever color(s) you like. You will not regret this purchase, and odds are good that you'll buy them again. Especially if, like me, you're a nice guy (or gal) and give them to friends in need.

Note: I bought a [[ASIN:B01042PWTC different package of these same cloths]], but the review applies these, as they're the same microfiber cloths.

review_body:
I have a non-digital Canon Rebel SLR and I didn't want to have to purchase all new lenses, so when looking for a DSLR, I wanted to stick with camera bodies that were compatible. The Rebel T5 fit the bill. Not only are my existing red dot lenses compatible, but I have always been extremely pleased with my non-digital Rebel. I had read a few reviews that said the quality of shots with this camera isn't necessarily as good as some other higher priced cameras, but I'm not a professional photographer, so that didn't bother me.

I'm happy I didn't listen to those reviews. I'm very pleased with this camera. My shots look professional and are a much higher quality than any point and shoot camera. Plus, since it's a DSLR, I still have control over my settings. I suspect this camera will last me for years to come.

The package that came with the camera was nice. The small tripod is good quality and I really appreciate the extra battery. I'm not sure if I will use the extra hand strap, but the tripod and extra battery are well worth it.

product_title: Arlo Smart Home - 1 HD Camera Security System
review_headline: Inconsistent performance, not a surveillance system
review_body:
If I could, I would give this camera system zero stars.

I purchased this system from Best Buy with the four cameras and used it for 2 weeks. I really wanted it to work because in theory it's great. Simply put, the cameras don't do what is advertised. Since it's based on motion activation, you would think they have that dialed in but it's the biggest flaw. The motion detection is extremely inconsistent and there's no rhyme or reason in terms of what part of the screen actually actuates the motion detection. As such, there were way too many occasions where people and things walk directly in front of the camera with no motion detected and therefore, no recording.

Example: I had a camera on the corner of the backyard which covered the porch, an area that obviously gets a lot of foot traffic. I could walk directly in front of the camera, approximately 10 feet from it and get absolutely no activation. I would have to get within 2 to 3 feet of the camera before it would detect motion.

Also, even with full wifi signal, the feeds would take often 10 seconds or more to load on the mobile app and that's if it does actually loads. More than enough times it would simply have no signal. The often mentioned complaint of the delay in start of recording after motion detected is also very real.

The system is just not consistent enough to be used as a surveillance system. Whether it's a hardware or software issue, this system is not ready for prime time. It's more like a toy or a beta test phase. Don't waste your money. It's only going to give you a headache.

review_headline: Great batteries and chargers with irrelevant accessories
review_body:
I was happy to have ordered this pack as I needed extra batteries for my camcorder. The original battery doesn't last long enough for many events. I received this package and charged up the two batteries prior to a family wedding. As it turned out, I needed all three batteries by the time the night was over. The batteries from this package lasted longer than the original battery and will be good to have for future events.

The included charger works, but takes longer to charge a battery completely than the charger that came with the camcorder. Still, it's handy as an extra charger and is less bulky to take on the road. [[VIDEOID:9542c83e6a926d541d8df1e6c0b71a77]]I grew up with binoculars, but I was never a huge fan because I have trouble getting the eye pieces spaced properly for a cohesive image. As such, I've become a bigger fan of monoculars because they are so easy to use. They are also more compact than binoculars.

I made a video that compares four different Intsun optics: two compact binoculars and two monoculars. It's pretty long at nearly eight minutes, so I'll summarize the highlights for this model below.

This 6x18 version is SUPER compact. Even the carrying case is plenty small to fit into a pocket (but it also has a belt loop). The size is its main selling point, IMO. The image quality is pretty decent, but you do pay a price for having this compact size. The 6x magnification works well, and the 18mm aperture lets in a decent amount of light - but it is dimmer than optics with larger apertures, including Intsun's own [[ASIN:B011NBWLXS 8x30 monocular]] (which happens to be my favorite out of the four models that I tried). While not the brightest, the optics are clear without aberrations, and I can't see any trapped dust or other marks on the lenses. The main body is easy to grip with two or three fingers and your thumb, and it is nicely made. The eye cup isn't my favorite, being flexible rubber - which is nice in that you can fold it down if you wear glasses, but I prefer rigid cups that let you adjust their distance from the lens. When you twist the end to adjust the focus, the rubber eye cup twists, too. Like the other models, it comes with a carrying case, lens cloth, and carrying strap.

Pros:
(*) Performance and measurements are true to the 6x18 specs
(*) Incredibly compact, both the monocular and the carrying case, making this super easy to keep with you
(*) Adjusting the focus is easy and not overly sensitive
(*) Well made and robust build quality
(*) Good quality carrying case
(*) Carrying strap is removable (and, hence, replaceable if you wanted)

Consideration:
(*) 18mm aperture is great for such a compact unit, but just know that the view won't be as bright as with a larger aperture
(*) The flexible eye cup might arrive out of round like mine did (I got two different models with this type of flexible material, and both showed up that way)
(*) There are no lens caps, which isn't my preference. Even when it's in the protective case, you will probably want to be careful to not have the carrying strap rub up against one of the lenses

If you're willing to go a bit bigger and spend a bit more, their 8x30 model is a noticeable (and I think worthwhile) step up in performance.

review_headline: Not Impressive but not terrible for the price.
review_body:
EDIT (21 Aug 2015): A huge, huge inconvenience of this product forces me to take off another star in my review. Apparently, there is no way to change the time on the camera and all your footage will default to "12/31/2009 11:00PM" on the file's timestamp. Of course for people who just like to point and shoot, upload their files, then delete them, this is but a minor trifle, but for me, I like to have an accurate timestamp so that I can archive the footage I shoot throughout my life. Unfortunately, the manual offers no way to do this and there no online sources out there to help. Again, it's terribly inconvenient for me to not be in control of things like this. Also, I would like to take back what I said about using this as a backup camera. I've been test shooting footage in 720p and the colors are just smudged and not very good looking unless you are planning on shrinking the footage down to another 16:9 resolution that is 640 x 360 or LOWER. I may use this as a back facing cam on my helmet. Personally, I would avoid this 720p midland camera and look into the newer models from midland.

I'm normally very critical of action cams when I'm buying one to replace an older one--- but in this case, I hadn't planned to buy the 720p Midland XTC200. I was looking at the 1080p model and was iffy so I repaired my broken down Sony AS10 and went with that. I noticed this camera on sale and kept it in my cart for a while before deciding to try it out. It was less than $20 so if I didn't like it too much, I could still keep it as a backup camera or lend it out to friends.

Here's what I found. I bought this from warehouse deals so I didn't expect all the accessories to be present but after opening the box, I found that everything was more or less thrown in there: A mount for the waterproof case with 3 sticky pads, the camera and waterproof case and lanyards for both (which I removed because they were fussy and tangled up). I briefly flipped through the manuals and learned nothing about switching between 720p and 480p mode but I highly doubt I will be using anything other than 720p.

The mount had me worried the most because the instructions again were unclear and I was afraid I'd snap it in half, but worked it in after a while. Slides right onto the rails on the case. Don't force it in. If you have to force it in then you're most likely doing something wrong.

The dimenions of the camera are slimmer than my Sony AS10 (but of course the quality is nowhere near comparable to those of the AS10). I threw an old SD card in (8gb class 4) to test out the footage. Everything was shot in 720p, 140 degrees.

Everything was recorded inside the waterproof case. While my voice was not completely blocked out, I could barely make much out besides rustling and bumping around. That's something midland could try to work into their design. Some sort of filter or diaphragm to allow sound vibrations to pass through without letting water pass through. Viable but was not implemented sadly. Speaking of vibrations, I did not experience any jelloing driving in my car or walking which lends itself to the hardware of the camera, so that was good. The bad: The submersible case doesn't grip the camera well enough so the camera is bouncing around inside the case vertically if you shake it up and down which is murder to your ears when you playback the footage and listen to the THUNK THUNK THUNK as if you were inside a washing machine with a rocks thrown around.

In lower light situations, the camera has an umbearable amount of grain and interlacing (like in the photo I included of my car inside the garage). You do not want to be shooting with this camera in those situations. Anything beyond 50 meters will be a blurry mess even in broad daylight. On the other hand, I was happy to see that the overall picture was nice especially anything that is close up (compared to a fake SJ4000 I was unfortunate enough totest).

A good camera if you do not mind shooting 720p with poor background details and lots of grain in low light situations. Otherwise I'd recommend Sony 1080p action cams for casual shooters on a budget.

One more thing I'd like to note is that there are three light on the midland camera. One for SD card, one for battery and one for REC. All of them are color coded (details are in the manual) to indicate things like battery level and storage capacity. There is a slide instead of a power on/off button and sliding the camera ON will light up the SD and battery lights (unless one or both are dead/out of space). 7-8 seconds later, the REC light will start blinking indicating that the camera is recording. The delay is a bit annoying.

product_title: Zhiyun Z1-Pround 3-Axis High-Precision Handheld Steady Gimbal PTZ Camera Mount with Built-In Independent IMU Module Stabilizer Extra Power Charger for GoPro Hero 1/2/3/3+/4 - Silver/Black
review_headline: Great product, does exactly what I wanted it to do.
review_body: Very nice accessory. At first glance it seemed to be very simple and I was not expecting too much from it. Then I've played with it a bit more and I've discovered what's really "under the hood". This unit has three modes, for different types of filming. 1. With the yellow LED blinking fast - the X axis (left-right) is fixed.   The Y axis (up and down) is tilting the camera up and down, as you move your hand.   This could be useful if you were filming a room or a cave, and if you wanted to smoothly transition, from the ceiling to the floor.   The Z axis (a wrist twist) works, and it softly follows the twisting of your wrist.  A gentle nudge turns the camera.   In this mode the black, up and down buttons tilt the camera left and right.   You can us these buttons to level the camera, i.e. with a bubble level. You can do it ONLY in this mode, and the level is remembered in the next two modes. 2. With the yellow LED blinking slowly both X and Y axis are fixed.   That means - no matter how you tilt your wrist - up and down or left and right - the camera stays put on the subject.   The Z axis (a wrist twist) works same as in the previous mode.   This mode could be useful for filming from a front seat of a car, or a bicycle.  You would see what's ahead of you all the time.   In this mode the black up and down buttons tilt the camera up and down. 3. With a yellow LED steady on all three axis are fixed.   This is very interesting. No matter how you tilt it the camera stays fixed  at what's ahead.   Even the Y axis is fixed. You can twist your wrist as much as you want - it will not change the angle.   This can be useful for filming from a SIDE window of a car.   If you can avoid LIFTING camera up and down you will get very nice side view shots.   It can also be useful for filming wide, stationary object, i.e. a holiday table full of food.   You can move a camera from one end of a table to another and it will stay "flat" against the edge of a table.   Sort of like putting it on a straight railing.   I sat down in my office chair and I spun around.   The camera stayed fixed and when I turned my chair 180 degrees, the lens ended up "looking" at me.   This is a really cool mode!  Great for video selfies, with a pan/twist. Ha!   In this mode the black up and down buttons tilt the camera up and down.  The middle black button has three functions: - press it for three seconds - the servo motors are off.  The whole thing goes limp. Yellow LEDs are off.   Press it again for 3 seconds - it comes back to life. - press it twice, quickly - you get into fast yellow LED mode - press it for two seconds - you get into slow blinking LED mode   There is a mechanical on/off switch in the bottom of the handle, where the battery cap is. It shuts the unit down completely.  Overall - great product, priced reasonably.  You get a lot of bang for your buck here.  Pros: - three advanced modes, useful for different filming techniques - solid, metal design - good battery life - I've played with it for four hours and there was till some 'juice' left in them. - very nice storage box, with a pre-cut foam inserts.   I wouldn't want to just throw it in a duffel bag and damage the mechanism.   The original box serves perfectly as a protective case. - clear battery indicator - blue LED. Four blinks - full battery.  Three, two or one - the battery level gets lower. - a handle can be extended with additional monopod-like tubes.   That calls for great crane shots, except you pay $25 for it and don't have to carry a $5,000 crane with you.   How do you explain a crane in your luggage, to a TSA officer, right? - the unit is small and it doesn't scream "professional photographer with expensive gear", to potential bad guys. - modern, elegant design.  Cons: - the manual is awful! It's one page, one side in Chinese, and the other side is in Engrish. Yes, I said Engrish with an "r".  You know what I mean..   As bad as the manual is written - theletters are so small 'nobody' could read it without a magnifying glass.   Skip the Mandarin page and print the thing in a normal font, thank you very much. - the manual doesn't explain how to change modes.  I had to figure it out on my own. - I wish I wouldn't have to remove the batteries to charge them.  There is a USB port on the side but it's not for charging. (service?)   I hope the batteries will last for a while because they seem to be some odd size - smaller than C but larger than AA.   An external charger is included and it works with a micro USB cable. Pretty much a standard, these days. - the unit is not waterproof.   Not expected at this price level but I would hope it would be water resistant (meaning it would survive a few drops of rain).   It's not mentioned anywhere, in the manual (no surprise there...) -  There are two brackets for mounting a GoPro camera. Both plastic, with flimsy copper screws, inside. I will have to be VERY careful with them.  I would recommend this product.  It does what I wanted it to do and more. I take good care of my electronics so it will probably serve me well. A person who's not patient, who does faster than he thinks may be disappointed with it. Overall - I like it and I'll keep it. Maybe I'll post some videos later, when I take it for a 'test drive', in a real world.

product_title: The Imaging World Canon EOS Rebel T5 18.0 MP CMOS DSLR Kit with EF-S 18-55mm IS II, 75-300mm III Lens, Wide-Angle Lens, Telephoto Lens and Accessories (19 Items)
review_headline: Focus on the camera and the lenses. Don't pay to much attention to the rest.
review_body:
There's really nothing to say about (or against) the Canon T5 body or the Canon lenses. There are far better lenses from Canon, and the combo leaves out a range from 55mm to 70mm, which is an excellent focal space for portraits, but for the price, there's really nothing do complain about. The two small lenses (macro and 2x) seems promising, but I've hadn't have the chance to test them yet. Also, the (really) small bag is not only cute, but very useful, specially for small outings or if you are not planning on adding lenses to the pack. The filters are fine enough. The remote shutter also looks promising, but I haven't tested it yet. The memory cards are very basic, good enough for storing pictures, but you'll need to buy a faster one for video recordings (not my aim).
Having said that, you can simply throw away the tripod and the flash. Complete rubbish. Both of them. Don't use them to choose this pack over some other. Forget that they are there.
Do I recommend it? Yes. Despite the obvious low price of most of the stuff in it, the combo still shows an excellent cost vs. benefit ratio. Think it that way: you'll be buying the camera and two original lenses, plus two memory cards and a set of filters for a very good price. The rest of the pack, don't wait for pristine stuff, and actually be prepared to simply throw away some of it.

review_headline: Don't buy a baby monitor! This Camera is great!!
review_body: Don't waste your time or money on a baby monitor!! We care for my 97 year old grandfather who is a fall risk. I used our baby monitor to keep an eye on him but since his room is at the opposite end of the house, I couldn't keep a signal. Also, whenever an electronic device turned on that used the same frequency, it would cut out. Not to mention the tiny little screen that looked like an ultra sound (this was a top of the line monitor with the longest possible range). Anyway, on to the good news. I bought this camera to connect to the internet so that I would have better range and no interruption. The camera has a great picture, very clear night vision that turns on automatically. You can turn in 360* from your phone or tablet and up and down plus zoom. Such a great feature! It was easy to install on both my Iphone, my Samsung Galaxy and my Ipad. I tried to get it on the Kindle but of course that's not the right system (not the camera's fault). It says you can connect on a computer through a website, which is true. However, when you go to the website your computer will highly recommend you slowly back away from the security threats. I chose to not proceed. I doubt any creepers want to watch an old man sleep but it was still concerning. Because I want to have it on constantly to see if he needs help (as opposed to the occasional glance) I had to turn the power save option off of my devices otherwise I'd have to restart the app, restart the feed and hope he hadn't gotten up while I didn't notice. Of course this is going to drain the power much faster so I bought a portable device charger (Jackery) which I'm hoping will solve the problem. An absolute fantastic buy!

product_title: Polaroid Z2300 10MP Digital Instant Print Camera
review_headline: Super fun, digital camera/video/printer all in one!
review_body:
Being of the "Poloarid generation," I was excited to see this camera. I wasn't quite sure how it would work...would I need to replace ink cartridges? how will the picture "develop"? Would I be able to use it as a digital camera as well? What I found is that basically you get a 10MP camera with an on-board 2'x3' photo printer! The camera has all the features of a point and shoot digital camera...I haven't played around with it, but there is even image stabilization. You can zoom, you can record video at 720p, you can add an SD card to store your photos...but the fun part comes when you are able to instantly print out the pictures you like the best.

The printer (right in the camera) prints out little 2"x3" photos (which can also become stickers if you peel off the backing. There is no ink...yes, inkless printing! There are fun little frames you can add to the photos too. I was pretty impressed with the speed and print quality. The camera is a little larger/bulkier than other point and shoot cameras, but it does have to hold the paper and all the printer mechanisms, so it makes sense. The display on the back is very large. The paper is a little pricey (you pay about .50 for a picture - buy it on Amazon in bulk), but considering you can CHOOSE which picture to print (which was never the case with the original Polaroid cameras), and there are not ink cartridges to replace, the price is pretty fair.

If you want a fun camera that lets you print out cute pictures instantly, I would recommend this camera. It's not for those wanting professional type photographers. This would be an amazing thing to use at parties, weddings (guests take pics of themselves?), classrooms (pictures of the kiddos on mother day cards, etc), or even around the house - making chore charts or visual boards for kids. So many options! I think teens would really love this camera as well - I know mine do!

product_title: Qkoo Selfie Handheld Extendable Stick Pole Monopod + Mini Tripod + Phone Holder Mount Kit Set for Apple iPhone 6 Plus 5 6 5s 5c 4 4s Samsung Galaxy S5 S4 S3 Note 4 3 2 Blackberry Sony Xperia HTC One LG PS2
review_headline: Ok If Used Carefully, Limited In Some Situations
review_body:
The selfie stick screwed into a compact camera works really well. The stick in combination with the phone holder is only just ok, you'll either need to use the camera timer, or get a separate bluetooth remote, and the grip is also questionable and not good with phones thicker than 8mm. It also has a problem with rotating when the stick isnt fully extended. The stick can't be used on top of the tripod, it just falls over. The tripod with the phone holder is very light weight and will blow over in the wind but it's fine inside. Overall the package is ok, but quite limited due to design flaws.

SELFIE STICK 3/5
The build quality is good, the handle is rubber, and extremely grippy. The bottom tripod mounting hole, telescopic pole, and tripod screw at the top are all metal which is good. The head where you attach the phone holder is plastic but it seems to be strong after giving it a lot of vigorous shakes. The screw to tighten it is also metal but I found it loosened a little. It works good with compact cameras, and ok with gopros.

The problem with the selfie stick is that if you shake it the camera starts to tilt/rotate sideways, especially if it's not fully extended. There are no grooves in the metal pole to stop it from rotating sideways. Also, there is no bluetooth or any kind of connection, so you will need a bluetooth remote trigger or use the self timer on the camera.
It measures 8.5" closed, and 42" fully extended.

MINI TRIPOD 2/5
The mini tripod is made almost entirely of plastic, even the ball head and tripod screw... It kind of grinds when you adjust it, and the screw already partially striped when trying to screw into the bottom of the selfie stick, it just keeps rotating in the hole, but it screws into cameras and the phone holder fine. It's ok if you want something ultra light for a compact cameras, or phones with the phone holder, but it's not sturdy enough to stay standing on a windy day, and the thin aluminium legs dont stay extended after repositioning it a few times. I have a model that looks exactly like it that's made entirely out of metal and it worked really good, but this plastic one is subpar.

PHONE HOLDER 3/5
The phone holder is made out of plastic and metal. It's spring loaded and will hold phones and thin compact cameras ranging from 55-75mm wide, and up to 8mm thick (thicker will be less secure). With my galaxy S4, it fits nicely in the indent, but if it's not fully pushed in, it slips out with a few shakes. It's also less secure with my phone case on and giving it a few vigorous shakes causes it to pop out. It's only good if it's not shaken, and should be checked between uses. The top grip should be wider and grippier rubber, and the bottom grip should be angled rubber instead of flat foam. It's good on a tripod, but I dont trust it on the stick.

review_headline: Cheap solution for home or small office security video
review_body: I have the FN3004H and, after setup help from Foscam Tech Support, I am pretty satisfied. The initial setup is complicated as you need to hook up the device to a monitor and a USB mouse. That is necessary to program the username and password, but thereafter the monitor and mouse are no longer needed as you can then control the device  on your Windows or MAC computer. However you can choose to keep a connected screen for permanent monitoring. My initial setup did not go well as for one reason or another my 4 Foscam cameras seemed to have some kind of IP conflict, but when I contacted Foscam Tech support, they took remote control of my computer and set up the device perfectly. I added a Samsung M3 hard disk and you really need a (compatible) hard disk to take full advantage of the NVR. I set up 3 of my cameras to activate on motion detection and 1 camera on a schedule of continuous recording. To review activity, you choose the camera(s) that you want to see, click 'search' and then click on the play icon. If you review motion detection activity, it is best not to include from the search a camera that has been set up for scheduled recording, so that the review goes faster. There are 5 different speeds for recording review and you can start the review at any time of the day (meaning you don't have to review a whole day if you look for a specific time of the day). One useful function is that you can program the NVR to record up to 5 seconds before motion detection activity. Between the NVR and the hard disk, this setup cost me about $ 140 and I find it well worth the price. I took off one star of this review because there is no App for Iphone or Ipad for this device. Furthermore, the online description on Foscam's  website lists that the NVR includes a USB mouse, IR cable and a network cable, but neither came with my purchase. ----------- Two weeks later ---------- I continue to have problems with my four Foscam cameras that I did not have before I installed the NVR.  Every few days one of my cameras goes to factory default or just changes its 192.168.1.XX address . This makes it that the NVR no longer accesses the camera. I have hooked up the cameras to wifi access points which allows me to reprogram the cameras without having to connect a factory defaulted camera directly to a computer. The NVR clearly  creates some kind of  (IP ?) conflict with the cameras which Foscam should correct with a firmware upgrade. I have downgraded my rating to 2 stars until this conflict has been resolved. ----------- Three weeks later --------- Performance has improved since (again) I asked Foscam Tech Support for help. Through remote control of my computer, they changed network settings of each camera to static. This being said, occasionally  a camera stops connecting to the NVR all together. I have now added a ZWave switch to two of my cameras which allows me to remotely reboot the cameras. Remember that I did not have these issues before installing the NVR. So, my current setup is : two 8909 cameras and two 8910 cameras, one 3004 NVR All four cameras are connected to WiFi access points, which allow me to reconfigure the camera if randomly it goes back to factory default. without having to connect the camera directly to a computer. I have also backed-up the settings for each camera, so no need to reprogram a camera after a factory default reset. However, such backup does not include PT settings. Two cameras are powered through a ZWave switch, allowing remote reboot if they stop connecting. My setup with the addition of WiFi access points and ZWave switches makes the system more expensive, but if it works then ok with me. So far (now) the system is usable, but I strongly recommend that Foscam looks at possible conflicts between the NVR and its cameras. By the way, Foscam Tech Support is very friendly and helpful (and free !!!) but agents often don't look beyond the specific issue and therefore it required (in my case) follow-up calls to tech support while the first agent could have resolved all issues. ------------------------ 5 Months later _____________ The NVR has now been working for almost 5 months without any issue. Apparently the changes suggested by Foscam as well as some tweeks I made myself, work out. I upgrade my rating to a 4 star.

review_headline: Good IP Camera, Low resolution of video, needs to be improved, mobile apps work well
review_body: I always wanted to have some sort of surveillance system in my home. Not some professionally installed stuff which will run into hundreds or thousands of dollars but something to start with so as to know if this thing even works for my requirement. What the package contains..  Conbrov Wifi Camera Mini USB Cable (not MicroUSB) Silicon Cover for the Camera 3 different mounts for the camera MicroSD Card Reader (no MicroSD Card included) Neck Strap User Manual “CCTV in Operation” Warning sticker  Phew ! This is a long list of items which come in the package. Now I had read the reviews on this camera from others and I had seen lot of negative ones as well. So I was well prepared to know what I was getting into. So lets see how I went about using this camera. First of all I needed to download the mobile app and I see one reviewer mentioning that the “Mini Wifi Cam” worked for him and not the manufacturer recommended one. So what I did was to install both the apps on my iPhone to see if the issue really persists. I never tried the wifi cam app first and tried the one recommended in the manual. I first charged the camera for some time but then I thought that it is better I connect it to a power bank so it does not die while I am checking it out.  There is a ON/OFF Switch on one side and you use that to turn on the camera. On the right side of the lens is the MicroSD Card holder and the AP/P2P Switch. First I wanted to configure the camera to setup as an IP Camera so i could see the live feed even when I am out of house over my phone’s 3G/4G Network. I went to wifi settings and connected the camera to my home’s wifi (TPLink that you see in list). But remember that using your mobile phone you need to first connect the phone to your camera directly. Once that is done, then only you use fire up the app and connect the camera to wifi network. Sort of like how you setup google chromecast.  Now once you have fed your home wifi’s password in the “Mini IP Cam” apps wifi settings area. This way your camera will connect to your home’s wifi. Add the camera from within the app. Now you can use the app to view the live feed on your mobile. I had kept the external switch on AP and I was able to directly view the live feed on mobile over my wifi network. Basically the camera and phone both were on same wif network. The footage was very smooth on my wifi. I have a 15 Mbps down and 1 Mbps Up connection. Now I changed the external switch to P2P and again tried to connect to the camera using the app. Initially it wasn’t able able to connect to the app. It seems you need to wait some time. I was able to now connect the camera over 4G network.  Please mind that the live feed when viewed over 3G connection is pretty choppy. I am yet t try a situation where I am in my office and using office’s wifi network to view the live feed from my home. Also I am not sure if my understanding is correct but I believe that in AP mode I should be able to view remotely and P2P means local viewing. But the opposite happens. You can see various pictures I have attached so you know how the app looks on iPhone.  I did not try the MicroSD so I have no idea if it will record properly or not. I will try to update this review if I do try that my purpose is more of using as wifi cam. You can see how my setup is currently. I haven’t really made any attempt to make it look discreet because I am still experimenting with the camera. I have observed that I can see the time on top left side when I am viewing the live feed over Data network. You can check my phone’s screenshot which clearly shows I am using data network to view the footage.  There are also options to enable motion detection or sound an alarm or send email when alarm is triggered. I haven’t yet tried all these things.  Some Issues I have found till now are I am not sure if the P2P and AP are reversed or my understanding is wrong. Choppy video over data network even when such low resolution recording. At least 720p recording or 480p should have been provided.  Apart from these things, I am as of now satisfied with the camera. If I find something else I will update this review. I received this product i exchange of my honest and unbiased review and all the opinions mentioned above are based on my usage with the product.

product_title: Fujinon XF90mmF2 R LM WR
review_body:
I've owned a Fujifilm X100 (sold for X100s), X100s, X-E2, 18-55mm OIS, 35mm f/1.4, 56mm f/1.2, Zeiss 12mm f/2.8 and a couple flashes. I'm biased towards my positive experiences in the system and the "look" I get from the jpegs (which are amazing btw) and RAW. With that in mind ...

I love this lens. This and the 56mm were the two I most looked forward to. I do a lot of candid shots of people and more shots of my pets than I want to admit. I used to think the 56mm is the ultimate portrait lens, but in many ways this eclipses it (both have great merits).

For starters 90mm is a great portrait focal length. ~85mm-95mm is probably the most common one for DSLR users these days, and it's much more flattering than ~50mm. Cropping helps with some things, but good ole fashioned focal lengths help with conveying depth, or in this case slightly compressing it. 90mm will start to make features more subtle (the extreme opposite effect can be seen in ultra wides which can fill a frame with a nose), and most of us look better with subtle features. That model in a magazine or catalog was probably photoshopped, but pick up old magazines. They still looked great. Yeah there were some darkroom tricks, but it's not uncommon to see 135mm-300mm used in studios to compress features. Fuji didn't invent this effect, but it's one huge leg up this lens has on the already stellar 56mm f/1.2. 90mm generally is better than 56mm for portraits (1.5x focal length crops really don't matter here, but even if you think they do, 135mm is better than 85mm).

Onto this particular lens. It's really your only option for the X system outside of adapters and manually focusing with a lens from another system, but even if you could magically put a Nikon or Canon 85mm lens on with AF and everything, this lens has them beat. It's amazingly sharp edge to edge. You will get a noticeable bump in sharpness stopping down to 2.8, but honestly it's good to go wide open. Sharpness is just one aspect, and while easy to see/measure, it's probably less important than contrast (my opinion at least). This lens excels there as well. Pictures really shine with a very crisp clear yet flattering look. It's not quite up to the best Zeiss glass (sadly neither does the Zeiss glass available for the X system), but it's quite remarkable, and better than my Nikon primes.

It is heavy, but it handles surprisingly well on my X-E2. I'd prefer a X-T1 and a grip, but It's not too bad, nor do I worry about my strap lugs pulling out. The generously sized MF barrel (no surprise, as there's no need for a zoom) is well damped, but I'm not generally a fan of MF feel on the X system. The aperture ring is a nice step up from earlier ones on the 35mm f/1.4 that seemed to lose their place a bit too easily. In both cases, my old Nikon glass does still leave me wanting here (direct manual focus and an aperture lock), but that old glass has nothing on this. Autofocus isn't a strength here again, but it's no worse than other X system glass. Plenty for portraits. Not ideal for moving subjects (unless they are parallel to focal plane).

The rest is all good. Modest but generally low distortion, flare, and CA (distortion and CA should be fixed automatically), and ghosting is all but a non issue. Compared to the 56mm f/1.2, I'd say this is a better portrait lens, and it's a bit better all around (YMMV and sometimes 56mm fits the bill better than 90mm no matter the lens). The basis for this is the overall sharpness wide open (though stop down the 56mm to f/2 and it's comparable), more flattering focal length, and better close focusing. The 56mm f/1.2 has a greater minimum focal length. It's a real tour de force and statement with the f/1.2 max aperture, but this lens is a bit more practical. Then again, I enjoy owning both. Plus the same grads, polarizers, NDs, etc... work on both.

Do I recommend this lens? For some,absolutely. If you're already using the system and and you're comfortable using primes, it's highly recommended. I'm quite delighted!re comfortable using primes, it's highly recommended. I'm quite delighted!

review_body: I got this Q-See QTH916-10AI-1 16 CH HD System with 10 x 720p Cameras, 1TB Hard Drive to upgrade from the QM97038 8 channel system with 4 cameras. The Qm97038 has worked well for me so far but the cameras don't pick up well enough in complete dark. Comes with white cables instead of black but they are thicker which is nice. The Hard drive is the same 1TB but the box is larger and has a loud fan. I use this system in my home and have the cables run up through the basement floor into my living room, the old system was barely detectable, the new sounds like a playstation3 running, considering putting the hard rice in basement and running just the monitor into the living room to reduce noise level. Other than that the software is the same or so similar I haven't noticed any difference yet. The access to recorded data does seem faster. The cameras do have visible infrared, people can see them in the dark but I like that they will know they are being recorded. Only draw back on that is they attract bugs and moths, which in turn attract spiders who build webs around the cameras. I suggest placing them at a level you can clean then off with a broom but high enough to deter vandalism.

review_headline: I have used Q-See cameras and recorders before, but these are higher resolution than the other cameras I have installed.
review_body: I have used Q-See cameras and recorders before, but these are higher resolution than the other cameras I have installed.  The picture is clear, and the night vision works well.  I am using these mainly inside, and I get a clear picture in a totally dark room.  It is pretty easy to set these up so you can view them over the internet.  You will need to know how to do port forwarding on your router, and it helps (but isn't absolutely necessary) if you have a static IP from your provider.  If you don't get a static IP automatically, you may be able to add it on to your plan for an additional cost.  The recorder works well, and is also easy to set up.  You will need to connect it to a monitor, and it has both HDMI and regular RGB, so a computer monitor or a TV will work fine.  This set comes with four cameras, but has inputs for four more.  The hardest part of the install is running the wires.  I do have a suggestion for Q-See.  All of the included wires are at least 50' long, and they don't sell shorter ones.  I could really use some that are about 10' long, with additional sizes between there and the 50' ones.

review_body: You DO NOT want to buy these cameras.  There are two primary reasons.  First, they do not work on modern WiFi frequencies.  Second, and this is FAR more important, they drop the WiFi signal if a pigeon farts.  And, when they do, they do not reacquire unless you MANUALLY unpower and repower.  Hence, they are USELESS for an unattended monitoring purpose.  If you have a vacation home and the internet powers off then comes back on you must send a human in to physically reset the camera in order for it to reacquire its WiFi link.  What'smore, the manufacture freely admits this and acknowledges it is a firmware problem which they are "aware of and working on."  Meanwhile, you are stuck with a beautiful to look at but not particularly useful piece of tech.  I really hated writing this review because these cameras are simply elegant to set up and lovely in the room.  Sadly, they fail in operation.  Independently tested and verified on four units.  Sorry.

product_title: DJI Phantom 3 Professional Parent
review_headline: I don't think a Ready-to-Fly Quad Copter could get much better than this!!
review_body:
The best Phantom so far. I've had the Phantom 1, Phantom 2, Phantom 2 Vision + and now the Phantom 3, and this by far beats them all when it comes to features, stability, photo and video quality, and flight time/characteristics.

*** If you were lucky enough to buy one of the previous batches with FIRMWARE 1.1.8 DO NOT UPDATE firmware at all, and if you got one with firmware 1.1.9, DO NOT UPDATE firmware to 1.2.6 no matter what you do. 1.1.8 is the best to be on, 1.1.9 is ok since you can't go back, 1.2.6 is horrible and breaks functionalities and makes flying safely a problem. I will explain later Don't worry if you get the warning that you have to update firmware, it'll work fine even if you don't, it'll just complain. It won't force you to update firmware. Do not update until DJI gives you a way to roll back to the previous firmware version, supposedly they have said they're going to do that. ***

Things that are improved over previous Phantoms models:
- Camera
- Gimbal
- App
- GPS lock time and number of satellites used to tell position
- GPS hold
- Position hold using Vision Positioning System (VPS), new on this Phantom model from the previous Phantoms, also used on Inspire 1
- Range
- Video preview quality (720p HD)
- Flight time (about 22 minutes)
- More powerful motors
- Much more stable during yaw / spin during hover
- Video and RC both use 2.4GHz, no need to deal with 5.8GHz for control like on the P2V+, which caused the RC control to drop out way before video

Things that got worse compared to previous Phantom models:
- Maximum altitude AGL limit cannot be removed in app, although no one needs or should ever go above 400 ft, it still shouldn't be added by force
- Constant firmware check / complains about not being up-to-date, even if it works just fine, never had this problem with P2V+ or P2
- Proprietary DJI battery even more expensive than the P2/P2V+ batteries
- Motors and battery get really hot during flight
- Unable to choose any 2.4GHz other than between channel 13 through 20 for image preview transmission
- No ability to record 1080p or 720p at 120 fps

The Phantom 3 no longer uses Wi-Fi or a Wi-Fi range extender, it uses 2.4GHz band with digital modulation, and has a solid cable connection to your tab or phone so it won't keep losing connections. It uses the DJI Lightbridge (HD video down-link and RC control both in the same radio module). It has very crisp video, and control link does not usually go out at all, not within a reasonable distance. Firmware version 1.1.8 has the best video down-link. On firmware 1.1.9 and 1.2.6 DJI messed something up with the video encoding in the gimbal unit, so the app struggles to decode the video on your tab/phone, and the video constantly drops, blacks out or freezes. 1.2.6 is even worse. The tab/phone overheats while decoding video, and their solution was to shut down all other processes on your tablet or keep its processor cool, not really feasible! I would recommend for DJI just to downgrade the functionality back to whatever worked so well on firmware 1.1.8.

It has been known that some people have got about 3 miles of range on a stock Phantom 3 Pro and controller. Supposedly the Phantom 3's on firmware 1.1.8 and 1.1.9 have amazing range. Supposedly firmware 1.2.6 reduces RC range, and RC drops out and complains about "unstable RC control channel". This hasn't been confirmed 100% yet, but a lot of owners complain about reduced range after updating to 1.2.6. Again, DO NOT UPDATE firmware if you haven't yet.

The gimbal and camera on Phantom 3 are amazing. You cannot tell that it's a moving camera platform, there is no fish-eye, the resolution is amazing, and it is stunning in 4K resolution, the images are so crisp you feel like you can touch the trees or count the blades of grass! The only negative things about it are DJI's codec for coding the 4K images, and the bit rate is very poor for what it should be at that resolution, but it produces some nice videos either in 1080p 60fps or 4K 24fps. If you don't have very new Macbook Pro , leave the video recording at 1080p 60fps max, otherwise you will get very choppy video playback at 4K, unless you are going to post-process it, in which case you will get better resolution once you transcode it into 1080p later.

The Vision Positioning System (VPS) uses a camera and sonar to tell position when it's close to the ground. At 10 ft of altitude or below, it holds position down to a few inches accuracy, above about 10 ft it uses GPS for position hold. VPS also allows you to hold position when flying indoor or when you have no GPS fix. Be careful when using only VPS, because it won't hold position if the Phantom is above about 10 ft. Firmware 1.2.6 breaks the VPS functionality and makes it non-functional. DO NOT UPDATE FIRMWARE. DJI's solution to this is to turn off the VPS in the app to avoid getting complaints from the app.

Also, when flying up and then back down, firmware 1.2.6 creates a hysteresis effect in the barometric pressure altitude that gives you the altitude reading once the VPS (sonar) can no longer tell altitude above 10 ft. So when you start it up, your baro altitude reads approximately zero ft, if you climb then descend back to zero, the baro altitude reads about 20-40 ft. This does not seem to occur with firmware 1.1.8 or 1.1.9. This issue can be very dangerous for RTH if you lose RC control, and it has been known that some Phantom 3 Pro's running 1.2.6 just suddenly turn the motors off and drop 20-40 ft in the air. This could be a catastrophic disaster if you are below 40 ft or not high enough so that the fall can be stopped on time. It is a safety hazard for the Phantom and everyone around it. Again, DO NOT UPDATE firmware to 1.2.6. This cannot be stressed enough.

The Phantom 3 is a great quadcopter. You can probably not get a better one with more features out of the box. If you're wondering whether to get one or not, definitely go for it. If you're new to multirotors, get a small Walkera Ladybird or Blade Nano to practice and learn, then get a Phantom 3 once you know how to control them safely.

There's no question about how good and well designed the Phantom 3 is! DJI's customer service, however, is not as good. For those who have problems, either by the firmware update or by problems with their individual Phantom 3, their only suggestions for solutions is "calibrate the IMU (sensors), the gimbal and wait long enough to get good GPS lock", DJI will not acknowledge or confirm any problems, and keeps telling everyone the same thing. If you have an actual problem or anything that needs repair, their turn-around time is horrible, so if you get one, check everything, do not update your firmware, and if anything is wrong return to your vendor in the first few days and avoid warranty repairs, it'll take forever to get it back. product_title: GoPro HERO4 Session Parent
review_headline: The new default choice for the average GoPro user *Review Updated*
review_body:
26Dec15 Edit: A lot has changed since the Session came out. The price is much lower and some of the settings can be changed on the camera without a phone. This changes a lot, so my review below is heavily changed to update this new reality.

BOTTOM LINE: You need to decide if you want a removable battery. If you don't plan on filming more than two hours at a time, the GoPro HERO4 Session is a great choice. If you don't want a camera with a view screen, and you don't need swappable batteries, this is the camera to get.

I own a few GoPros. When the HERO4 Session came out it was $400, and quite frankly, the smaller size was not worth the price for most cases. But now at $200 the Session is competing with the lower tier GoPros, and it blows them out of the water.

There are many different models, so I'm going to boil them down into three choices. These are my overall recommendations for GoPros, including the Session.

Choice #1: Price is the most important factor to you. Get the GoPro HERO. It's affordable ($129 for now), simple to use, and works great for many, many uses.

Choice #2: You are willing to pay a bit more for some nice features, but you aren't a power user and you don't plan on filming over two hours of footage between charges. Get the GoPro HERO4 Session (the product for this review).

Choice #3: You need a viewscreen on the camera, or swappable batteries, or don't care about price. Get the GoPro HERO4 Silver

The lack of a removable battery is a downside. While a 64GB memory card will hold a ton of footage, the battery will only last a couple hours. Not being able to swap the battery in a matter of seconds and start filming again means the larger memory card is less useful. This is a problem if you want to do really long timelapses, since the battery will run out every couple hours.

For $200 this is a great camera, and it has become my go-to recommendation since the price cut. Some people (like me) need/want the additional features of the HERO4 Silver, but for most people the HERO4 Session is worth the extra $70 over the baseline GoPro price.

product_title: HDVD™ HDVD-T1BRF 720P Megapixel HD TVI CCTV Security Surveillance Bullet Pipe Camera 3.6mm Lens
review_body:
This is my first HD-TVI security system, so I still have a lot of the learn regarding the the pros and cons of HD cameras. I bought these cameras to try out on my new system because of their low price and I plan on gradually replacing my older analog cameras with the new HD-TVI cameras.

The quality of these cameras in the day time is really good. The picture is amazingly clear and I don't think it could get much better for 720p. However, the night time quality is very poor. In some aspects, my analog cameras actually perform better than this camera does at night. They're very grainy and almost impossible to see anything at all. Also, for whatever reason, these cameras have a greenish tint to it at night, even though it's supposed to be in B/W. I've uploaded some photos here for you to look at which I hope will tell the whole story.

At night, the driveway is virtually impossible to see. With my old analog camera, I could see the driveway and actually see the house across the street. Not with this camera. The garage camera is assisted by a small shop light that we have set to come on at night so that's probably one reason why it turned out as well as it did. The front yard camera is fair at night, but not great.

While I like this camera, I see myself trying a different brand -- even if it does mean a little more money. While day time quality is nice, most of the bad stuff happens at night and if I can't see what's going on at night, then these cameras are pointless. I'll probably end up moving a couple of these cameras to areas where they might be of better use like the front door and back door so they don't have to cover as much ground.

product_title: Lowepro LP36857 Santiago (Black)
review_body:
Material:

It is a semi-hard shell with with synthetic material over it. The material is black and shiny - aesthetically pleasing. The inside of the case contains 2 distinct areas. One part contain an inlay of sound-dampening (acoustic) eggcrate cones that protects a camera by providing a damper. It also presses the camera against the opposite wall when the case is closed which virtually eliminates any camera free-play. The foam is attached to the case's wall by a 2-sided adhesive tape. It is possible to remove the foam for custom trimming.
The inner opposite wall of the case is very soft and, perhaps, lint-resistant. The integrated pocket for some small accessories (memory cards and, maybe, an extra battery) is adjacent to the soft wall.
Once the case shell can be opened for ~ 3.5 inched wide (~ 45 degrees). 2 side flaps prevent the case to open any further and protect the camera from falling-out sideways once the case is open.
The zipper around the case contains 2 heads. The heads are metal.
The case is built very well with attention to details.

The belt loop can accommodate belts up to 65 mm wide.

Dimensions:

1. Outside Dimensions: 150 mm x 125 mm x 52 mm.
2. Inside Dimensions (approximate ) : 135 mm x 105 mm x [ 25 mm (to the surface of the foam) & 45 mm (with foam pressed in) ]

Test Scenario: Camera Panasonic ZS-40 with dimensions 113 mm x 67 mm x 38 mm fits very snug thickness-wise. There is not much room in the inner pocket to accommodate anything but a few memory cards. A single battery MAY fit. I would not recommend this case for cameras thicker than 40 mm.

The neck ribbon is rather thin and a bit too harsh if worn directly over the neck (skin). It is ~ 10 mm wide with hard plastic carbine hooks. The hooks are well-made and should not break easily. The ribbon can be adjusted to the shortest length of 80 cm (31.5 inches).

Conclusion:

With careful match between case's inner dimensions and camera's dimensions, this product will serve you well and protect the camera from dust and small drops ( to test, I dropped my case with camera camera from ~ 4 feet on hard-wood floor. There were no issues whatsoever). The rugged shell does the work well. High-quality zipper should be able to withstand day-to-day abuse. product_title: Canon PowerShot ELPH 130 IS 16.0 MP Digital Camera
review_headline: Good for hiking, could be better
review_body:
I've been hiking more lately but I've been disappointed in the photos from my phone. This is a clear upgrade in terms of photo quality. It seems like it's around the level of my friend's iPhone 6+ or maybe a touch better. The wifi "send to server" feature is nice but it's pretty slow so not as useful as I'd hoped. I wish it could sync to Google Photos or Dropbox directly instead of syncing via server to my computer then a separate upload to Google Photos.

Good
-Better image quality than phone
-Easier to stabilize than a phone
-Much better macro photos
-Zoom allows for good shots of mountains and allows better control of the angle of the background
-Very light and compact

Bad
-More work to transfer photos vs phone (fully automatic with Google Photo)
-Occasionally it's tough to get it to focus on the object I want
-Switching to macro and back is annoying

The panorama software works fine but it's pretty clunky. I wish the camera had a panorama mode that would keep the exposure constant at least. I also wish the image quality were a bit better but I can understand it's tough at this price/size.

review_body:
Excellent focus monitor!
I'm a career First AC based out of LA, and, having tested all kinds of monitors from the SmallHD AC7 and DP7 to the TVLogic 5.5", the Bon 5.5" takes the cake. It seems they held true, as I couldn't find a significant difference beyond the exterior and menu system (which I found I prefer to the TVLogic). Really fell in love with the design with the easy access buttons, adjustable levels of zoom and focus without having to delve into the menu, and I don't burn my hands when I touch it, as it has a low decibel fan (almost impossible to hear) as opposed to the heat sink built onto the TVLogic.
That said, the only thing I feel could be improved is the fact that the acrylic protector over the screen is a bit weird, with its tool-less locking screws kind of jutting out. I did solve the issue by replacing the screws with regular ones, but just thought that it was a touch odd.
Really happy with my purchase!

product_title: DJI Phantom 3 Professional Parent
review_headline: The product itself is amazing. It's easy to fly and the camera takes ...
review_body:
Let me start out by saying this review is for DJI and not Sunset Electronics, the third party seller. Sunset Electronics was excellent. I ordered and received my Phantom 3 in less than 2 days. There were absolutely no issues on their end. This review is about a product that does not function as advertised, and pretty much the worst customer service department (DJI) in retail.

Bought this product less than 3 weeks ago. The product itself is amazing. It's easy to fly and the camera takes stunning pictures and video. If this product worked properly I would give it 5 stars no problem.

Now for the terrible. The quadcopter functions properly about 50% of the time. It has a built in failsafe auto land, which is for people that are irresponsible and wreck less with the product. Sounds like a good idea, but it causes more trouble than good. The app will freeze every 5 minutes, leaving you no control over most of the functions it promises to deliver.

My quadcopter went into auto land, when I tried to over ride that the app froze. The copter flew itself, not under my control into a tree. It fell about 50 feet and broke into more pieces than you can imagine. Now I own a pile of junk.

I didn't even bother to call customer service because it's not even worth the hassle. DJI is under the impression that only irresponsible morons are buying this product and nothing can go wrong in their end. It's a brilliant product with inferior consistency.

You should not buy this product unless you are comfortable with multiple losses. I will not be purchasing another DJI product. Good luck everyone. Do not make the mistake I did.

product_title: IPCC-7210W - 4X Optical Zoom, HD 2.00 Mega Pixel, Plug and Play, Wireless, Metal, Outdoor Dome Camera with IR Nightvision, Audio and 4GB SD storage, BlueIris compatible - color White
review_body:
I just purchase my second IPCC 7210W camera (five weeks apart). For the money, it is a very good camera. It has all the functions, optical zoom, digital zoom, auto focus, night vision, etc. that most users would want. I give it 5 Stars for its overall performance and it’s construction quality. The picture and operation seem very stable.

I have installed other IP cameras and found the 7210W manual to be better than most other camera manuals, but, the manual could use some improvement in some of the instructions. [Likely it is a translation from Chinese.] The camera set-up is VERY easy, I had both of my cameras working in less than five minutes with the IPC Cam Central utilities and the IOS apps.

You will likely run into trouble when you start working with the various browsers to view the camera images; here, EXPECT problems. Before you get frustrated at the camera, remember, that browser issues (settings) ARE NOT camera problems. I access my cameras from six different computers, each with IE, Chrome and Firefox. In none of my computers were the browser settings the same, and in each case I had to figure out what the appropriate settings were to view the cameras. I have not been able to use the Safari browser on my iPhones and iPads [I guess I haven’t figured out the right settings, but, the IOS apps work well.]

Some things you need to verify is that the required plugin(s) are installed and not blocked by your virus protection. In the case of Internet Explorer, make sure that the Active X plugins are turned OFF, and in case of Chrome you need to enable NPAPI (the manual page 12 talks about this). I found that Firefox had the fewest number of issues to address and was the easiest to set-up.

Also, when using a browser for camera viewing, make sure you know the difference between the IP address assigned by your gateway/router and the IP address assigned by your Internet Service Provider. If you use the wrong addresses, you may think the camera is the problem. You will have to use the DDNS address and make sure the HTTP and RTSP ports of the camera are portforwarded. If you use an ISP assigned Dynamic IP address, remember that it is subject to periodic renewal and may change.

For smart phone access (iPhone and iPad), I used the P2PIPC and Rotro free apps. All the functions on both apps work well. . The great thing about them, is there is no need for router configuration changes. You scan the QR code or Search the LAN and the camera is configured. The one drawback is that they are free apps and they are short on written “how-to” instructions (no tutorials). You have to figure everything out intuitively. The paid app IP Cams Pro works even better and is great because it comes with lots of instructions and tutorials (and they have real customer support that understands you and is responsive). Here too, you have to portforward the HTTP and RTSP ports.

There is a way around the browser set-up issues. Try the Blue Iris software package for viewing and managing the camera; they have a free trial period. This software also has many really useful features and you can view multiple cameras without the hassles of a browser set-up.

Lastly, the Customer Service at IP Cam Central is great; they are quick and responsive.

YES, I would definitely recommend the IPCC 7210W camera from IP Cam Central to a friend.

review_headline: Cheap Softbox but gets the job done i guess
review_body:
It's cheap and does what it's supposed to do. However, the quality of the product is not anything special, especially the white diffusion cloth that comes with it. It crumples pretty easily after a few uses and does bug me a bit. One more thing to note is that the velcro on the softbox itself is pretty thin and makes attaching a grid slightly difficult (I bought the grid separately from a local store).

Oh and because the cloth is so thin and there's only one layer of diffusion cloth, you can't just point your light at the cloth and out of the box. I'd recommend putting the the light at the 'entrance' of the box where the cloth is and bouncing the light off the inside of the box, otherwise you don't really get good diffusion. The downside is that the catchlights you'll get from this have the silhouette of the speedlight.

Besides the cheap diffusion cloth, the rest of the softbox is pretty well made and since it's pretty compact, it works well as a travel softbox.

Get this if you really just want a cheap softbox.

It's focal length is 750mm, which means that it can magnify as well as a traditional long barrel telescope. What sold me on this item is the weight and durability. My son can carry it around, take it to the treehouse and I don't have to worry about it. It is inexpensive enough, so if it gets broken in a kid accident, we'll get another one.

I tried it out for sky watching the other day. We live in Michigan, so clouds are a frequent occurrence. It was a clear night with lots of mosquitoes. I did my observation through a large picture window of my home. I used a free iPad app Sky View to figure out what was visible in my line of sight. The first planet I saw was Saturn. I saw the rings and I liked it. That night I also watched the Moon, which is almost too bright in this scope, but the detail is good.

The trick is to overcome the wobbliness of the tripod and point the scope in the right direction. I guess the fun of it is in the search and a great satisfaction when you do spot the item you'll looking for.

product_title: DBPOWER 5MP 20-300X USB Digital Microscope Magnifier Video Camera with 8-LED, Base Stand,Software for Windows, Mac, Vista
review_headline: Opens Up A Tiny World Via Your Computer.
review_body:
I was one of several who received the unit for review. I like this unit as it allows me to look at a tiny world on my fairly large PC screen (Windows 8.1).

As a photographer, the fact that you can turn off the LED lights opens a whole world of "rephotography" from negatives, slides and prints. Negs and slides will require some home-brew light source, but with simple LED flashlights and some milky glass or plastic, you should get good results. I have some tiny Minox negs I want to work with! The color shot here is from a machine-processed regular print and is an area not much bigger than a match-head.

Now, if you can pry it away from dad, this would provide hours of fun for a child exploring all kinds of inanimate objects.

You can also make interesting art photos such as the tiny plastic soldier I found on the street.

Up to 5 MP resolution is OK for most prints, especially of you do not waste a lot of space and crop it later.

Setup was easy and the unit works well. Depth of field is narrow (as with microscopes) so a thick item (such as the fly in the pic I found mixed with cat hair!) is tough to take in all at once.

Obviously not for serious scientific work, as it only illuminates from the top, not from underneath as traditional microscopes do. But really a lot of bang for the buck!

Hmmmm....I've written for some photo magazines and maybe I can freelance an article on this. Gotta build that lightbox.

The peace symbol dog tags, the old toy solider and the dime are fine with the lights on.

A nicely made unit with very easy software. Just be sure you are not expecting to be seeing amoeba in a drop of water!

This is a much better choice for an inquiring youngster than a telescope in the same price range. (A fellow I know blogs for the Vatican Observatory and steers everyone away from nearly useless "Christmas Telescopes.")

Hope this helps!

review_headline: ... Hikvisions and had high hopes that they'd be as good as the Dahua cameras for a lower price
review_body:
I got these Hikvisions and had high hopes that they'd be as good as the Dahua cameras for a lower price.

Just as a point of reference, I have a Dahua 32 channel NVR with a mix of QSee and Dahua 3MP cameras. They are working with the Dahua NVR using the Private standard, as well as internal Foscams on the ONVIF standard. I used the ONVIF standard and PSIA and both worked with the Hikvision.

Unfortunately, the Hikvision dome that I have has a lot of IR bleed at night in one of the corners, making it useless. Also, these cameras are the Chinese versions, with hacked English firmware. I decided the extra headaches and bad picture quality was not really worth saving $30-40 per camera, and went back to the Dahua. Also, setup was a complete nightmare... why not enable DHCP from the factory, or even use the same IP range. How many computer does anyone have running on 192.0.0.x ? I'm sure it was someone's bright idea to make it a little more secure, but all that ends up happening is you have to jump through hoops to get it to the IP range every other device you own is using anyway.

The build quality of the cam is really nice. The image quality for daytime is pretty good, albeit missing a little detail compared to the Dahuas. Like I mentioned before, the IR bleed at night is terrible. I've tried moving it, but unfortunately it cannot be moved too much without negating why I got the camera in the first place. It may simply be the luck of the draw on the foam seal to reduce the IR bleed, but if it doesn't work, it doesn't matter how cheap/great value this is.

product_title: The OFFICIAL ROXANT PRO video camera stabilizer for GoPro, Smartphone, Canon, Nikon - or any camera up to 2.1 lbs.
review_headline: Amazing Stabilizer + Amazing Customer Service = Happy Customer
review_body:
The Roxant Pro really does live up to all its hype. Once properly balanced, it is a pleasure to use. I wanted to take one star off because I think it should come with some type of counterweight for the top (GoPro cameras, for example, are too light and need a little extra heft to provide a nice, even balance), but Roxant's excellent customer service earned back that one star.

As I was trying to balance my GoPro on the Roxant, the gimbal came apart. Not sure of the 3-in-1 lube I put on it broke down the bond between the two gimbal parts or if it was just a faulty gimbal to begin with. At any rate, I contacted Roxant about the issue, and they responded within a few hours. Mind you, this was around midnight. I was really surprised at the quick response. What's more, they were understanding and very personable with their response. Seriously, this is some of the best customer service I have ever experienced. They even wished me a Happy 4th of July and congratulated me on my newborn son (I mentioned him in my original email). Who does that in this day and age?! So kind.

Not only did they offer to send me a new gimbal, they also threw in the low profile version of the Roxant handle to help me get a better balance with my GoPro. I would not hesitate to buy this product if you are looking for a stabilizer for a DSLR or GoPro. Once you get this thing balanced, it really does its job well. I ran around my house to test it out. Checked the footage: smooth as my son's little baby bottom. Thanks, Roxant!

product_title: Ctronics Camera
review_body:
Received this today from Amazon. I had purchased this camera to keep an eye on my front door from the outside which would require a wireless setup. After spending several frustrating hours just trying to get the camera to work, I am boxing it back up to return.

Pros: As a wired (ethernet) device, I did (finally) get the camera to work and the image was very good quality. The camera was metal (a plus) and seemed to be very durable. Other than that, this has been an exercise in futility.

Cons: There are no paper instructions - just a small CD containing two folders. Click on the "English" folder and you'll find several sub-folders. Each contains Word files which appear to be manuals and "quick start" guides for different aspects or portions of the overall software. Four of these folders also have executable programs that install separate portions of the software. There is no indication I could find describing the order in which these should be installed or if it matters. Compounding the confusion and the frustration, all the instructions are obviously written by non-native speakers which makes the documents almost impossible to decipher. I tried lots of installations and un-installations. I could never get the camera to work as a wireless device. I have built and configured computers (hardware and software) as a hobby for over 20 years and I can't even imagine how someone not familiar with setting up software and troubleshooting would have a chance.

It's so sad (as with too many devices nowadays) where great hardware is basically wasted because of bad software. It's as if the manufacturers are about ready to apply the mailing label to the first one sold and someone says, "Hey, won't we need some software to go with this so people will actually be able to use it?" so they throw it together in a rush.

This product has potential but is not yet ready for prime time. Would give four or fivestars for good picture / hardware quality but zero on software which makes this unusable for me.

review_headline: Good camera, but it needs improvements.
review_body:
Working as a law enforcement officer i had been in the marked for a while trying to find a replacement for my three year old existing camera which had limited storage and no infrared capabilities. When i found this product i figured that this indeed would be the right one for me. It's a little pricy, but the video quality is good, and having a two in one set up like this one with both a camera and microphone sounded like a winner to me. But it has not lived up to its promise the way i would have liked to. First, the quick connect cable between the unit and the radio is somewhat "flimsy" with that i mean that it can fairly easily come loose, rendering the microphone part useless (The camera will still work.) I have already also changed the cable once due to a breakage in the connector, this in less than a year of use. Furthermore, the clip, at least compared to my old Motorola clip has also broken once and is of less quality, the same also goes for the audio quality from the speaker, which after a rain storm almost dosapared all together. (It came back after drying up.) Also the software that came with the camera worked fine initially, but after a while it froze up, this so i could not update time and date.

All this said, 10-8 Video has taken care of all these issues in a promptly manner without any cost to me. This company makes excellent in car vehicle cameras, but this product needs improvements before i would give it a 5 star rating.

review_body:
The system and the design itself is intuitive. However, one big problem I have is that it--despite the newer version promising 20-30% lighter materials--is still heavy on my flash. I am using Pentax AF540fgz ii. When I pull up the flash head to a perfect 90degrees, the flashbender sits there tight. However, when I tilt my body a little forward, then this thing pulls my flash head over; I have to hold the head to the desired angle just to keep it up. Worse, if you put the diffuser (in my case, I bought both as a kit), this problem becomes more obvious.

Other than that, the flashbender really works in making that little lightsource bigger significantly, and I really mean that. Shooting in front of the mirror really shows how much spread there is. Light is really evenly distributed at different flash zoom levels. I admit there are like 2 stops of light lost, but controlling flash output would compensate for this.

Another annoying thing. The lower left and right corners of the flashbender doesn't really bend because there're no hard wires or anything in it. The only part that you can really bend is the top and center part of it; the rest just dances along.

Lastly, this kit really isn't for rapid shooters. No matter how hard I try, I still have to use both hands to strap and unstrap this addition to my flash--while sitting down. I also wish the texture of the material to where the strapping happens has better grip. This one is still very slippery.

product_title: Sony NPFH100 H Series Actiforce Hybrid InfoLithium Battery for most Sony Camcorders
review_headline: If you do buy this battery, make sure it states "Sold by Amazon" and not a "Third Party Vendor" - Most are counterfeit
review_body: If this battery were still being sold by Amazon, it would be five stars.  Now, they're mostly by Third Party Vendors and they've all been likely counterfeit.  My first NPFH100 battery died years ago.  I replaced it with one bought direct from Amazon in 2010.  That battery, like my first FH100, were fantastic over 400 minutes of recording time on an SR-11/12 (the thirsty one with the Hard Drive).  Those batteries each weighed about 190 grams (naked, without packaging).  All the ones being sold now on Amazon all weigh 170g WITH the packaging.  Without the packing, you're looking at a battery that weighs around 140-150g.  The counterfeits typically last around 140-150 minutes (if you're lucky).  Lots of times they just give you errors and your camcorder shuts down.  My advice, if it doesn't look right, return it.  While I still love my "real" FH100 batteries, after a few years they get damaged or simply wear out.  I've tried other alternatives here on Amazon.  I've tried the Wasabi (they're okay, but still only give you about 150-175 minute of recording time), they're registering as 275 to 300 minutes when fully charged but will shut down close to the 100 minutes left mark.  Most recently I tried the one from "Maximal Power," also bought DIRECT from Amazon, not a Third Party.  That turned out to be the best alternative so far.  I ran it on Record the entire time, and it did go nearly the entire 275 minutes it registered as.  I did die at the "20 min" left mark... but I think that's really decent for a knock-off.  Most recently I charged that "Maximal Power" Battery, it registered as 305 minutes fully charged.
