review_body:
Fantastic starter drone!

1) Do not buy the one where you need to mount the GoPro, instead buy this drone with the integrated camera system. You can control the camera, get a real-time video feed of whatever the drone is seeing, and the quality of photos and video is good (not great yet).

2) If you are going to spend a ~ $500 on a drone I highly recommend spending a bit more money and getting something like this. A $500 drone will feel like a cheap toy that will most likely break after a few flights. I've flown my drone into a tree and it kept on flying after it fell from 50 feet or higher.

I have two major issues:

* Portable - I wish the drone was far more portable. You can't just stick it any old backpack.
* FPV range - you can fly up to about 2,300 feet before you'll lose your real-time video feed. There are some tricks to extend the range, but you'll have to tinker.

product_title: Dolica Proline Tripod
review_headline: Good budget purchase until you can save up for something better.
review_body:
This is a good photo tripod to get started and practice with but here it is less than a year later and it broke on me. I only occasionally used this (indoor shoots only) and when I wasn't using it, I stored it in it's bag and keep the bag in the manufacturer's box. Well taken care of but the knob that allows adjustment of the ball head just fell off one day. I tightened the ball head down to take a shot and unknown to me it fell off. This was the first time I used it outdoors so I ended up looking through grass until I found it. I was shooting a sunset so I wasn't running and gunning with it. I was pretty stationary.

This is not very durable for a long run I think, but I think that it makes a good back up. Get it to start out with and when you can afford to upgrade to a Manfrotto or something keep it as a spare (or lightstand, tablet stand, mic stand, slider support, etc). There is padding on the legs and the locks work great. So far there has been no issues with anything other than the lock on the head, the sticks are still great. This can be dropped to practically floor level but that adjustment requires a little wrench (included) to spread the tripod legs wide and low (which is why I have never used that setup during a shoot). There are little spikes on the feet, a bubble level (although somewhat mediocre), it comes with a bag, is light to lug around and it holds my full frame DSLR without too much wobble. The head is detachable. After the knob broke I unscrewed it from the tripod and attached it to my slider since I needed one for it anyway (I would not be using it as often and not have to adjust the ball head as much on the slider).

All in all, I guess that I got my money out of it considering how cheap it was. I wish it turned out to be more durable, but it still was not a horrible purchase (especially for someone who was just starting out with no experience and little budget).

Overall here's how it works. You set up the camera to Slow motion and either always or software button controlled. I used always. I took a 6 second clip of water running from a spout. What I got on the SD card was a 12 second clip at 60 fps. Therefore the camera captured 720 frames. Importing the clip into Aftereffects it yielded 28 seconds at 25fps or 24 seconds at 30fps.I did not do much as far as having the camcorder play the captured video file. (5) HDR recording has low and high settings. I did not get a chance to experiment and compare the two but this will be my next experiment. Overall the camera is slightly larger than you handheld camcorder but also noticeable lighter and smaller than the comparable Sony camcorder. (6) I did extract a few frames from 4K movies. They are great as family or general purpose photos. They will not be professional quality photos. Concerns: (1)Battery life is OK but just OK. You will need a spare battery and I hope these get offered soon.(2) If you frequently switch between different modes, let's say between 4K and HDR, it takes at least 6 seconds to perform the switch. Not bas for general purposes but not fast if you see an opportunity to take a good slow motion video. (3) The manual is hard to find. Try downloading it from here: https://eww.pavc.panasonic.co.jp/hdw/oi/WX970/battery life and the ability to switch between the many independent modes of operations may change this rating

product_title: Nixplay Edge 8-Inch Wi-Fi Cloud Digital Photo Frame with Hi-Res Display
review_headline: High quality frame and easy upload process
review_body:
Would rate 4.75 stars if possible as there are just a couple minor issues I ran into.

This is my first dedicated digital picture frame. I have used computer screens, TVs and ipads to display slide shows, but never was happy with the quality of dedicated picture frames until now. I have a Canon 5d Mark iii and L lenses, so I wanted a high quality display to show off my photos.

The unit came well packaged, similar to how Apple would package their products. I plugged it in and was prompted to connect to my wifi network. The firmware was automatically updated from the Internet and I was ready to begin uploading pics to the Nixplay.com site. Took less than 10 min.

I expected the Nixplay.com site to offer a poor experience based on some of the reviews. I was pleasantly surprised with the simple interface and upload process. Maybe some of the reviews were older and the features were improved since then. I uploaded 3 pictures to test the process and to make sure the format, etc would work fine on the frame. Everything worked well, so I proceeded to upload 1300 pictures to the site in the next couple days. All my pictures are full size jpg, ranging from 3MB to 20MB. I am continuing to upload more pics as time permits.

Realizing ahead of time that the Nixplay Edge 13 has a 16x9 ratio, I converted my pics to 16x9. I actually prefer the wider ratio and have updated my pics stored on Smugmug to 16x9 as well. I use Lightroom to manage my photos and it was fairly easy to convert. I recommend converting to 16x9 as it fills the screen as intended on the Nixplay.

The screen quality is impressive. Not as vibrant as the retina display on my MacBook Pro, but still very good.

Couple of minor issues....when I "sent" a new playlist to the frame from the Nixplay cloud, the frame would reboot after displaying a few pictures. (30-40 seconds). Unplugging the frame and restart resolved that issue. It does not happen everytime, but it did a few times. Another issue is my frame would only play for 1-2 hours, before shutting down. I ended up turning off the "sleep interval" which allows to turn off/on the frame at a certain time of day. My problem is fixed. I have not tried the motion sensor feature yet.

Suggestions....I wish there was a Lightroom plug-in. My current workflow is to export to hard drive and then upload to the Nixplay cloud. It would be much easier to manage the upload process directly from Lightroom, while also automatically publish updates to Nixplay if changes are made to picture. I use a similar process for Facebook, Smugmug, Flickr, etc. If not from Lightroom, a link between Smugmug and Nixplay would be much appreciated.

Overall, I am very happy with my Edge 13. I am looking forward to the 18" Edge to come out.

product_title: Evecase DSLR SLR Camera Water Resistant Canvas Case Bag with Shoulder Strap
review_headline: I usually don't do this, but for this case I'll make an exception...
review_body:
I use it for a Samsung NX3000 ILC with its mini flash, amd the 20-50 kit, 50-200 zoom, and 2 pancake lenses. I researched extensively online as well as trooping through several retailers, getting my hands on a multitude of cases at various price points. This was simply the best all-around case that I found for my needs and it costs about half what you'll pay if you buy a comparable competitor's product. I was impressed enough to write this, my first review ever for Amazon.
Appearance: The blue trim is subdued and does not overpower the black. Looks smart.
Dimensions: Picture an unsharpened pencil placed horizontally onto the case logo. It extends to the edges of the top flap. Stand it on end by the side of the case. The pencil is an inch shorter. Now picture removing the dividers inside. You can fit two large grapefruits in there, side by side. All the padding seems perfectly adequate.
Pockets: Lots! Webbed side pockets. A little too small for 16oz water bottles; 8oz ones would snugly fit. All interior pockets have standard zippers.Top flap pocket will easily hold pens, a small note pad and a couple of lens caps. Webbed pocket on the underside of top flap for SD cards, loose change, and will accomodate a couple standard pencils. Front pocket will accomodate a 6x4" instruction manual and has yet another webbed pocket. Rear pocket which would be good for a thin pair of gloves. The external zipper tabs are rubberized and easily grabbable with gloves on. The main compartment zipper has a pull tab on each end, and fabric end tabs to facilitate pulling. On this, as in ALL the other bags I tested, the main compartment zipper is tricky and the flap tends to catch - which is the reason for needing the buckling top flap! Many cases this size lack the top flap, which means a royal pain if you must repeatedly struggle with a finicky zipper during active use. The buckle is an ideal size to open with one hand and its strap is adjustable (oddly lacking in many other bags).
Possible issue down the road: The end points of the main compartment zippers could wear out over time because they take the stress of the top flap opening and closing hundreds of times over the life of the bag. True with any zipper end in such a location.
Overall very, very pleased. Bag fits all my stuff and more. Long-term durability remains to be seen, but based upon its capabilities and price compared to its competitors, if it wore out I'd probably buy another one.

review_headline: Fantastic gift especially for relatives that live far away
review_body:
Besides a GPS, was probably the best gift I've ever gotten my father (according to him, anyway). I live a few states away and just had my first child. Now, he's able to see any picture I want to send within minutes after I email it to the account. It's wonderful. This sits on my parents' breakfast table and he checks it everyday for updated photos.

Set up was a breeze. I just had to create an account, set my preferences on the frame, itself, sign into the wifi at my folks' house (with their WEP key) and that was it. I was transferring photos within 20 minutes. And to transfer, you simply email pictures to the email address you'll set up with Pix Star. You can log into the account any time from anywhere to manage the pictures. It stores quite a bit, too- on the frame and on the account. So, when we have pictures that are getting old, I remove them from the frame, but leave them in the account in case we ever want to see them again. It's wonderful.

The quality of the photos is very good (it leaves them in their original aspect ratio, unlike some of the less expensive versions of this product). The photos look very sharp. This is a good size frame for most pictures, too- and it can be hung or left on a flat surface (it has a prop to hold it up).

Now, you can send this videos, too, but I haven't tried that. I'll update when I get a chance.

We've had other family members contribute their pictures, too, so this has turned into a gift we were able to share with everyone. Well worth the price!!

review_headline: Easy to use but not sure if worked correctly
review_body:
Just bought the skyquest xt12g and figured I'd need a tool for collimating the optics. Using the lasermate initially I quickly got the mirrors aligned. It was very easy to use and seems to be very intuitive.

Then just to check my work I used the free lens cap tool Orion provides. I expected alignment to be right on the mark. Instead I found the primary mirror to be off center by a fair amount. I adjusted again using the free lens cap and the method laid out in the Telescope manual. Everything looks good.

First light viewing was good, sighting on moon and then later Jupiter and several stars, leads me to believe I have adjusted the mirrors correctly using the free Orion supplied tool. I need to go back and realign using the laser tool to see if it works but so far I am not sure that the lasermate has been a worthwhile purchase.

Not sure if this was user error or a result of the overly bright laser playing tricks on my eye when making the final adjustments to the primary. The light reflecting off the target is very bright then disappears when it is centered on the target.

product_title: Wasabi Power Battery & Charger for GoPro HERO4 and GoPro AHDBT-401, AHBBP-401
review_body:
These batteries are a no brainer for the GoPro Hero 4. We purchased Wasabi for our last GoPro and have been pleased with the result ever since. The last generation of batteries for the Hero3+ had a higher capacity that the brand name batteries and you got 2 batteries and a charger for the same price as one brand name battery. This is almost the same story. The capacity is the same between these batteries, but you do still get 2 batteries and a charger for the same price as a GoPro brand battery.

We have used these batteries through several charge cycles now and their real world capacities seem to be the same as the GoPro brand. We went on a Cross Country Ski trip a few weekends ago and we went through all 3 batteries in a 12 hour time-span taking time lapse every 5 seconds. I'll take it!

We also love that these are so inexpensive because we spend a lot of time white-water rafting and we are incapable of charging devices in a traditional sense mid trip. Our solution? We have about 8 of these batteries and a small portable solar panel, so that we can record as long as we need to! This set-up has successfully taken us down a 16-day trip in the Grand Canyon.

So let me sum up:
Pros:
Same capacity as original
Much more value for your $
Charger is USB based and can be used with a variety of charging points

Cons:
You will want more than 2
They have not yet made the capacity greater than the name brand like they did in the last generation (minor gripe)

review_body: These binoculars are well made and sturdy.  They come with caps on all the lenses and a case with strap for carrying.  Also included is a thin strap for putting on the binoculars themselves to wear around the neck (the strap is on the thin side for neck wearing and I'd recommend getting one of those more comfortable thick straps for that).  Looking out at the night sky is fantastic.  Not long after we got these, their was a night when the moon was the tiniest sliver and so near the horizon that it appeared larger and orange in color.  In addition on that night you could see Venus clearly as well as Mars (smaller and also orange) near the moon.  It was a sight to behold.  Never have I seen such clarity with such a moon as that--to me it a once in a lifetime view and the perfect way to test out these fabulous binoculars.  We can definitely see more stuff up in the night sky than with our lesser binocs.  This set is heavier than the average binocs, but we expected that. product_title: Canon PowerShot SX710 Digital Camera
review_headline: This is what you want and need in a travel zoom
review_body:
I was looking to replace my Kodak Z950 travel zoom after nearly 5 years of service, and was very pleased with the performance of my now 2-year-old Canon SX40 HS super-zoom, so I was going to look at Canon first. I was considering the SX700 HS, but late last year, the Canon website noted the coming update to the SX710 HS, so I waited. I ordered directly from Canon and have had it a couple of weeks now (about 2 weeks ahead of Amazon).

The main change from the SX700 to the 710 is the increase in resolution from 16 MP to 20 MP. The other features are basically the same, including a 30x optical zoom (fairly high for this range of camera), Canon's DIGIC 6 processor, and wireless connectivity including NFC to tap-transfer pictures to a compatible cell phone. The SX710's body is also the same as the SX700, with a pop-up flash and a small easy-to-hold form.

If you're familiar with Canon cameras, the mode wheel and controls will be what you're used to - if you're new to the brand, they're straightforward and very easy to use. I usually leave my camera in M (manual) mode and select the exposure, shutter, ISO, and white balance myself. I'm by no means a pro, but that level of control allows me to get the best picture quality in virtually any situation, including very low light without flash. And unlike my old Kodak, the Canon screen - a very sharp 922K 3-inch LCD - adjusts with the settings you choose to show a much more accurate representation of what you'll shoot *before* you take the picture. The Kodak's screen was basically one setting and I often had to retake shots after seeing how they came out. The mode dial is a little on the stiff side compared to my SX40, so I did have to get used to that, but unless you frequently change from one mode to the other, that really shouldn't be a problem.

In actual use, the SX710 shines. Again, it's a travel zoom, so if you're going on a photo-intensive trip, bird watching, or some similar activity and want "awesome/incredible" pictures, then use a super-zoom or DSLR. Just to compare for myself, I took the exact same picture with both the SX40 and SX710, with the same image settings - the 40's photo was sharper and had better focus on tiny details, and I expected that from the better lens of the super-zoom. But for "very good" pictures, the SX710 is far superior to the old Kodak, and is just shy of the SX40 for the pictures I generally take (parties, general scenery, fixed targets, etc.). The range of shutter speeds, exposures, and ISO settings allow you to get a great picture whether in full Auto, full Manual, or anywhere in between. The aperture is fine for this type of camera, ranging from f/3.2 to 6.9, although again, it won't match the abilities of a super-zoom or DSLR.

Both the image and video quality are what you'd expect from Canon. Images print clearly on photo paper and look good shared online in all the resolution ranges (although it's always recommended to shoot in the higher MP ranges if the pictures are intended for hardcopy printing). The video shoots up to a very clear 60 fps in full HD (1920x1080p) and allows standard zoom during shooting for very nice movies. You also get clear stereo sound.

Besides the stiff mode wheel, the only drawbacks I've encountered are a less-than-quick battery/card door (you need a very dry/tacky finger to open it quickly), and the flash snaps to its position with an audible "twang" of the spring which has me just a little concerned about long-term durability. All minor issues, though - and nothing that really takes away from using the camera.

Since the SX710 is just an update of the 700, the full range of accessories are already available, including AC adapters, 12V car chargers, higher-output batteries (I like the [[ASIN:B00DWIAWQE Vivitar NB-6L / NB-6LH Ultra High Capacity 1700mAH Li-ion Replacement Batteries for Select Canon Digital Cameras, Pack of 2]] for this line), and other equipment. I also went with the [[ASIN:B003F7DWH8 Case Logic DCB-302 Compact Case for Camera - Black]] as I have had good experience with Case Logic bags for other equipment, and while it's a very snug fit for the camera body, it works pretty well. Canon warranty is their standard 1 year on the camera body and 90 days on the OEM battery. (The Vivitar batteries come with a 5 year warranty, which is why I like to use those.)

For a travel zoom, the SX710 HS is a terrific camera. Features, settings, and capabilities are first-rate, and all in a very tidy package that can fit in your pocket. While this brings my run of Kodak cameras to a close after nearly 30 years of 35mm, APS, and digital products, I'm much happier with the Canon equipment I have now, and look forward to years of excellent service from the SX710 HS.k of 2]] for this line), and other equipment. I also went with the [[ASIN:B003F7DWH8 Case Logic DCB-302 Compact Case for Camera - Black]] as I have had good experience with Case Logic bags for other equipment, and while it's a very snug fit for the camera body, it works pretty well. Canon warranty is their standard 1 year on the camera body and 90 days on the OEM battery. (The Vivitar batteries come with a 5 year warranty, which is why I like to use those.)

For a travel zoom, the SX710 HS is a terrific camera. Features, settings, and capabilities are first-rate, and all in a very tidy package that can fit in your pocket. product_title: LensAlign MkII Focus Calibration System
review_body:
I have used this product to calibrate my Canon 5D mark iii and a number of zoom L series lenses. Most lens / camera combinations were close right out of the box, but they all benefitted from calibrating. I would rate this system 4.5 stars if I could. The concept is great but the execution could use a bit of fine tuning to make it easier to get consistent results.

There are a few YouTube videos (Michael Tapes Lens Align) that demonstrate the process so I won't repeat that here. I will focus on what worked for me.

Regarding consistency: It is imperative that the target be perfectly level and parallel both horizontally and vertically to the camera focal plane. I used two tripods with bubble levels to initially level the camera/lens and the target. I made sure that the center of the lens was exactly the same height as the center of the target. I placed a yardstick on the front face of the target and used a laser ruler to make certain that the target with the yardstick was exactly parallel to the camera. Was all this necessary? Maybe not, but I solved the consistency problem by perfecting the alignment. If you realize that a very tiny alignment error with such a small target is very significant, then you will take the time to get everything adjusted perfectly.

A few other things to note: Make sure that image stabilization is "OFF", that the target is very well lighted (it helps to place a large black or dark gray background behind the target), that the camera/lens is on a firm tripod and if it is a very long lens - do everything possible to minimize vibration from all sources.

The construction material is not paper but a thin plastic laminate. I agree that it could be constructed out of thicker material. However, if you take the time to get rid of all the variations in alignment, lighting, vibration, contrast et.al; you can achieve a very high degree of accuracy that is repeatable using the Lens Align System.

I've only tried a few hand-held shots in natural light so far with the aperture set between F/1.8 and F/4, and the pictures were fine. review_body:
This is a very good value if you are into 5 inch apos. However, the stock equipment is only 1 step above that of the so-so quality stuff that you get with cheaper scopes. I would definitely replace the diagonal as mirror diagonals tend to produce light scatter. You do lose a tiny bit of light and detail using it on planets.
The focuser probably is the weakest part, imo. It feels rough if it is not greased up, or may loosen up if it is not tightened. To grease it up is relatively easy. You'll need a metric hex wrench set and only need to take off the right knob(s) using the hex wrench set (take off the microfocuser first, and then take off the larger focuser next to it next). This will expose the 3 ball bearings that is usually the cause of roughness. Insert some lithium grease, turn it some, and then re-insert the nobs. If you feel roughness when using the left knob of the focuser but not the right knob, then the left knob is not positioned correctly. Take off the left knob (there is a hole in which you have to rotate the focuser until the hex nut is exposed), and pull it out a little until it is not touching the rest of the focuser and retighten.
If the draw tube is too tight or too loose, then you need to look on the underside of the focuser at the set of hex screws located there. There are 2 center hex screws and also a finger screw that can be used to fixate the drawtube to a certain spot. Loosen the finger screw a little. Don't touch the 4 hex screws at the four corners as they attach the black part of the focuser to the white part of the focuser. If the focuser is too lose, you want to loosen the 2 hex screws that are in between the 4 hext screws and the center screws a little. Don't loose them too much. Then tighten the focuser by using a hex screw to go clockwise on the center hex bolt. It would be rare for you to want to loosen the focuser, but if you did, you would just do the opposite. Turn the center hex nut counter clockwise to loosen, and then turn the 2 hext bolts clockwise.
The optics are probably the strongest part of this package, imo. It is definitely an apo. Just remember that it is only 5 inches still, and a larger scope with excellent optics will still show you more on deep sky objects, and even planets should the seeing allow it. Overall, an excellent value.
The only thing I don't like about it is the length of it. It is rather long, which can be awkward, when trying to view at zenith.n, and then turn the 2 hext bolts clockwise. Pro #2: Good picture.  Good night time vision.  Not a bad price for the picture quality and wireless capability.    Pro #3: Solid build.    These cameras have a web server and should all be capable of user configuration and use via web browsers with clear instructions in the user guide using freely available de facto standard (non-vendor) browser plugins.  The documentation should clearly document the web port.      Camera viewing should NOT require vendor provided installation or vendor plugins to see the image.   Downloading manuals or firmware updates should NOT require registration.    Con #1 - I had to install their program to find the camera.  I found the IP address, but did not know that the camera's http server is on port 88. They should provide the port in the instructions to connect and configure for those of us who do not wish to run an executable.  I installed it on a virtual machine because I don't trust a foreign camera company to give me clean code.    Con #2 - A vendor-specific plugin is required for the browser to log into to the camera.  This is complete and total BS.  I have never seen another vendor require this.  I installed it on a virtual machine because I don't trust a foreign camera company to give me clean code. product_title: Nikon 50mm f/1.8 AF-S NIKKOR FX Lens
review_headline: Reasonable lens for a reasonable price, but with some serious limitations.
review_body:
I am a low noise, low ISO, high detail shooter. That being said I purchased the Nikon 50mm f/1.8G AF-S NIKKOR FX Lens under the impression a primary lens would be clearer than the kit zoom lens. Optics, physics and experience indicate that would be the case. The less number of glass elements, the better.

For comparison purposes I am going to compare this lens to the Nikon AF-S NIKKOR 16 – 140 mm 3.5 to 5.6 G ED lens. If you bought a Nikon DX camera kit, there is a good possibility this is the lens that came with your camera. I use a D7100 24 MPS camera myself, so not judging.

I am that guy that reads the manuals inside and out. I am a firm believer that you need to know your equipment and be keenly aware of the capabilities and limitations of anything you use for a shoot. When I get a new lens, I refine the auto focus for each of my lenses. Everyone should do this as I have found even the most expensive lens can have a focus point a few centimeters off. I have found even the most expensive lenses can be off my a mile. I did this with my AF-S 16 to 140 mm DX lens and it was a +6. After that, it has been dead on.

When I opened the box for the Nikon 50mm primary, I ran an auto focus refinement but for all intended purposes, it was pretty much spot on, so no complaints there. As a matter of fact, I cranked the AF refinement up to a +20 and it seemed to be just as good as when it was zero. I question if it is even possible to adjust the auto focus at all on this lens.

I then started to do some shooting in various lighting conditions. With a max aperture of 1.8, I expected this to be a very fast lens; meaning is should be more forgiving in low light situations. This is where it falls down. With the kit lens, I can crank down the aperture speed to 1/30 and get a decent picture. My kit lens also has vibration reduction which when locked in, does a pretty good job of stabilizing the image for a shot.

With this 50mm fixed lens, there is no vibration reduction. From as far back as the early 1970’s when I was learning photography, it was drummed into me that anything below 1/60th of a second needed a tripod. This was even more important in the days of film as you didn’t find out your image was blurry until after all the darkroom work was completed.

Without vibration reduction, this lens became hit or miss. Even at 1/60 of a second, each image had to be checked for motion blur. Below 1/60th and it was pretty much a given the image was not going to meet standards.

Let me back up a wee bit here; I shoot with an ISO as low as possible. I am always looking to improve detail and reduce noise. That being said, I try to get my ISO to hover around 200 and shoot 100 ISO in most every situation. With my kit lens, I can drop my shutter speed to as much as 1/30 of a second and get a good image. With this lens, I have to stay above 1/60 and in moderate lighting situations; I have to hover around 800 ISO or higher most of the time.

Image quality is what it is all about. It is expected that a primary lens, with a minimum number of glass elements would be sharper than a zoom lens which has a higher number of lens elements and mechanisms that can degrade the sharpness of an image. This appears to not be the case. In comparing image quality of the 50mm Nikon primary to the D7100’s, 18 to 140 zoom (after autofocus refinement and set to 50mm on the lens barrel, on a tripod too) the images were equal. Color and focus at the edges were effectively comparable. I spent the better part of a hour trying to find anything that gave the 50mm primary an edge over the kit lens. If there was anything that benefited the 50mm primary, it was marginal.

I’m not going to say, there isn’t a use for this lens, but I’m going to ask some questions when I fill up my equipment bag as to the necessity of the additional weight, which is actually minimal. It’s a very light lens. If I had to do it over again, I might go with a 35mm primary instead which would be much better than the kit lens in wide angle mode. (less fisheye bowing)

So make your decision and match this to your shooting style. I’m going to keep this lens around, but I don’t think it is going to get much business to justify the $200 I spent.

Regards.ery light lens. If I had to do it over again, I might go with a 35mm primary instead which would be much better than the kit lens in wide angle mode. (less fisheye bowing)

So make your decision and match this to your shooting style. I’m going to keep this lens around, but I don’t think it is going to get much business to justify the $200 I spent.

product_title: Manfrotto 036- 14 Standard 1/4-20 Stud for Super Clamp
review_body:
I use the 036 Standard Stud to mount a standard light head on a Super Clamp. The stud fits into a hexagonal socket and is secured with a double lock system: spring loaded lock pin and a twist knob. If you forget to torque the knob, it's loose but will not fall out unless you press the release pin. The tip sticks out an inch, plenty of room to secure a light head.

The 036 is reversible and has a 3/8\\" screw for ball heads and a 1/4\\" one flip side for cold shoes and other accessories. However, because it protrudes an inch, ball heads \\"float\\" above the clamp, increasing vibration and weakening the connection. If you want to mount a tripod head, buy the [[ASIN:B001M4HTDE Manfrotto 037 Reversible Short Stud]] It's similar to the 036 but is shorter, allowing the head to sit flush against the Super Clamp.

Between the 037 Short Stud and 036 Standard Stud I can attach anything I want to my Super Clamp. I use the 036 Standard Stud more since it fits light heads but both studs are essential tools.

product_title: ClearSounds Communications CS-CSC600ER SOS Alert Amplified Phone
review_headline: Nice product - only two small gripes
review_body: This is a high quality SOS phone. It does what it should to alert a family member that your loved one is in distress and needs immediate assistance when they push the pendant SOS button. The SOS phone will autodial up to five phone numbers - one after the other - until someone is reached. If no-one is reached it starts the autodial sequence again. When you (the family member or gaurdian) receive an emergency call for assistance from someone in distress, and you answer, you can press any number on your phone to commence a two-way hands free conversation with the person who called for help. Nice feature and the hands-free mic on the phone is pretty sensitive although it can really only pick up voice if the effected person is close enough to the base station to have their voice picked up by the microphone. Despite that, you will have been alerted that your loved one needs help and will know that you need to respond even if the person in distress is too far from the base station mic to carry on a two-way conversation. This phone will also allow family members or gaurdians to call in remotely to the phone and commence a two-way conversation if after 10 rings there is no answer. Also nice. Two gripes: 1. The number dialing buttons are pretty hard to push for my 86 year old frail mother. The number buttons should be easier to push to input a phone number to dial. 2. The velcro wrist strap that is provided for the wrist use of the pendant SOS button is way to large for smaller wrists and the pendant remains very very loose and hanging around my mothers rather small wrist making the button hard to get to. If your loved one is overweight or a large individual than you should have no problem with the pendant strap fitting the wrist. NOTE: There is a neck lanyard that can be used for the SOS pendant but my mother does not like it around her neck...she prefers having it on the wrist.

This is a TRUE POE camera, and can be sold without power supply reducing the costs.  Network : This cameras does not came with an static IP like the others  and come with DHCP enabled, which I prefer because I did not have to set an different IP address in my machine to access the camera. After the initial startup with DHCP is possible to set an static IP.  The cameras are broadcasting UDP packets to port 7999, after version v1.10 is possible to disable it, the directions are in a post in microseven website.  Time : It already came with time server configured, no need to manually set the time. only some servers available, will be nice to set the server name/IP to use an local server.  The camera does not have my time zone, and no option for specifying manually, the support said they will include in the next release, I cannot use an standard GMT-x because of DST settings.  Images : Comparing the image, not as best like other cameras that are 3MP, and this is only 1.3MP, but in many places the 3MP are not necessary, and this camera is cheaper and can fill this places.  The night quality are not so good, but maybe they can improve in firmware updates.  Firmware / Web Interface: The firmware updates are available on the website, just register to have access, no need to be asking seller to send new version.  There are two updates in this month 2015-02, and two in first 3 days of 2015-03.  After firmware 1.10, more options on web interface work without any plugin, is possible to view the camera images (javascript getting snapshots, but is like an video), working fine on Linux with chrome.  The web interface shows option to capture to sdcard, but I did not find any place to put an sd card.  The interface also have configuration for audio, but I did not get any audio result.  The firmware appear to be generic to many models and did not check the existence of the sd card interface, wifi or mic, because the options are available but are not present in the hardware.  Other Points: The camera appear to be solid.  The support appear to be the best of three brands that I have, fast responses, and after some time I will know if they are the best if the problems are solved.  The Android App, is simple and easy to configure, just define the IP, as the other parameters are default, also have an option to scan, that I not used as I know the camera IP.  The camera has option for motion detection, to send by email, ftp, or write to sdcard. But this configuration only works on windows with the plugin, after v1.10 is possible to enable motion in full area without the plugin.  I'm starting with for stars, but if issues are solved this is a great contender for update to five stars, considering the price and being true POE. Now after some firmware updates, I think it can receive 4.5 stars now, but this is not available, if they still in same pace soon they will get 5 stars.

product_title: Canon EF 70-200mm f/4 L IS USM Lens for Canon Digital SLR Cameras
review_headline: Amazing lens, just need to be aware of its fuctionality
review_body:
This lens is amazing for its sharpness and color. One thing about purchasing a good quality lens, is that you will use it over multiple cameras. I have used this lens on Canon XT, 7D, and now the 6D, each time I increase the pixel count and sensor size. With all cameras, the lens just just as amazing.

One thing that I would keep in mind with this lens is the Image Stabilization. This was my first lens which had IS. This lens has an option for panning or yaw compensation as well.

When you are using the IS, this lens is only best when shutter speeds dip under 1/100 per second, and or the distance you have between your subject. Also do not leave the IS on a tripod. When do you do either of these cases, the image quality is wavy and soft due to the IS overcompensating for a shutter speed that is savely covering the sharpness.

This trick made a huge difference for me to optimize the sharpness of this lens to its best potential.

Another great benefit of this lens is its size and weight for travel. The lens is about 750g and about 172mm for the length. This length is about the large size to be mounted with a camera and placed into a moderate sized backpack for travel. While a single prime in the similar focal lengths, you can’t bring all lenses at once, and the f/4 is great for travel conditions.

I would stipulate that the lens is not quite enough suitable for indoor work unless you are comfortable working at higher ISO speeds or auxiliary lighting work.

Despite these minor stipulations, this lens is an excellent choice for travel, landscape, and some wildlife. It will last longer than several of your cameras if well treated and cared with keeping it clean and protected.

review_headline: WORSE THAN A FREE PIANO APP FOR YOUR SMART PHONE OR TABLET
review_body:
The worst, most useless and poorest built keyboard I've ever used in my 16 years of playing. You will have an easier time playing from any free piano app for your smart phone or tablet and i sincerely mean that. I don't know who this "grammy nominated piano teacher" is in the good review, but he definatley wants his student to struggle. These are my reasons.

1. It is programmed wrongly. When playing certain chords or notes, an extra note or the wrong note is played. Some c major chords have and extra Eb thrown in or even an Ab, without either of those notes being pressed. An E major chord automatically becomes an Emaj7 chord. You will see examples of this on youtube videos, one in particular being where a person plays "heart and soul" and if you're familiar with the song it will sound different to you, despite the right keys being played.

2. The piano sound is far from realistic. This is surprising because the data for a basic piano sound takes up very little space, and takes almost no time to create. It would be very difficult for the creators of this machine to NOT make the proper effect for a keyboard, especially with modern software developing being as advanced as it is.

3. Notes cannot be played fast or lightly. The machine cannot process too much, so if a set of notes are played in fast order, only the first one will be heard and the other notes will be forgotten. Also a strong force is needed to be applied in order for the notes to recognize being played. On top of this, only one spot on each key can recognize being played, so if you miss by a mm nothing is played.

4. An actual piano keyboard without these problems could be bought for the same price and at least they don't need a flat surface to be played on.

In all, you are gaining nothing out of this. Perfect for a joke gift sure, or maybe a nice door mat, but should not be considered by any means useful.

I use the included cloth to cover the lens area of my GoPro to help protect it from being scratched for anything inserted into the lid pouch.

review_headline: Great fill light - dimming by PWM can cause problems
review_body: Feb/16/2015 - reduced rating to 4 stars -  the adjustable light level is done by PWM (pulse width modulation) -  so under certain conditions can show strobe/scan lines on the video -  it is usually under low light conditions with the light set to a low level.    This cannot be avoided even using flicker reduction setting (fixed shutter speeds) on my camera.    I will link to two frame capture stills in the comments area to show this.    Great fill light -  - Dimmable one can adjust the brightness to suit the scene  - 3200K warming filter helps blend the light in with existing lighting.    I do not need a light to light up an entire room -  but mainly to help fill light when the main subjects are against the light, or in silhouette.    The continuously adjustable light intensity level allows me to set the right amount of fill light.    Most of the dim/low light situations are under artificial lights, so the 3200K warming filter allows the light to blend in well with the existing lights.    As others have pointed out, this unit uses 3x AAA batteries and I estimate they last just under 1.5 hours on max.    It is compact and very handy, and fits my needs really well    I'll include a link to a recent video I shot using this light in the comments area - the venue has stage lights directly overhead which puts the main performers in the shadow or in silhouette -    The video starts with the light off, and one can see the light being turned on and adjusted to what I considered the right fill level - it is using the 3200K warming filter so it blends well with the existing room lighting.    I'll also upload photo still frames from that video (links in comments area)  showing without and with the light on.  I adjusted the light so that it would not be in variance with the scene.

product_title: Canon EF 50mm f/1.4 Parent ASIN
review_body: This is one of the sharpest lenses in Canon's lineup, especially when used on an APS-C size sensor. It also has superb contrast and color. Wide open at f1.4 it is a bit soft but very usable, becoming tack sharp by f2.0.  However, Canon's 50mm f1.8 is a great lens and cheaper, so why buy this one? Three reasons:  1. F1.4 enables low-light photography impossible with other lenses  2. F1.4 gives excellent narrow focus depth with beautiful bokeh.  3. This F1.4 lens has higher build quality than the 50mm F1.8.  On an APS-C size sensor it's effectively an 80mm which is a bit much for street photography and portraits, though works well for close-ups.  Yet it is quite fragile. Mine failed after 5 years due to one of the tiny electric internal focusing motors burning out. According to the shop that fixed mine, a more common failure (that I didn't experience) is it doesn't take much of a bump to the front of the lens to break the internals requiring a repair costing > $100.  Highly recommended, but handle carefully.

product_title: CamKix Telescopic Pole for Gopro Hero 4, Session, Black, Silver, Hero+ LCD, 3+, 3, 2, 1 and Cameras - Adjustable - Remote Straps - Easy Extension – Tripod Mount / Wrist Strap / Lanyard
review_headline: Very nice lightweight 9” to 21” camera pole with GoPro mount
review_body:
Sometimes you don't need a long camera pole, but just something to give you a little extra reach. This adjustable telescopic 9 to 21 inch pole by CamKix fits the bill nicely for a smaller camera pole with adjustable ends. The pole is lightweight, and three parts that telescope out. You twist the end to tighten or loosen these sections. When fully extended, there was a little looseness in the third segment, but not enough to bother much.

There is a cap that screws onto the end that allows you to position the camera in any direction. It has a ball that pivots and a screw that tightens down to lock it in place. Note: you want to make sure you tighten this well, and make sure the base is tightened to the pole. On top of this is the GoPro mount, but you can remove it and use with other cameras or a cell phone mount if you wanted. There is a wrist strap connected to a screw in plug that screws into the base of the pole. This allows you to remove it and use the pole in other possible configurations. It also comes with a couple of straps that you can attach the wifi remote to the pole or your arm. These are just simple straps with a buckle. (The one that can be used on your arm is longer.)

Very nice lightweight 9” to 21” camera pole with GoPro mount.

product_title: LaView Channel Complete  Security System w/Remote Viewing
review_headline: It works, but there are caveats.
review_body:
This security system has been a bit of a thorn in my side. I've been installing it gradually, when I have time. The first camera I installed seems to have a clearer image than the other 5 that I've installed thus far. I can't find a setting to get the other cameras to an equal quality. Additionally, when setting the cameras for motion detect, it works fine for all of them except the one camera that has the better image quality. Initially it would record non-stop, so I did what I could to set it for motion detection, then it stopped recording completely. The camera is functioning fine, I can see the livestream on my PC, and on my phone by DDNS, but for the life of me, I can't seem to make it record on a motion detection setting. It's frustrating. When you log into the DVR and attempt to increase video settings, it becomes questionable whether they'll be applied or not. You crank up the settings, click save, and more often than not it says \\"save unsuccessful\\" or Something about XML. This is so frustrating.

Does it work, sure.
Is it user friendly, no.
Does it come with decent instructions, no.
Is crawling through your attic with a fishing pole easy, no way.

I needed this system after someone helped themselves to some of my Christmas lights, but in retrospect, I think I should have done more research. It's just not intuitive enough for your average person. Heck, I even had to find a video online explaining how to set up DDNS; that requires opening up 3 ports to your DVR's IP address, I suppose that's actually unavoidable, but it is unfortunate. The inability to get higher quality video settings to save is a big deal. If your seriously considering installing a security system like this, I'd look elsewhere, read the reviews, and if possible, find out how user friendly their instructions and UI are before making the investment.

product_title: Neewer NW-985C E-TTL 4-Color TFT Screen Display Slave Flash Speedlite with Flash Diffuser for Select Canon EOS and DSLR Cameras
review_headline: It's not perfect but it offers a lot for a very modest outlay
review_body:
Note: The maker sent me a review sample for evaluation, the opinion of the product is my own personal view

Model: Neewer NW985C

This flash unit comes boxed with a clip on diffuser, a padded bag (with a section to store the flash stand) a flash stand with a brass thread and instructions. Third party flash makers have in recent times been “upping their game” offering more and more features on flash units that cost far less than OEM makers.

This model has a significant important addition over some budget flashes, the ability to do HSS (high speed sync) older third party models were usually limited to manual or basic TTL, HSS can be very useful as it allows you to use fill flash at all shutter speeds (even above the cameras official sync speed) it does this by very fast strobe bursts, whilst range is limited it means you can use fill flash outside in bright light with faster lenses, and it can be useful for some flash tasks (which require a fast shutter speed)

I've been testing the unit quite extensively and have rounded up a list of the stronger and weaker points of the flash unit.

Good points:

+ Solid build quality, tight joins on the flash body and metal shoe
+ Operation is intuitive and straight forward very easy to grasp
+ Large and bright LCD panel with colour coded display for flash functions good viewing angles
+ Supports a wide range of features including E-TTL dedicated flash, TTL wireless flash, optical slave flash (with or without pre-flash suppression), “multi” strobe, flash bracketing and FEL (flash exposure lock) and full manual flash control (in 1/3 stop increments for fine tuning)
+ Good bundle includes a well made padded case, diffuser and flash stand
+ Mostly consistent exposure v a dedicated Canon flash (slight tendency to be about 0.5 EV half a stop under at times) easy to adjust output and not a huge problem
+ Built in WA panel and white card
+ High speed flash shooting is available at 1/16 output @12fps, supports rear curtain sync
+ AF assist beam is quite effective (a sprayed out pattern of dots outside the central area)
+ Audio signals (can also be turned off)
+ Port to add external power pack
+ Has a pc sync port

Weaker points:
- GN (power output) a bit lower than the headline figure I tested the output v a Metz 58 AF-2 (which is accurate) and calculated the actual GN to be about GN 48-50 (a bit less) still quite powerful just not as strong as some higher end units
- Flash shuts down when it overheats (would be better to slow down the re-cycle times) see flash heat test below
- Supplied diffuser a little fiddly to fit

Notes:

Manual power output is 1/128- 1/1 in 1/3 stop increments
Zoom can be set to “auto” (will zoom the head when you change the lens focal length or zoom) or manual from 18-180mm
Re-cycle times at full power were about 3 seconds

**Flash overheating test**

I fired off 25 shots at full power (normal room temperature) and the flash started to emit a rapid beep, this was the overheat protection kicking in, it took about 3 minutes before the flash could be used again. Once the flash was operational I fired off another 17 shots and it took a fairly lengthy 8 minutes before it would let me fire the flash. You can change settings but you won't be able to use the flash until it's cooled down. In normal day to day use it's not that likely you will be firing the flash at full blast in rapid succession, so you might not encounter the overheating (to be fair even some expensive flashes will shut down) it is preferable though to slow down the re-cycle times rather than shut down.

**What it doesn't have**

Whilst the flash is well featured for it's price, there are a few points to note where some of the high end OEM makers units offer a bit more, firstly there is no “modelling light” this fires a burst of shots so you can see where the shadows are, you can mimic this mode by using the “Multi mode”

The flash isn't weather sealed nor would I expect it to be
It can't act as a “Master” flash that is control other flashes via TTL, again at this price point it's not something I'd look for, but you can set the output manually and another optical slave flash controlling it that way

**In use**

Operation is simple the mode button cycles though the E-TTL mode, Manual, Multi (strobe) and Wireless. To enter the custom functions simply push and hold the central button (surrounded by the 4 buttons) and you can adjust settings like bracketing order, audio signals, AF light (HSS can be activated here) Using the 4 way controller/buttons you can cycle though the settings. A pilot light test fires the flash and lights when it's ready to fire. Holding down the on/off button controls the power.

The supplied manual was easy enough to follow though the translations were quite poor in places fortunately the flash is intuitive to use and it won't take long to get the hang of it

Flash head does not have a locking mechanism but is quite stiff moving it around at various angles very unlikely it will be knocked out of place easily

**Wireless flash**

There are 3 settings here E-TTL dedicated slave off camera flash this is a metered exposure and you can use multiple flashes in combination, you have 3 groups and four channels it's possible to set the zoom manually from 18-180mm.

The other modes are “optical” off camera flash operation S1 fires the flash instantly when it sees a flash, S2 is “pre flash” delay if you are using the on-board or a TTL flash then this will have a pre-flash. This mode also allows you to use the flash with any other camera (even compacts)

**Final thoughts**

There are some niggles and points to note with this flash, but really considering the very low cost and overall strong feature set most of the compromises are unlikely to be a major problem.

Both the build and bundle are impressive for such a low price, the flash performs well in use both on the hot shoe and in wireless mode with a good range on the optical sensor too. The addition of HSS sets this flash apart from other models, this usually is reserved for mid level OEM makers and you'd normally be looking to spend in the region of £200 to get that to see it on a flash at this price point would have been unthinkable a few years ago.

With a few tweaks and improvements Neewer would have a top tier flashgun at a cracking price, as it is they've managed to get most of it right and this flash is very capable and does most of what a higher priced flash does for a fraction of the price.ling light” this fires a burst of shots so you can see where the shadows are, you can mimic this mode by using the “Multi mode”

product_title: Maximalpower NB 4L Battery
review_body:
I bought this battery along with my Canon PowerShot SD780IS 12.1 MP Digital Camera, back in Dec. of 2009. I used the battery in conjunction with the original battery that came with the camera. It charged well on the Canon supplied charger. Since I have purchased the camera I have taken over 9959 pictures and a few videos. It wasn't until about six month's ago I really became aware of a problem with the battery. I would put it in and started getting fewer pictures out of it. Now the problem may have started earlier, but I just didn't notice it, and after having it 5 years it no longer keeps a charge even for one shot, while the originally supplied battery still today lasts a long time, it was made in Japan, yet the Maximal was Japanese made also.

Now you might say for $8.95 it lasted years and is still a deal. But actually it's hard to notice the reduction in usage time as it can start slowly, and you may actually not notice Furthermore it can run out of power at a moment when you are in the middle of taking a great photo. This happened to me a few times.

Now the battery is completely dead, yet the original still delivers hours of usage. Yet I'd rather have something I can really count on and not worry about .

Spending allot of time searching here on Amazon for the original battery I came up with vast differences in prices for a Canon battery. From $29.95 to $90.44 (this one exactly the same as the one supplied with my camera). I finally settled on STK's Canon NB-4L Battery - Two Pack 1400 mAh for Canon Powershot for $17.99. Cheap enough for two batteries, decent reviews also.

http://www.amazon.com/STKs-Canon-NB-4L-Battery-Powershot/dp/B000BO1L7G/ref=sr_1_7?ie=UTF8&qid=1421898390&sr=8-7&keywords=Canon+SD+780+IS+powershot+battery#customerReviews

A searched Amazon for a pet harness, but they only seem to carry harnesses that are compatible to GoPro or Sony camera, so I decided to make my own. I modified the black plastic mounting plate that the camera came in by cutting holes in the plate with a Dremel, then feeding the nylon straps of an old harness through those holes. Since the mounting plate already had a mounting screw attached, it was easy to create a level platform to ride on my dog's back. The camera received its first durability test after I put the harness on my dog, because as soon as I opened the garage door, he ran outside and banged the camera on the wheel of my car. No damage! Shot some video yesterday (without reading the manual fully) and tried to play it on Windows Media Player, and was initially concerned with no sound, but realized that you need Quicktime or RealPlayer to receive the full experience. Even with the bump against the car's wheel and running through some bushes, the video turned out great! I would recommend this camera as an inexpensive, high quality pet cam.

review_body:
The Gorilla Gear monopod is superior in so many ways to the two other brands I already own that it's worth buying despite a few drawbacks. It's much more compact and more sturdy.

The handle folds down to just 8", which makes it easy to pack and carry around when you're traveling. Opening the telescoping sections takes a bit of practice at first since each section is freed by a separate twist, but once you get the hang of it, it becomes second nature. When you have the length you want, a quick twist in the opposite direction locks it in place. The phone holder is a little odd: two u-shaped piece connected with a rubber strap. The strap lists devices such as iPad, iPad mini, Galaxy S5, Note 3, and iPhone 5 for quick setting the opening for those devices, but oddly doesn't have a marking for the iPhone 6, a device that has been out a while. No matter, though -- if you have a device not listed in the markings, you can adjust the strap and opening for just about any size of phone or tablet. You just lose some of the convenience of knowing where to lock it. The Bluetooth remote control is a separate fob with an included camera-type battery. Without the remote, there's no way to take selfies, and because it's a small and separate piece, I recommend getting a small carabiner clip to attach it to the handle strap for quick retrieval and safe storage. Although the main reason I wanted this Gorilla monopod was for the selfie stick, it also comes with a small tripod. The tripod can be connected directly into the device if the device has a tripod screw hole OR to the detached holder.

The phone, once it's in the holder, can be rotated up-and-down and side-to-side. All you need to do is twist the wing-nut-like piece on the side to lock the position. The selfie stick can be carried using the wrist strap.

I love that the Gorilla selfie stick has a squishy, foam handle for both comfort and a better grip. The contruction is solid, with both metal and plastic parts. When I received this monopod, I put aside the others I own. This one is the best of the lot. Note: I received a sample for review.h both metal and plastic parts. review_headline: Some things to be aware of that I wasn't.

I've just gotten this camera so I will write this and may write more after I have had some experience using it in many situations.

But to start I'm not as enthusastic about this camera now that I have it in my hands as I was thinking about it. I would caution everyone to READ CAREFULLY before you buy anything of course but particularly something like a camera where a small item tucked away can make a BIG difference. For instance I did not see that the camera can only be zoomed in and out using the electric button for the right forefinger. I am used to cameras that have a manual and electric zoon. I find electric zooms annoying and they never get me to where I want to be and I have to zoom forward and back several times before I get it right. It is especially annoying using video which I never realized would be such a big deal but it is!!

Also, these great zoom lens are useless unless you are going to bring along a tripod. And think about getting a remote shutter to go along with it. You may get a decent shot using the roof of the car or something to keep it steady but not if you are zooming way out there! So resign yourself to lugging your tripod with you or continuing to crop to get the long distance shot you want.

The camera I got did not have the disc so I'm going to have to download the manual and print it out because there is a hell of a lot of stuff that I am going to have to learn if I am going to use this camera as it was meant to be used. It has a lot of potential but you have to have the knowledge to unlock the potential.

review_headline: It works fine after 25' both from the front and from the ...
review_body:
I bought this because I need to add $6 to for free shipping. I did read those one star reviews before I buy it and just hope for a luck. Yes, it is a five star buy!

OK, as far as I read, those one star reviews have 3 reasons: 1, not working; 2, it delays and 3, it doesn't work at distance.

Here I'm telling you my story: when I received it, it didn't work either. I thought, oops, I had it too. However when I read the D7000 camera manual, I figured out it was my problem.

(1) to make it work, the camera has to dial to \\"remote\\" mode. On D7000, it's beside the \\"self-timer\\". If it's not on that position, it won't work, of course.
(2) in \\"MENU\\", the remote has 3 options: (a) 2s delay; (b) quick release and (c) mirror-up-then-shut; It has to be on quick release mode to avoid delay. However, even on quick release, it will delay, why? because it will adjust the focus before it shots. So, for real quick shot, the camera has to be on \\"manual focus\\" mode. But I don't think the focusing time bothers.
(3) I'm writing this after I tested the distance. It works fine beyond 25 feet both from the front and from the back. My room size is only that large and can't go further. I'll try it out door in the spring or summer. But I don't think you need that far.

Anyway, if yours doesn't work or has the issue some people said, read the camera manual first and set it up correctly.

This item only sends a signal to the camera to shot. As long as the camera receives its signal, all the issues should come from camera and not from this item.

Hope this helps.

product_title: Holy Stone RC Quadcopter Drone with HD 720p Camera,4CH 2.4Ghz 6-Gyro Headless Mode, includs BONUS BATTERY
review_headline: Side by side comparison of  Holy Stine RC and  Holy Stone M62R
review_body:
[[VIDEOID:c18fe2570f9621e4da2cf60a72b11eb7]]This is my second Quadcopter. I also own Holy Stone M62R and having experience with both gives a chance to compare them.

The main difference between the two is that RC copter has a \\"headless mode\\". What this means is that the direction of the flight is determined solely by the controller in your hands and not the direction in which the copter is flying. When you pull the stick on the controller towards you (i.e. down) the copter comes back, when you shift the controller to the left the copter goes left and so forth. Without \\"headless mode\\" the direction of the stick is relative to the direction in which the copter is flying and it makes is much (much!) harder to control it.

Headless mode makes RC copter much easier to control than M62R.

However, the video on M62R works better for me. There are several difference. First, the controller on M62R indicates when the video is on and off by a light. RC copter requires fewer steps to turn the video but there is no easily visible indicator that the video is happening. There is a tiny light on the copter's belly. I can see it at home in the dimmed lights. I cannot see it outside and certainly not from any distance.
The second difference is that I got several nice video from RC copter which were saved incorrectly (missing a video index). I can view these corrupted videos in VLC media viewer which is able to correct problems on the fly, but it does not saved those corrections. None of my video editing software were able to open these videos so I was not able to edit them or include them in attached video. There were a couple of video segments that were saved correctly and those are the ones from which I could select what to include in attached video. Unfortunately, the coolest looking video was one of those that had the \\"missing index\\" error.
RC copter generates 720p video and the focus sometimes slightly soft but sometimes quite good. I am also including a couple still photos that the copter took. I thought they were good.

I recommend that you figure out how video/photo works at home before doing it outside. The copter does not have to fly to take photos and videos. You can hold the copter in your hand, turn on video, then look at the micro SD card on a computer to make sure you see video files / images. I was also able to check the videos we took by using OTG cable with my phone. Since there are no visual indicators that the video is rolling it was handy to be sure that it was working.

The documentation that came with M62R was bad, in my review of it I included many missing steps. Documentation that came with RC copter was reasonable, no missing steps even though it was not always easy to understand and required a couple of readings to get it.

RC copter has a wing span of 15.5\\", M62R is much smaller at 5.5\\" wing span.

Both copters survived multiple falls from very high elevations. However the propeller guards on RC copter are attached much looser than on M62R and we lost them multiple times, and eventually were not able to find one of them. However, the guards do not effect the flight so it is not a catastrophic loss.

RC copter got tangled in two different trees, however we were able to rescue the copter both times. Once by just increasing the throttle power and the copter managed to work itself out of the branches. The second time I managed to throw a stick at branch which shook the branch enough to drop the copter. Both times the copter survived without any damage. I was impressed!

The copter comes with two batteries (same size for both copters). The small M62R was able to record video for 13 minutes on one battery. The larger RC copter recorded for 9 minutes. However, RC has a larger body cavity so changing batteries is fairly easy. We were able to rotate the batteries and got a lot of continuous flight time by charging one battery from an external battery while using the other. With M62R this was difficult because the battery is such a tight fit that it was hard to flip batteries when we were not working at a desk.

Both copters come with a micro SD card. RC copter comes with a 2 gig card, M62R with a 512MB card. Both worked with my own larger card as well.

One other difference is the color of the copter. M62R is red and much easier to find when it falls somewhere. RC copter is white and since we have snow on the ground sometimes it was a challenge to find it, especially those white propeller guards that kept falling off. If you have a choice go for the bright colored copters!

Camera carrying drone is a really cool idea! These copters are a promising start. Neither one of these copters is perfect but both are fun! Between the two copters I like the RC copter better because of the better ability to control it. As you see in the video it was possible to bring it back and forth and even navigate between obstacles (although not all the time).

product_title: Arlo Smart Home - 1 HD Camera Security System
review_headline: Home Security for the rest of us
review_body:
I've been watching the security market for some time, ever since being inundated with X10 security camera ads a dozen years ago. The problem has always been a simple solution for consumers to get some of the benefits of home security via a nice DIY kit. Buying a security camera in the past has been an issue on multiple fronts:

Where does the video go? How do I store it? How can I review it?
How do I install a wire run to the camera? How do I protect the camera?
Is the video nice quality?
Can I install the system myself? Can I maintain it myself?
Is it affordable? What are the long-term costs?
Is it easy to use?

Over the years many of these questions have gotten reasonable solutions. Camera video quality has improved, costs have gone down, and vendors have offered solutions make it easier to setup. The hardest to get right was ease of use; namely video storage and installation.

In Arlo's case I think this is the first total package solution I can recommend to someone wanting to buy a home security system. Let's talk about why.

Setup
=====
Setup was extremely easy. I unpackaged the included access point and plugged it into my router just like another client. I then installed batteries (included) into the camera and pressed the sync buttons. The camera flashed and setup was complete. To access the camera and complete the setup required me to signup for the cloud service. The signup was also painless and didn't ask for unnecessary information.

Using it
========
With the hardware ready, I logged into the site and installed the android app on my phone. Aligning the camera using the android application / web site was easy. I placed the camera in a spot and requested a picture to ensure it was correct. Then I discovered I can turn on live video and walked around my house while my SO directed me as to the best viewing angles and potential locations. Both modes make it really easy to test your setup.

So where did I install it in the end? One of the most interesting features of the camera was being able to use it outside and of course without wires! I took advantage of this to setup a "gopher tortoise cam" outside my favorite local tortoise burrow. We get notifications now when our friend pops out and can get some lovely videos of him in his native habitat without disturbing him. The unit's range was excellent as the burrow is several hundred feet from my house.

The Good
========
+Excellent video, with customizable quality
+No wires
+Easy setup
+Cloud service is free
+Fine grain control about when and how to record via rules
+Magnetic bases are both aesthetically pleasing and easy to use

The Bad
=======
-No local storage options
-Requires internet connection
-No audio
-Default mounts are not secure against thieves

As there are places (usb ports on access point) to add hard drives for local storage, I remain hopeful the local storage option will be fixed in the future. The cloud storage makes video archiving and storage dead simple and it is part of what makes the package easy to recommend. Still, I would like to use the system in a location without internet (my cabin), which currently isn't possible.

On the lack of audio, I've noted it but it's not a must have or perhaps even desirable feature in this scenario. The extra hardware would drain the batteries a bit more and isn't likely to pick up useful information. I can see some use from detecting sound and triggering, but the heat based triggering currently employed seems to work adequately as it is.

Final Thoughts
==============
Overall Arlo has some lovely hardware and an awesome design that makes it pleasant to have installed. Many of the shortcomings I listed above can be addressed by software which is sure to improve. The cloud service has experienced some growing pains, but I don't suspect any longterm issues. It's an excellent buy for anyone who has been waiting for an easy to use home security system or to simply monitor wildlife :-)

Note, I received this unit free from netgear as part of a test and review program.perienced some growing pains, but I don't suspect any longterm issues. It's an excellent buy for anyone who has been waiting for an easy to use home security system or to simply monitor wildlife :-)

product_title: Nikon AF DX NIKKOR 10.5mm f/2.8G ED Fixed Zoom Fisheye Lens with Auto Focus for Nikon DSLR Cameras
review_headline: A truly spectacular lens - in the right hands!
review_body:
I have owned this lens for over ten years and it is one of my most highly prized pieces of glass. It's just astonishing what you can accomplish with it, but people considering it really need to do their homework, unlike some of the prize fools who've complained about its 'distortion' - what the heck do you think 'fisheye' means, for heavens sake!

While it most certainly can render some interesting distorted views - and with some practice you can really achieve stunning results - where this lens really shines is in the field of spherical photography, which is what I would imagine most people buy it for. Use an appropriate mount on a tripod, pan around for 6 - 8 horizontal shots over a 360 degree circuit, add in up and down shots, and hey presto, with the appropriate software you too can create those snappy interior and exterior shots where you can pan around and look at any point in the scene. This is one of THE best lenses in the business for doing that kind of work, and once you get the hang of it and learn to master the required software (PTGui is a good example) you'll be amazed at the results you can achieve.

A point to note though for the uninitiated - this lens REALLY magnifies the distance to objects, so what you might think is a really catchy scene in the great outdoors can look like a blank and featureless landscape when the final spherical image is viewed! Learn to get CLOSE and anchor the picture with at least one notable feature nearby.

Bear in mind though that with the same software you can use the lens to create some stunning conventional landscapes by stitching numerous images together and correcting the fisheye effect.

In sum, it's a very very potent lens that has uses which far exceed the novelty value of the basic fisheye effect it renders. It boils down to how much you want to put into learning its many charms. All other lenses are basically a case of what you see is what you get. A fisheye like this isakin to a magic wand - you can get some spectacular results, but only if you go to the trouble of learning the spells.

product_title: Neewer 52MM 0.45X Wide Angle High Definition Lens with Macro for NIKON D5300 D5200 D5100 D5000 D3300 D3200 D3000 D7100 D7000 DSLR Cameras
review_body:
This is for anyone who has an 18-55mm stock lens. You screw this onto the end and it works to give a wider angle. There is a large circular black border, known as a vignette that will appear. If you want this to disappear, you should go out and get a 'true' wide angle lens. Search for anything lower than 17mm for a 'wide angle look'. If you're looking for a true fisheye, search for an 8mm.

If you're okay with the look of the vignette and you're on a budget...this is the way to go. Ideal for that 'skater movie' look...or a great all-around attachment for an adventurous day with your friends.

Pros: Lightweight, comes in a small tote bag with fuzzy material inside to protect from abrasive scratches while carrying, wide angle
Cons: Lens cap is flimsy and slides right off, vignette around images/videos

product_title: Parrot Mini Drone Jumping Sumo - Black
review_headline: Jumping Mechanism Defect in Parrot Jump(less) Sumo
review_body: A Christmas present for my son.  It was the one big thing he wanted.  A total hit for 20 minutes, but after maybe a half dozen jumps, the Sumo stopped jumping.  Did a little online research and quickly saw that others were having the same problem.  Following a tutorial on YouTube, examined the internal jumping mechanism and discovered that the wheel that retracts the springs on the jumping foot had broken.  It's made of cheap plastic and snapped where the jumping mechanism grabs it to pull in the jumping foot.  From a look at the reviews here at Amazon, it looks like this is a very common problem, especially with recently purchased Jumping Sumos.  This is either a terrible design or there was a significant quality control problem at the factory that makes these parts.  Still, my son really wanted this to work out, so I called Parrot support.  What a waste of time!  They were totally unhelpful and actually got a little snippy with me when I suggested this was a widespread problem.  They said they didn't know what was causing it, and they told me to send my unit back to their warranty department (which they outsource) for a replacement which would take 4-6 weeks.  I said that was unacceptable, but I'd be willing to keep the Jumping Sumo and fix it myself if they sent me a supply of the plastic jump wheels.  They said they couldn't do that.  All they can do is a full unit replacement which will take 4-6 weeks.  I asked if they wanted to see the pictures I took of the broken jump wheel (see below).  They said no.  At this point, I gave up.  The Jumping Sumo is going back to Amazon for a refund.  Maybe we'll try again after Parrot acknowledges the issue with their factory or makes a design change.
