product_title: AGFA Photo/Video Professional Tripod
review_headline: Legs can be used to make a great travel tripod
review_body:
Looking for a travel tripod that is very short collapsed but not a table top; light enough and short enough to put in my bag and carry as my standard set of equipment. This tripod gets down to just under 11 inches; or you can take the pan head off and it is 10 1/4\\". This is short enough for either of my travel bags. Although it's a bit wobbly, I have had great success with it when using a timed or external shutter release. Run a cord to the ground and use you foot to hold it down, and it stabilizes well.

There are two problems with this tripod. First, the pan head is small and flimsy, and doesn't lock the tilt very well. A large camera will drift up or down. Second, it is nearly impossible to level the camera with the horizon. Although it is possible to open fewer than all 8 sections on any leg, the legs do not have fine adjustment on the length, . And the legs really need to be spread out to be stable. So there is not enough flexibility to get a precise level.

You can attach a ball head onto the pan head, and put the camera on the ball head; that solves the leveling issue but not the drift issue, and adds weight. What I did was remove the pan head and attach the ball head directly to the tripod legs. I used a 1/4-20 x 3/8 Socket Cap Screw, a Heavy Duty 1/4\\" Female to 3/8\\" Male Bushing Adapter, and a Redged Professional R-0 Ball Head. This holds my Panasonic FZ-200 without problem. And I've even used it to hold the FZ-200 with 1.7x tele adapter, but with a tripod mount ring attached to the adapter tube to balance weight. Total cost for this modified tripod is less than $60. And it's light, long, and sturdy enough to use as an extender arm as well (with a remote shutter release).

Now my standard kit is the camera, a filter pouch (with polarizer, ND400, ND8, graduated ND, +3 macro), remote shutter release, extra battery, ball head and modified tripod legs, and Metz 28 CS-2 with Ultra-Pod. Super compact, light, and ready for nearly any kind of shot. If you like this kind of photography, then this is the tripod to get.

product_title: Smatree Battery (1200mAh x 2 Packs) and Charger kits for GoPro HD HERO3, HERO3+ and GoPro AHDBT-201, AHDBT-301, AHDBT-302
review_body:
I've had this battery set for under 30 days and used it for one afternoon.

If GoPro's extended life battery would cheaper that would be the better alternative. But for the price, it is really tough to beat this deal. Each battery lasted me about an hour of on-and-off use while using the wifi remote and the app for a little while (the app is better as a post review option than for recording action).

The fact that you get a car charger, wall charger and European adapter tip that are also compatible with the original battery, well, I've looked and can't find better alternatives FOR THE PRICE. Granted, the chargers and the wrapping on the batteries feel cheap, but who cares. Even it fails in some way, it's so cheap I would buy another set. I chose this over the Wasabi option because numerous reviews online showed that the Smatree gets a few more minutes and runs a few degrees cooler.

***** DISCLAIMER *****:
I have over 10 years experience in IT and technical support, troubleshooting and sales for higher end and specialty users. Traditionally 3rd party batteries are not tested for longevity. They are created to initially provide the most similar charge to the original product for the least amount of dollars. I would not be surprised if after 6-12 months the battery charge life decreased by 50%. FROM WHAT I'VE SEEN, this is pretty typical when you see a 30-day warranty on the battery. If you see 1-year, that usually means it stacks up against the original very closely. BUT, as I said, FOR THE MONEY, it would be worth it to just buy another set later, even though being such a consumerist is bad for the environment.

Of course, the bag can be used for other things, such as supplies for a hiking trip or camping trip, e.g., cans of soda, trail mix, compass, maps, and plastic lunch bags for collecting leaves, seashells, and whatnot.  Ordinarily, a bag of this type would cost about $50.00 at high-end camera stores.  The main compartment has two adjustable walls, as is commonly found in other camera bags.  The adjustable walls are used to ensure a firm grip of two lenses.  My own lens collection includes a 50 mm lens, 21 mm lens, and 300 mm lens.  The walls are adjustable by way of Velcro connections.  All four walls are well-padded.  Regarding the top flap, the left and right sides have pieces of cloth that resemble the gills of a fish.  These gills fold in and out when you open and close the top flap, in order to ensure that supplies do not easily fall out.  (I would prefer a zipper top, in order to be absolutely sure that supplies do not fall out.)  The lack of a totally secure top opening is a shortcoming of this bag.  There are eight compartments in all, counting the main compartment.  Two of these are zippered compartments.  The bag has a wide shoulder strap.

product_title: Pentax Q 12.4 MP CMOS Sensor Kit with 8.5mm 1.9 AL [IF] Prime Lens and 3x Optical Zoom
review_headline: Pentax Q - Good Camera in a Smallest Package
review_body:
I received the Pentax Q and saw it for the first time. Wow, it's so cute. I looks like a toy camera. It's even smaller than most point and shoot cameras in terms of the body size. Even with the lens, it's smaller than most cameras with its lens extended. I did try the zoom lens, but I really like the prime lens for size, speed, and image quality. Zoom lens was also good in terms of image quality and more versatile, but 50mm equivalent view of the 01 prime is very useful too and just simple. As for the image quality of Pentax Q, it's very good. I have used Sony Nex, Nikon 1, Lumix GF3 (m43), and Canon DSLRs Full and Cropped Sensor. Yes, you are able to get some \\"rich\\" quality pictures from Nex and Canon DSLR with larger censors in ideal situations, but in normal situations and for most people who aren't professionally skilled, you will get mixed bags of results on any camera regardless of the sensor size.

During initial stage of just testing out the camera, I was very impressed. Pictures were sharp even at 100% crop. I thought the various filters were fun to use. Out doors and indoor pictures were good compared to other cameras I mentioned. It is capable camera with tons of features for you to utilize. I really liked it. Then, I took the camera to my children's school fall festival. I shot more extensively. I ran into few problems there. This is with the camera updated to the newest firmware 1.13 I believe. When changing settings and shooting, sometimes the camera was bit confused at times and needed some time to figure things out and get it right. There was bit of lag of buffering and writing to the card. (Use a high speed SD card) Still, camera processor did seem bit slow compared to my experience with other cameras like Nikon 1 J1 and Sony Nex 5N. There also was some lags on screen display which I didn't experience on Nikon or Sony. Also, face detection and auto focus area didn't work as well as other cameras. I used center and recompose method which isn't very good when you are trying to shoot kids moving around. Over all, I preferred the Nikon 1 Series for its simplicity and allowing me to just shoot without worrying. Pentax Q can be used better by people who can adjust settings to get most out of the camera, but that isn't what I am looking for in a casual camera. There are plenty of features to play around with, so I will keep it for little longer. I was able to get good pictures from the fall festival. Still, I personally prefer the Nikon 1 J1 overall. Better Focus speed, lens selection, ease of use, etc. Pentax Q is a very good camera for set shots and taking artsy pictures. I have no complaints about the image quality. But, for a family with kids, I would get the Nikon 1 J1 with 18.5mm f/1.8 (same 50mm equivalent) rather than Pentax Q with 01 Prime. Sony nex has good image quality, but it's bigger and bulkier to carry around. It's not as \\"fun\\" as these cameras to shoot with in my opinion. As I said, since I already have a Canon DSLR for absolute image quality, I want a \\"fun\\" carry everywhere camera with good image quality. Pentax Q and Nikon 1 Series even with much smaller sensor are great camera for that purpose. Nikon 1 is easier to use, but Pentax Q is easier to twik settings with more control.

review_body:
This package seemed like a great deal and I was excited to receive it prior to taking a trip to Africa. I bought these to use with my new Panasonic Lumix FZ200 camera and wanted to ensure I had enough battery power to last while out on outings.

In total, I had the original Panasonic battery that comes with the camera and the two with this package. I fully charged all three batteries about a week prior to the trip. I had one of these batteries in the camera and the other two in the camera bag.

Upon arriving in Africa, I pulled out my camera to take a few photo of family members I met there and when I turned the camera on it was completely dead - nothing. I then put the other battery in from this set and the camera worked fine. I took a few photos - maybe a couple dozen or so, most without flash. The next day we went out again and I took a few more photos and videos, all without flash. Upon trying to take another video, the camera died completely without warning, leave the lens extended. Since I did not have my camera bag with me at that time, that was the end of using the camera and had to walk around with the lens out until I could get another battery.

I then put in the original Panasonic battery which had not been used yet and not been charged since a week prior to leaving the states. I took hundreds of photos and videos on this battery for over a week before it went down by one bar. I took many more prior to it showing 1 bar and finally recharged it before it even died, since I could not count on the other batteries.

Long story short; this was a complete waste of money as I can't return them now since I was out of the country beyond the return period and now will have to order another genuine Panasonic battery if I want to have a spare.

I experimented with focusing on a angled ruler and found that the focus was quite accurate however, in portrait applications even with a tripod and completely still subject, all of these lenses had a strong tendency to front focus leaving the eyes in the  the rear of the DOF and not as sharp as the shirt collar or whatever else happened to be directly forward of the focal point.  I was using a single focal point and I have not had the same issue on any of my other lenses.  When it functioned properly, I loved this lens.  However, 1K is to much to accept "great when it works properly".  The DC function works well, bokeh is as adveritsed but it does seem to increase the front focus issue at 2.0 & 2.8. It mounts easily on the lens in both shooting and reversed storing position. Unlike the Canon, it locks into place with a small button on the side of the hood to release it. product_title: MeFOTO Classic Aluminum Daytrip Travel Tripod Kit
review_headline: Very good except for one thing (maybe)
review_body:
The MeFOTO A0320 Tripod Kit is a nice tripod for travel, still life, and macro shooting. It is sturdily built with rugged yet light materials and easily collapses to a packable size. All the knobs, twist locks, and other hardware feel solid and robust. It's stable even when fully extended. Yes, it only goes to a maximum height of 24 inches...but being creative and working around obstacles, especially out in the field, is what separates great photographers from good photographers, right?

What's not to like about this tripod, then? Well, it depends on your shooting and processing workflow. If you use your camera's display to ensure level shots in real time or routinely correct crooked views in post-processing, then you won't mind that the bubble level on the A0320 is not visible when a camera is mounted. Otherwise, the placement of the leveler where it is hidden whenever the tripod is in use may be a showstopper.

Personally, I haven't found the location of the bubble level to be that much of a hindrance to my style of shooting. I don't take a lot of action shots or panoramas and my camera can generate a viewfinder grid when necessary. I think the inconvenience of not having the level always visible is more than offset by the good portability.

Bottom line: Four stars, keeping in mind that this tripod is only two feet tall fully extended and that the bubble level is covered when a camera is mounted.

review_headline: Two issues: corners and a 37mm protective filter.
review_body:
For the most part, I like the lens hood very much. I wish it were a bit firmer, however. It is not always perfectly round (because it is flexible) and on a few shots the hood made shadows on the upper corners of the frame. Perhaps a wire imbedded in the outer edge would prevent that while still allowing it to collapse. Also, one needs a 37mm filter to protect the camera lens. I was unable to find a 37mm filter at the DC Leica Store or at Calumet. I had to order one online at Adorama. A 37mm filter should be included in the package or be available as an option with the lens hood. From a cosmetic point of view, the lens hood is proportional with the D-Lux 6 body. Other than the corner problem mentioned above, the lens hood has prevented flares. Adding a wire to the outer edge and providing a 37mm filter option would
make this 5 stars. People who buy Leica cameras aren't going to balk at a bit more expense.

product_title: Sony 20.4MP Digital Camera with 3-Inch LCD Screen
review_body:
After using the CSC-HX50V/B for 1-1/2 months, I'm happy. 30X zoom is awesome and makes surprisingly sharp snap shots. Video worked great and that was also sharper than I expected. I had a Canon SX260 but that went under water. I \\"upgraded\\" to the Canon SX280, did the firmware, nice pictures but only 5 - 10 minutes of video. The SX280 had some real battery issues which Canon does not appear to want to address.

The Sony HX50V/B is a little bulkier than the Canons, but I still consider it a \\"pocket camera\\". Slightly heavier than the 260/280 but, again, not a \\"con\\". If I had one objection, the snap shot process time seems a little slow and I'm using Sandisk 32GB SDHC Class 10, UHS-1 80MB/s card. Not a biggie, I just got used to it. Excellent idea for the manual pop up flash, I didn't care for having my finger pushed out of the way with the auto flash. I don't understand why people complain about the LCD screen not being bright enough, I had my screen brightness set at #4 (out of 5) at the beach on a clear day and had no problem what so ever. It can still do 10 shots per second. So, yeah, I'm sticking with this camera (for a while). I like \\"pocket cameras\\", much more fun than luging around camera bags. Can't wait to try it out skiing.

I would absolutely recommend this camera to family and friends.

Update after a Year: Still in love with this camera! What still amazes me, is the picture quality when I crop a picture taken by zoom. Yeah, I'll keep this camera for a while or until I drop it in the water. Took a zoom picture of the grandkids playing in the water from the beach and zoomed, it actually froze clear droplets of a splash cropped.

product_title: Nikon COOLPIX L820 16 MP Digital Camera with 30x Zoom
review_headline: Great photos but missing the little things.
review_body:
First, let me just say that no matter what follows in this review the camera is very easy to use and takes great photos.

The camera body is not well thought out. If you have a tripod mount on the camera you cannot open the battery door/sd card bay. If you work with a tripod a lot this becomes extremely cumbersome. The camera does not come with an AC adapter and thought the ac adapter would be only 5v you cannot power the camera through the included USB cable. I usually do product photography with a light box and continuous lights so it's lack of a hot shoe was not an issue. The camera also works without horizontal banding under florescent lights (some don't). The camera is a point-and-shoot but has some cool semi-manual settings.

I usually expect to get a SD-card and an AC adapter with my camera. The ac adapter is like $45. Also, the camera has HDMI out but requires a micro hdmi cable or something that it again does not come with.

Again though the camera takes really good photos with minimal fuss. It's just missing the little things (like all of them).

Update: I ended up returning the camera. It's lack of an adaptor burned through all my batteries while taking product photos. Then nearly complete on a new project I opened the door that the sd card and batteries share and dropped a battery and lost it under some equipment I couldn't move. So I had to end up using my old camera to finish the job. After going back to it I just felt that it was a much better workflow and I am going to look for a camera more similar to that one. It's just a pain to need to take the tripod mount off to get into the sd card/battery bay. If I was taking nature walks or taking a bunch of pics on vacation or something this would be a great camera for me.

Even though I'm returning the camera I'm going to give it another star because it has seriously amazing zoom. I have bought lenses that don't have this much zoom that cost more than this camera.

If you need to get to the SD card a lot and you use a tripod it just doesn't work. If you don't need that you'll be hard pressed to find a better camera in it's price range. I do love the it but it doesn't work for me.camera.

During the installation I temporary installed the camera in three different locations. I wanted to see how it performed with different outdoor lighting. Like most cameras, it did not do well when the sun was in front of the camera. I live in Nevada and we get a lot of bright sun. When I installed the camera on the east side of the house, facing north, the video was clear and color good in the day light. At night, the IR light was good (biased to the center like most cameras I have used) and the video is black and white. The IR reaches 20-30 feet providing good video.

The mechanics of installation took about 20 minutes. The mounting plate could be a little sturdier, but it works. The final place I installed the camera took less than ten minutes. It is about 60 feet from my router and the WiFi signal must pass through 4 walls. There has been no loss of connection during the two weeks I have had this camera. As far as construction, it looks well made. I will see how it handles our winters when the snow comes and the temperature falls to 0 degrees Fahrenheit.

I rated this camera 5 stars because it does what I need very well for the price.

product_title: Ravelli APGL4 New Professional 70" Tripod with Adjustable Pistol Grip Head and Heavy Duty Carry Bag
review_headline: Meh - levels way off, huge 'slow'-release plate, decent build
review_body:
I said I was going to buy a different brand after sending back the last Ravelli tripod I ordered (that one didn't stand straight - yes really). First thing I noticed is that my free mini tripod is mysteriously absent from the box. Next thing is that one of the legs is scuffed up. Neither of these is the tripod's fault though, so I'll move on. I loosen the center column to extend it and the knob is very loose and wobbly. I then discover a nice touch that it is repositionable - by pulling the spring loaded lever out you can change the position. The caveat is that it's so wobbly on the actual screw shaft that tensions the center column that I'm not super optimistic that it won't eventually round the corners and strip out, and I've already found that you need to really tighten it down to keep the column from rotating. It smells a little - no big deal. I like the design for the feet and the legs operate fine out of the box without adjustment. It seems quite sturdy. On to the head. Three bubble levels - yep three. Guess how many of them are accurate? Yep, none. The two circular levels on the bottom don't even remotely agree with each other - odd because they are on the exact same plane and should match each other exactly. The top of the head has a linear, front to back level that semi-matches the left side circular bubble on the bottom. I put my Pentax K5ii on to check it out since it has built in electronic levels. I leveled out the head, checked the bubbles, and not one of the three was even close. The plus for me is that I don't need them, but anyone who actually likes the idea of a level on the head should not think that this tripod has even one usable level, no less three. The action of the head is not exactly smooth and enjoyable, but it is quite solid and does work relatively well. My next gripe is the quick release plate. Holy moly is it big - it easily extends an inch past the bottom of the camera and I would never leave this plate on the camera unless I was going to be using the tripod. You also need to tighten down the thumb screw on the side of the head after putting it in. Not just a little turn, but several, as just loosening the screw a little won't allow the plate to slide out of the head. The advantage of a quick release disappears when you won't leave the plate on and it takes two steps to release the plate. My overall opinion is that this tripod seems to be doing a bad impression of a great tripod. The quality is good for the money, but I'm certainly not amazed as many other reviewers were. The pistol grip is what attracted me to it, and I may even wind up keeping it because of that in spite of my other misgivings, but I'm leaning towards the pan head Manfrotto 293 at my local BJ's for the same price. Lighter weight and no pistol grip, but the quality is all 'genuine'.

Edit - Wanted to add that, no, it does not fit in the case it comes with, and I processed my return soon after writing this review. Next time I swear I'm not ordering a Ravelli. No really, lol.

product_title: Q-See High Definition Camera
review_body:
This is my second attempt to put together a high-quality, reasonably-priced home surveillance system. My 1st try was a [[ASIN:B003Y73Q3O Defender PX301-010]] all-in-one kit that I ended up returning due to the camera image quality. To be upfront and fair, that system - which included a camera, LCD monitor and SD card recording - cost the same as this single camera does. The system had a max resolution of 640 x 480 while this camera can go up to 1280 x 1024. I wanted - and was willing to pay for - a higher resolution camera. I was also willing to use my PC as a DVR/NVR to view and store images and video clips.

The Q-See QCN7001B that I received included a power adapter, 100 feet of Cat5 network cable, mounting hardware (included mounting template), CD with software/user manual and a POE injector all in a sturdy retail package. Judging by other reviews of this product, earlier shipments included little or none of these. While on the topic of earlier reviews, I read them all and found the information VERY helpful when setting up my camera(s), especially the network information. I used both the included web service and configuration tool to get the network information of the camera before switching to [[ASIN:B008YD80KC Blue Iris Pro Software]] (which I highly recommend) for monitoring/recording. I did all my setup and network testing BEFORE choosing a monitoring location and mounting the camera. While this wasn't necessary (the camera works great) I wanted to avoid having to take the camera back down if it was non-functioning.

(Note: I really like the POE feature - it saves you from having to either mount the camera near a power outlet and only one cable is needed).

Mounting the camera was where I ran into my 1st \\"con\\" of this camera. The camera cable (ending with power and network connectors) coming out the rear is a little short - it's only about 18\\" long. This limits the mounting location to ~ 12\\" from the cable pass-through hole into the house. You could mount the camera further from the pass-through hole, but then the CAT5 and power connectors would be exposed to the elements. Although the camera itself is waterproof, I doubt the connectors are. This brings me to the 2nd \\"con\\" - the hole required to pass the cable through the wall needs to be ~ 1 1/8\\" or so. I had seen this mentioned in another review, so I knew it ahead of time and won't deduct any stars for this. I WOULD like to see the cable lengthened to roughly 2-3 feet long and/or make the CAT5 female/power plugs detachable. I only took off 1 star total for these minor complaints as I was able to work around them.

Once the camera was mounted and up/running, I was impressed with the visual quality at the highest resolution of 1280 x 920. Video clips (triggered by motion) and still images were crisp and well-defined. I had the camera mounted over my garage door overlooking the driveway and found that the FOV (Field Of View)) is too narrow for my intended location. The camera has a 6 mm lens and doesn't fit my entire (two-car-width) driveway in the frame. This is not the fault of the product however - the chosen area I wish to monitor is simply too close to the camera (I have uploaded two images to illustrate the difference). I would guess that the monitored area should be no closer than 15-20 feet from the camera - maybe closer if the area is fairly narrow. In the end I moved this camera to the front of my house to monitor where I park my car and anyone coming to my door. I then purchased and mounted [[ASIN:B00A6CUNCM Indoor/Outdoor IR Dome Network Security Camera]] camera to watch over my driveway. The dome camera has a 3.6 mm lens which equals a much wider FOV. A lot more of my driveway width is now in view of the camera. The dome camera does have a bit of a \\"Fish Bowl\\" look to it due to the wider FOV. As a side note, both cameras seem to be exactly the same with the exception of the lens and camera housing type. The same short power/CAT5 cable and large/attached CAT5 female plug is also present on the dome model.

In the end the Q-See QCN7001B is a great camera with a few (slightly) annoying design choices. It DOES work pretty darn well when used in the right scenario. Just do a little research to make sure what your needs are prior to ordering.t power/CAT5 cable and large/attached CAT5 female plug is also present on the dome model.

In the end the Q-See QCN7001B is a great camera with a few (slightly) annoying design choices. It DOES work pretty darn well when used in the right scenario. Just do a little research to make sure what your needs are prior to ordering.

product_title: Canon PowerShot SD950IS 12.1MP Digital Camera with 3.7x Optical Image Stabilized Zoom (Titanium)
review_body:
The truth is, I got this camera about 8 years ago now... A photographer friend had suggested it to me for the quality and my budget. I got some really amazing shots with it. Some have commented on my Flickr assuming that they were DSLR.

This camera lasted me until about 2010, when the lens got scratched, and the quality of the pictures just wasn't so great anymore. I made several inquiries about getting it repaired, but it would have cost more to repair it than to get a new camera, so Canon sent me a discounted upgrade in exchange for my camera. I got another Powershot, but can't even recall which one it was. The photo and video quality for that 'upgrade' was actually such a severe downgrade!!! But since I was stuck with that exchange, I went without a good camera until this year.

I found the SD950IS from an independent seller here on amazon, and purchased it. They were right about the excellent condition. The camera cord was a little soiled/discolored from use, but the camera itself worked just as great as my old one. I HIGHLY recommend this camera if you want something smaller than a DSLR but don't want to sacrifice the quality.

The only cons I should mention is that occasionally, this camera will take blurry pictures if there isn't enough lighting. Thankfully there is a nighttime setting, but this requires flash (of course). I personally hate having to switch to flash at dusk when I went to capture scenery. Sometimes you can up the brightness, which can aide in the event that you don't want to use flash or the nighttime setting just yet, but generally, you'll get that with any point and shoot. This has happened with most point and shoots I've had, but as far as cons go, this camera is a little more sensitive to darkness than others.

However, overall, this is probably the best point and shoot camera I'll ever own, and I sincerely wish Canon still made this model of Powershot!!

An additional tip that I want tomention--
If any concert lovers choose to take this camera and record some video clips,you'll get pretty excellent sound... not the crumby kind you'll get from most camera phones and other point and shoots with video capability. You can easily record an entire track with great sound and pretty decent video quality, with the ability to adjust the zoom while recording.

review_headline: TERRIFIC camera, WATER AND SHOCK PROOF and GREAT VALUE
review_body:
The FinePix XP60 is a great little camera. I purchased this for my teenage son just before we went on a vacation to Costa Rica. The timing for this particular camera could not have been better. While I was carefully removing my camera from the ziplock bag in the rainforest, my son was diving into a pristine waterfall and taking underwater photos through the crystal clear water of tiny fish. My identically configured Fuji camera seemed suboptimal in comparison in so many ways. It can rain anywhere, and this camera goes anywhere. He also dropped it from horseback, naturally onto a rock, and it was fine - not a stratch. It is so nice to have a camera that you do not have to worry about!

The camera is simple to operate and takes great images. The photos from the trip that we had blown up were all taken with this camera which outperformed my camera with identical features but which did not have the water and shock resistance. Something else that I noticed is that direct connection image transfers were much faster from this camera than mine - also a Fugi 16 MP.

The zoom feature is very good, and seems to take much better pictures from a distance. His photos of monkeys in the trees were all very crisp and could be enlarged easily. The camera seems to focus better at a distance than mine.

I highly recommend using a very large data card in this camera, because you will be much more likely to keep this camera handy in your pocket and use it extensively. I highly recommend this camera.

product_title: Opteka GH1 Professional Heavy Duty Metal Gimbal Tripod Head with Arca-Swiss Standard Quick Release Plate (Supports up to 30lbs)
review_headline: Great value, but not 100% right out of the box
review_body:
This is a quality product, however, there is a notable caveat: the rotating base is very stiff and doesn't rotate freely right out of the box, as many customers have pointed out. Heavy grease and an over-tightened hex bolt are the culprits. Contrary to what some customers have said, there are no ball bearings in the base. The rotating base is a simple bushing mechanism. The problem is easily resolved with a cleaning rag, hex wrench, a butter knife and WD-40 (or similar spray lubricant). Here's all that's required to achieve smooth, fluid motion in the rotating base:
1. Carefully remove the base cover (printed Opteka GH1). This cover can be pried off with a dull implement such as a non-serrated table knife or butter knife. Do not use a screwdriver or chisel.
2. Remove the hex bolt and washer.
3. The gimbal head can be lifted from the base
4. With the rag moistened with spray lubricant, clean the hex bolt, washer and bushing shaft.
5. Remove all of the thick grease and lubricate the moving parts with spray lubricant.
6. Carefully reassemble all parts and tighten the hex bolt, but do not over tighten.
7. Unscrew and remove horizontal locking screw. Clean threads and add small amount of spray lubricant. Reattach the screw. Turning action should be smooth now.
8. Test the swivel motion of the base. It should be smooth and friction free.
9. Replace the cover

The pivoting lens plate was a little stiff, too, but easily fixed. First pry back the foam covering the pivoting arm. Then apply a few drops of lubricant to the pivot points. Voila! Smooth, resistance-free motion.

Overall review:

Pros:
~ Sturdy, well-built product. Capable of high load-carrying capacity
~ Adjustable horizontal lens plate that allows precision center of gravity positioning of any size lens (this feature not found on gimbal heads more than 5 times as expensive!)
~ Arca-Swiss quick release plate--the de facto standard for quality mounts!
~ Ideal for panning photography and panoramas (requires a nodal slide to achieve no-parallax photography)
~ Great price!
Cons:
~ Stiff rotation, but easily improved (see above)
~ Gimbal mounting head is about ¼\\" smaller in diameter than my tripod mounting plate (I'm using a Manfrotto 190XPROB tripod).
~ No product instructions! If you need assistance on how to use the gimbal head, watch this helpful customer review video: http://www.amazon.com/Opteka-GH1-Heavy-Gimbal-Supports/product-reviews/B0071BIQZC/ref=dp_top_cm_cr_acr_txt?ie=UTF8&showViewpoints=1

Overall, the pros outweigh the cons. I'm very pleased with the Opteka GH1 Pro Gimbal Head.

product_title: Xit XTNPBX1 1700mAh Lithium Ion Replacement Battery for Sony NP-BX1 (Black)
review_body:
Since it was giving me less operating time than my Sony battery (Sony is rated at 1240maH) I tested the XTNPBX1 battery with a SkyCharger B6AC Lithium Ion battery tester. I have placed copies of the discharge curves in the photo gallery. The measured capacity was only 942mah, not the 1700maH on the label, and 20% less than the measured capacity of a Sony NP-BX1 battery.

You can also see that the voltage curve falls very fast as the battery reaches the end of its discharge. This is typical for Chinese cells, differing from the more steady discharge of the Japanese LiIon cells, and the reason why the battery indicator on the camera suddenly goes from full to empty in just a few minutes.

Still, for $7.76 it is less expensive than the Sony (typically $49), and it does work well enough for use as a spare. But be aware that the rating on the label is absolute fantasy. The battery will give you about 20% less life than a genuine Sony BX1 battery.

review_headline: Well-made bag with room for large lens
review_body:
I've been trying out the Lowepro 250 Urban Photo Sling case in each of the ways it's designed for camera carrying. Because of its size, I prefer to wear it as a backpack, although this isn't the easiest place to access the camera.

I like that it can be loaded two ways: from the top or with the front panel fully opened. It is considerably easier to use the top-loader since the front cover involves releasing two side clips in order to expose the interior compartments.

The compartments are adjustable so will accommodate the camera (my husband's Canon 60D) with a 70-200mm lens attached and still leave room for two additional lenses (one large, one small). A mesh, Velcro fastened cover holds the lenses in place. There's a separate compartment for a tablet in the rear of the bag. It will accommodate an i Pad, but not with a case. My Kindle Fire fits conveniently inside, however, this is not an item I'd normally use with my camera gear. A tiny Velcrofastened sleeve in the cover holds extra SD cards.

Beneath the protective cover is yet another zippered divided compartment, each about the size suitable for a touch type cell phone. This is also accessible only when both side clips are unlatched and the protective cover undone.

I like the carrying versatility and the bag is well made with adequate padding for its contents, which rates it four and a half stars. Since my go-to camera is a Sony point and shoot, the bag will hold my billfold, cosmetics bag and cell phone for a day trek, a convenience to tote these items and my camera in one bag. However, for general ease of camera access, I'll stick with my Case Logic CPL-106 DSLR that opens easily from the top and still holds all my gear for a weekend jaunt.

product_title: Avacom M1060W Wireless Pan&Tilt IP/Network Indoor Camera with IR-Cut filter, Night Vision and Two-Way Audio (Black)
review_headline: It's not perfect but considering the cost this is a decent camera.
review_body:
These are my initial thoughts after using the camera for a few days. I'll update this review if things change. This is my first IP camera.

* Initial setup was fairly easy, although the instructions were junk. What you need to do: (1) plug camera into an ethernet port on your router / network switch. (2) plug camera into power (3) run the little initialization utility from Avacom's website from a computer on your network: [...] (4) click \\"search\\" and the camera should show up in the list (5) select the camera from the list, enter the IP address you want it to use (or check 'set IP automatically' for DHCP) and then click \\"update\\"

* After initial setup is done and the camera reboots, you can now use a browser on your network to view the camera directly. From there you can access additional settings like Network / Wireless, Alarm, Email (it can email you a series of screenshots on an alarm), Security / Users, and a bunch of other stuff.

* The wireless connection is a little flakey. It sometimes takes 10-15min before the camera connects itself to my wireless network. It will also sometimes disconnect itself for a while and come back later. Also, the wireless range is not very good and there is no strength indicator in the camera's interface. I have a very good to excellent signal with my laptop and phone in the same areas. One other thing with the wireless that's bothering me is that since I've installed 2 of these cameras a few days ago, my wireless signal has gone completely down twice and I needed to reboot my router to get it back. I'm not sure if (or how?) it's the cameras' fault yet but it has never done that before.

* The pan and tilt feature work quite well. The motors are nice and quiet, although you can still hear them working.

* The image quality is fairly good, again for the price. I had to adjust the focus on both of the cameras by turning the ring around the lens back and forth until it looked decent.You're not going to be able to make out people's faces from more than about 7-10ft away. Colors are acceptable.

* I wanted to use one of the cameras to monitor my driveway and front porch by pointing it out a front window. This setup works fine in the daylight but once it gets dark, the IR LEDs automatically turn on and all I get is a bright reflection off of the glass. I haven't figured out a way to manually disable the IR yet, if that's possible. I may have to resort to electrical tape to cover them.

* The cameras get a little warm to the touch after being plugged in a while. Nothing too bad but it would indicate to me that these probably won't last the longest. I may add some ventilation holes in the base to help. Writing this review got me curious so I just plugged it into my kill-a-watt and found that it uses about 2w of electricity, not too bad.

product_title: D-Link Wireless Day/Night microSD Network Surveillance Camera with mydlink-Enabled
review_body:
I got this item yesterday and immediately started to set it up. I had compared this camera to the Foscam's and Dropcam and I bought this because of the wealth of information at the dlink site. Also, it looked like it would fulfill my needs.

I have an older router that doesn't support WPS. WPS enables you to push a button on the router to set up the camera automatically. I needed to physically connect the camera via the supplied Cat 5 cable to the router itself (not my PC). But there is a label on the camera over the power and ethernet port that notifies you to install the CD first.

The CD walked me through the installation process with no difficulty. I then went looking to see if there is a firmware upgrade. I found one on their site and downloaded it and browsed for it in the camera's web interface. That didn't work and luckily it reverted back to the old firmware.
If you have registered the camera with Dlink (I suggest registering), then the mydlink site will upgrade the firmware for you. They also warn that the ethernet cable needs to be connected to the router, which I didn't do during the manual firmware upgrade.

With the firmware upgraded, I moved the camera to the area that I wanted to monitor, then got the IP address of the camera from my router and pointed my tablet to that URL (use \\"https://) so that I could set the viewing area.

I wanted it to e-mail me video clips when it detected motion, so I pulled my account data from the t-bird e-mail account settings and tested it. The test sends a photo.

Somewhere along the way I also set up network time protocol (NTP) and pointed it to Dlink's NTP site. That way you get the correct time on the video within a few secondes.

There are 4 different video recording/playback modes that you can set. It actually captures video in all 4 modes at once. For an e-mail of a video, you might want a little bit lower quality and resolution than ifyou are monitoring it in your own house over your wireless. In fact, you can point Real Player at it and select which video mode you want to monitor (URL rtsp:///mode)

I put a 16 GB micro SD card in it so that the video would be permanently captured. You can record to the SD card only when there is motion detected and this is a great option for setting up the motion detection. You can then go through the captures (a little over a minute per capture) and make sure that recording only triggers on the events that you want. In my case I set up for PIR motion detection only at low sensitivity, since I only want it to detect motion 5-15 feet away. After reviewing some of the videos, it only triggers when one of us is walking through the room and not the ceiling fan. It hasn't been through a thunder storm yet.

When the camera detected motion, I wanted 2 things to happen:

1. I would recieve an SMS text on my iphone at @txt.att.net
2. My g-mail account would get a 10 second video.

The text message would alert me to check the e-mailed video. Unfortunately, it seems that you can't add 2 e-mail addresses in the e-mail setup. Nor can you select both a video and a snapshot to be sent, one to one address and the other to another. I got around this by setting up my g-mail account to forward the e-mail to my SMS text message account. While I can't see the video in the text message, the text message informs me in no uncertain terms that motion has been detected. Then I can revert to e-mail and watch the video.

Other nice features are that you can set up a schedule when it will record to the SD card or send e-mails when it detects motion. I haven't spent a lot of time playing with mydlink on their website, but it doesn't seem to be nearly as sophisticated as the camera's own web interface. The thing to do might be to set up IP forwarding on the router as others have suggested and access the camera itself remotely.

Maybe I will report back on it after I have some more experience with it. But, for now and for the price, I am pretty happy

7/30/2013 update. We went through a terrific thunderstorm last night with lightning close by. The only time the PIR detection triggered was when my wife walked past a couple of times. Also, when you log out of the web interface and it warns you to close the browser, do what it says! I was trying to permanently set its IP address on the router and couldn't get back into it with firefox. I brought IE up and logged in. I thought that I was going to have to figure out how to factory reset it. Another good thing is that by default it responds to ping.

review_body:

I can push a button, make 1 more selection then with the press of the shutter button, take many many pics at the same time. So its easy to get lots of shots as something moves and get just the right pic. I love this.

My last camera was sooo slow, that I would press the button to take a pic, but by the time the shutter actually closed to take a pic, the subject had already moved. It was terrible.

The thing that is driving me nuts though is that I cant get the pics out of the camera. With other cameras. I could just plug the USB into a computer, windows would pop up something asking to import the pics and that was it. Sure Easy.

With this, I plugged the USB cable into a Mac and then a PC. Nothing. I even tried loading their software into both the Mac and the PC. Still nothing. I searched the manual, but found nothing. At this point, Im thinking that the camera is defective. Surely the manufacturer would not make it this hard to do something this simple.

The pics are all stored, I hope, on the card I bought. So I am hoping that I can find an easy way to get the pics off the card. If anyone has any suggestions on how to do this, please let me know.

Phillip

I literally struggled with fear that I was going to break the lens.

Auto-Focus:
The Speedbooster does support auto-focusing for this lens. However, the AF is very slow. I would say about 2-3 seconds to fully focus. I gave up after my second picture and switched it to manual focus.

Manual-Focus:
The focus ring was too tight for fast focus. It feels 3 times tighter than my Canon 35mm f1.4 (my favorite lens and highly recommended combo for speedbooster). During my photo shoot, I was frustrated at the amount of strength needed to focus. I ended up walking back and forth sometimes just to compensate for focus instead.

Quality of pictures:
There was some vignette in the upper left corner. The speedbooster did allow for f1.0 but found it hard to get sharp focus with the small DoF especially with the tight focus ring.

Conclusion:
I ended up returning the lens. This was nothing like my experience with my 35mm f1.4 (smooth focus ring, sharp and easy to attach). I don't blame the lens. It's an excellent lens. I just didn't like it as a combo with the speedbooster.

I gave the lens 4 stars because of the tight focus ring. While most people don't use manual focus because the AF is very fast, but there are some who do slight manual adjustments after focus so it's nice to know.

I give the Speedbooster + 50mm f1.2 combo a low 2 stars. Not recommended even if the pictures came out very nice. The diffuculty in attaching the lens and trying to use the focus ring was enough to deter me. Maybe someone else might have a better experience but I couldn't deal with the copy that I received. Also note that Amazon expects for the person returning the item to pay for shipping, insurance and tracking due to the cost of the item (even prime members). This costs me almost $25 using USPS. (This did not affect my rating.)

product_title: Nikon COOLPIX AW100 16 MP CMOS Waterproof Digital Camera with GPS and Full HD 1080p Video
review_headline: Broke first time underwater!  Buyer beware!
review_body:
Nikon claims that this is a waterproof camera but the very first time I used it underwater water leaked inside and the camera broke. I followed all of the water usage protocol and procedures listed in the user manual, only using the camera in a few feet of water in a pool for about 30 minutes. The camera showed signs of malfunctioning immediately in the water when each time I turned it vertically the screen would black out; it would only show an image if the camera was held horizontally. I'm not sure if that's a settings issue or not, but that never happened when I took pictures vertically outside of the water. When I returned home from the pool and opened the battery compartment there was water inside despite making sure that the compartment was sealed shut. From that point on, the camera would turn on but the screen remained black and it was unable to take pictures.

I contacted Nikon about the issue and the only response from them was to send it in for service... that costs an estimated $125 to repair! Are you kidding me? That's a ridiculous amount of money to spend when there are other waterproof cameras currently on the market that have better reviews and cost around $150! It's absolutely insulting that Nikon would try to gouge their customers with exorbitant repair rates when the camera clearly did not function as advertised. If you look at other reviews, you will notice quite a few people have suffered the same consequences, sustaining water damage after only one use underwater. That is unacceptable, and Nikon should work harder with their customers to rectify the situation instead of robbing them of even more money. Apologies if this review turned into a rant, but I'm furious that I paid around $250 for the camera and now Nikon is trying to get me to pay another $125 just to get the camera to work like it was supposed to!

Buyer beware!

product_title: D-Link Wireless Pan and Tilt Day/Night Network Surveillance Camera with mydlink-Enabled
review_headline: Could be great but isn't very good
review_body:
The price is ok, but the experience is not very good for a few reasons:

1) Norton Antivirus quarantines one of the setup files as known-dangerous. The only way to get the camera running is to add a security exemption. Hmmmm.

2) No way to trigger photos from motion or sound detection, it only sends text email notifications which is pretty useless since there is no record of the event. Advanced setup says it will email images and video, but it doesn't work: the emails arrive text-only. This is the biggest problem for me since there is basically no security value.

3) Does not work through glass at night, the IR LED's reflect off glass at all angles, blinding the camera. Without glass in front of the camera, the IR night vision works very well.

4) Panning can only be done in increments, one nudge at a time. That works ok from a laptop, but the iphone app is flawed and rotates the video feed after every nudge, delaying the next nudge by 5 or more seconds as you have to physically rotate your phone orientation each time. Painful.

5) Picture quality is 480p which is ok but not great, zoom is digital so it only makes the same resolution picture larger, there is no optical zoom.

review_headline: It would be great if it was not so complicated, lasted more then a month and Foscam actually had some support.
review_body:
Update 09/09/2013.

After less then a month the camera quite. After days of trying and two hours on the phone with Foscam's Tech Support (what a joke!), it was determined that the camera was broken. Now here comes the best part. Are you ready for it? The Tech suppport could not issue an RMA number or even connect me to someone who could. NOOOO!! That would be way too simple! No I have to write a custom email message to another department and wait for them to contact me. No matter how this turns out, I will never buy another Foscam product again!!!

Original Review:

Pros: Great features and capability.

Cons: Complicated setup for a consumer grade product and it is incompatible with Wimax type internet connections for remote access.

REVIEW:

I bought this camera for my mom to use to monitor my grandparent's house who are very elderly but still want to live on their own. So remote access was the solitary purpose I bought the camera for, so that my mom could care for her parents without having to move into their house with them. Unfortunately, to setup this camera to be accessed remotely requires an extremely high level of tech expertise. It is not a simple process. I am a certified PC tech and the task was daunting even for me.

At first I tried to set it up for remote access at my own house just to try it out and see if it worked. After five days of trying and working Foscam's tech support, I was unable to get the remote access function to work. I have Wimax internet service and Foscam blamed my ISP for the problem and wanted me to ask them to reconfigure their hardware to make it compatible with their cameras, to which my ISP support just fell on the floor laughing.

I almost returned the camera at this point, but decided to try it out at my mom's house on her cable internet connection. It was still complicated to setup, but I was eventually able to get remote access to the camera. So it turns out that Foscam was right about the problem being my Wimax internet connection. According to market analyst, Wimax will become the most common type of internet service in the near future because of it flexibility and potential for growth. One day Foscam will have to find a way to make their cameras compatible with Wimax. Until then, don't buy a Foscam camera if you have a Wimax internet connection. Now you may be thinking that you don't have a Wimax connection, but 4G LTE is essentially Wimax and I doubt this camera will work over a 4G LTE connection either.

As for the camera itself, it works great and is quite amazing. The mic is super sensitive and picks up the smallest sound. This is good and bad. It is good because you can hear everything that goes on in the room and even the adjacent rooms, but it is bad because you get a loop audio effect which sounds like the echo in a canyon. Foscam need to improve their software to compensate for this.

The bottom line is this. If you want a camera for in home monitoring over your local area Wifi network (like for a baby monitor), then this camera is great. But if you plan to use it as a security camera which you can access when you are away from home, then you had better prepare for a task. If you have cable, DSL, Fios or any other hardwired internet service you might be able to remotely access this camera, but if you have a Wimax internet connection, you can forget using this camera or any other Foscam IP camera for remote access. Foscam needs to learn how to make a consumer product that is consumer friendly. Very few consumers will have the tech skill to setup remote access to this camera without several calls to customer support. Since they market this as a consumer grade product with Remote Access as a primary function of the camera, they need to make the remote access setup process a lot easier.camera. product_title: NIX Pro Series 12" Digital Frame with Motion Detection Sensor
review_body:
Received this frame and really liked the size, look, and functionality. Unfortunately... the first one I got quit working a month and half later. I had it set to turn off after an hour of no motion detect, and it would just go to a white screen and stay there. So it was still on, and using power showing a bright white screen until I re-started it.

Since I was past the 30 days for Amazon to return/replace, I emailed Nix directly and they were very cooperative in resolving the issue. I had to send my frame back (at their expense... pre-printed UPS label) so besides being without the frame for a few weeks, no complaints.

Only problem is... the replacement I received is also defective. Now... the motion detect shuts down the frame after an hour, but the frame immediately turns itself right back on. I have tested it over and over to make sure there is nothing weird movement-wise going on, and there isn't. It simply turns back on after shutting off as if it detected something when nothing is there. This naturally makes the motion detect feature useless, I might as well just leave it on 24/7.

So I have emailed Nix again, and am hoping they'll be as easy to deal with as they were the first time. I'm giving the frame 3 stars because as I said, looks and (if working) functionality are pretty nice. The price is also appealing. The question is, is the price so appealing because of issues like I appear to be having?

Will update what happens with the 3rd time around on this frame.

UPDATE: Received another pre-paid UPS label and have sent the 2nd frame back. Now awaiting delivery of a replacement and *fingers crossed* this will solve the problem(s).

8/30/13 UPDATE: Received the 3rd frame, and this one does not work right out of the box. Unbelievable. No screen image whatsoever, though the blue control lights on the right side will come on. I'm done with this, and have changed my rating to a 1 star. Maybe I'm just unlucky, but I say buyer beware big time with this item. Have emailed both Nix and Amazon stating my desire for a refund so I can obtain a product that might actually work.

product_title: Orion StarBlast 4.5 EQ Reflector - Telescope - f/4.0 - reflector
review_headline: Okay for beginners but lacks the proper lenses.
review_body:
Decent scope for the money, but the thing that is lacking is the stock lenses. They lack the power to see anything "amazing" other than the moon. After reading more reviews, I found that a "must have" for this or most any scopes is a lens called a "Barlow". The entry level Barlow lenses double the magnification or you can get one the magnifies 5x the stock lens for just under $200. The cheapest Barlow lens is $50, which I believe should have been included as a stock lens. Orion's own support technician sent me a link to a video calling this lens specifically a "must have accessory". After I pointed out, they agreed to send me one at no charge, which was more than fair. But I still believe that it should have been included in the first place. The bottom line is that if you have to buy expensive lenses to make it better, then why not just buy a more expensive telescope, with better optics to begin with? Orion's customer service seems to be very customer friendly and stand behind the products that they sell. I haven't gotten the lens yet after several days, but will revise if I never receive.

My synopsis is that this is sort of the equivalent of giving away free hot peppers, then selling a glass of water for $50. I would be willing to pay the extra price for bundled lenses that allow you to get everything out of this scope. It's just not apparent to a novice what it's limitations are without additional lenses. It's not a advertised as professional scope, but by the time you purchase the extra lenses, you might be better off going with a professional grade. The cost will offset.

If you're really not into astronomy, buy a $60 beginner's scope and you'll have roughly the same view. If you get hooked after that, then buy a real telescope.

review_headline: Excellent camera after a year of use

I own several DSLR's in addition to my Lumix GX1, OMD E-M5 and E-P5.

The E-P5 flash release button is poorly designed in that every time I handle the camera I inadvertently release the flash. Nearly always when I remove it from my Lowepro Adventura Ultra Zoom 100 case the flash is popped up and just waiting for me to break it.

After using the extremely well-designed E-M5 with its separate and substantial card and battery doors the flimsy door on the E-P5's combo compartment is annoying and waiting to be broken.

My other big gripe is the arrangement of the control dials on the E-P5. One cannot use the E-P5 and the E-M5 interchangeably because the E-P5 mode dial and the E-M5 rear control dial are in the same position which leads to confusion and mistakes. One has to get used to one or the other or one has to stop and think about which camera is being used.

It does take great pictures.

Update Feb 8, 2014: I used the EP-5 extensively and then gave it to my daughter who owns several cameras. She loves the camera paired with the Lumix 20mm lens. BTW the flash is still taped shut and has never been used because it is totally unnecessary with the fast lens and the excellent IBIS.

product_title: Wasabi Power Battery
review_body:
Using a recently calibrated iCharger 206B, I ran a few discharge tests on both of the Wasabi LP-E6 batteries I received. Testing with a 500mA drain from a 8.4V full charge to a depleted 6.0V, the batteries only gave me 1300mAh and 1409mAh. This is half of the claimed capacity. The claimed capacity numbers are being increased by Wasabi to \\"compete\\" with other brands that also do not meet their stated capacities.

Using the included battery charger, the batteries get slightly overcharged at 8.44V. 4.22V per cell is a bit higher than the 4.20V they should stop at, but it shouldn't be enough to cause major cell damage.

- The original Canon LP-E6 battery is rated at 1800mAh and sells for MSRP. Running with a 500mA drain, my 2-year old Canon battery provided 2095mAh.
- The Wasabi LP-E6 battery is sold as 2600mAh, but it tests between 1300-1400mAh. This battery sells for 1/4 the price of the Canon.

For the price, the battery works, but you will be swapping batteries almost twice as often. I cannot provide 5 stars because the battery capacity is falsely advertised like many today. I cannot provide 4 stars because the battery does not come close to the Canon battery, which was released with the technology available 5 years ago.

These batteries do not come close to matching the Canon in capacity, but they are 1/4 the price. I will not comment on expected cell degredation since it has not been tested, but other reviewers have covered my thoughts well enough.

I am moving on with the search for an aftermarket LP-E6 battery that offers similar capacity to the genuine Canon product.

*This review has been updated to better reflect my view on the VALUE of these batteries, rather than focusing on the marketing tactics of false capacity numbers*

The issue I ran into with both cameras is lines on the video, especially when in color mode. I thought maybe it had something to do with the lighting in the room I was placing the cameras so I tried out the 933L in their place. It had no issues whatsoever, the 933L is also nice since it supports video without needing Java.

I upgraded to the newest firmware, tried playing around with the anti-flicker settings, and it made no difference. I also tried contacting DLink support but have heard nothing. Searching the web it looks like others have had the same issue and ended up returning the cameras. Unfortunately I will be following suit.

Of course with so much stuff, it was not light; but once the excess items were removed, it was easier on my shoulders than my shoulder bag would have been. I found the construction to be strong with no splitting seams, etc. despite all the stuff I loaded into it. In fact, my only regret was that I forgot to take with me my tripod which can be carried in a space provided on the bottom (see product gallery image #18).

I heeded the advise of J. Remias and removed the Cannon logo from the bag (see product gallery image #40) and replaced it with a red rose. Thus the bag no longer looked like a camera bag but rather as a somewhat funky backpack. This gave me an added sense of security while travelling.

I highly recommend this bag to everyone, especially those who like to take their cameras with them when they travel.

product_title: Airbox Lights 450031 Macro Softbox (Black)
review_headline: Effective, but a shame to have to pay so much for so little
review_body:
As a softbox, it does the job. There was no real convenient way to place diffusion gel on my small LED panels, so it definitely fills a need. Opening the package was a bit disappointing though because it looked and smelled like a 99 cent pool toy and a couple of strips of velcro. Now, I'm not necessarily calling it overpriced, because there are economic factors of product design and manufacturing on a very small scale (there are probably not a ton of these getting made and sold) I just wish I didn't have to pay so much for so little.

Functionally, it is okay. I use the larger Sony-style batteries on the back of my LED panels and the velcro straps go right over the top of them, so it's a bit fiddly getting it attached. I use regular diffusion gels on the barndoors of my larger LED panels, and it seems like the setup time and diffusion quality is roughly the same. The thin vinyl tabs that attach to the velcro straps look precarious at best, but for all I know could hold up fine. There is a vinyl repair patch kit that comes with it in case it gets torn or punctured. I hope to not have to use this, but sort of expect that I will at some point.

So far the pros outweigh the cons as I now have soft, even, portable battery powered variable color temp lighting.

Update: So after a half dozen or so shoots the inevitable happened and one of those little vinyl tabs tore off. Bummer. Here's the good part though - I wrote the guy that makes these and sent him pictures of what happened and he sent me replacement units that have a new design that looks a ton better. The design looks much more integrated and the straps don't look like they are going to tear off with the new ones. Big improvement.

product_title: Kata KT DL-MX-20 MarvelX-20 DL Camera Pouch - Black
review_headline: Not Suitable For NEX-6 but there are others that are...
review_body:
This is a very well made camera case and it is very small which is what I wanted. The problem is that my Sony NEX-6 barely fit with the standard pancake 16-50 lens. You can not place the camera into the case sideways (vertically) as it is too shallow to accommodate it so you must put it in face down and that is the problem. The camera barely fits width-wise and so in order to close the case you have to stretch the zipper around the camera and pull it over the camera body and then carefully zip it shut. Getting the camera out of the case is a bit easier but still a chore and would definitely slow you down.

What I look for in a case is: protection for my camera, a belt loop so I can wear it at my waist so it doesn't move around and the ability to to get it in and out of the case quickly so it doesn't interfere with picture taking. Having to fuss every time I put it back into the case would negate it's purpose - at least for me. That said, the Sony NEX-3N and the NEX-5 are just a bit smaller and would probably fit better than the NEX-6 does. The tag on the case that says that it's for Sony NEX cameras is a bit misleading.

Amazon does carry two camera cases that the NEX-6 will fit into, both made by Lowepro: the [[ASIN:B004R71D0I Lowepro Compact ILC Courier 70 Digital Micro Four-Thirds Camera Case - Black]] which is a bit larger than the Kata DL-MX-20 so that the NEX-6 fits both sideways (vertically) or face down. The other case is actually smaller than the Kata and is a pouch type case, also with a belt loop yet just a bit deeper so the camera can be placed in vertically, [[ASIN:B00012FVYW Lowepro Rezo 60 Camera Case (Black)]] and zipped shut. Now here is a nice other use for the Lowepro Rezo 60, it can be used to carry your extra lens! I bought the NEX-6 with the optional Sony zoom lens [[ASIN:B005IHAIKM Sony E 55-210mm F4.5-6.3 Lens for Sony NEX Cameras]] and the lens fits perfectly in the Rezo 60 (with the lens shade reversed over the lens) sonow I go hiking with my NEX-6 in the Courier 70 and my extra lens in the Rezo 60, both on my waist.

In case you were wondering, the Courier 70 will accommodate the NEX-6 with the 55-210 lens on the camera however, you can not zip it shut but you can close it using the flap which goes over the zipped portion of the case and yes, it can still reach the velcro closure making it secure.

I hope this helped my fellow NEX-6 owners looking for a suitable camera case.

product_title: Sony SELP1650 16-50mm Power Zoom Lens (Silver, Bulk Packaging)
review_body:
This lens for me replaced the 18-55, 16mm pancake, and Sigma 30. Pretty good deal!

It bests the 18-55 in virtually every regard, except the build is not quite as good and it lacks a hood (minor complaints).

It's as wide as the 16mm pancake, and although slower, it has OSS, so it's generally a wash. It won't take the ultra wide or fisheye adapters that the 16mm can, but I didn't have those anyway. It's not as flat, but it's much smaller than the 18-55, making the 16mm less necessary just for size reasons.

It's not as sharp as the Sigma 30, but it's good enough. It's also not as fast, but again it has OSS, so it's better for video and generally a wash otherwise. It's also about the same size in practice.

So, this lens for me replaced 3 lenses. I use this and the 50 f1.8. If I need small and wide, I take this. If I need fast, I take the prime.

If you are a lens snob, you'll hate this lens. If you're using an original NEX 3 or 5, or shooting RAW, and not using software to correct distortion, you'll hate this lens. If you use a F3, 3N, 5N, or any of the new bodies with distortion correction, or use Lightroom or other software for distortion correction, you'll think this lens is fine. If you want something practical, like me, you'll probably really like this lens.

The power zoom is fine. It's smoother but louder. For still photos, it's generally a wash, and the price you pay for the size. For video, it is smoother but louder, so again, decide which is more important for you for video.

review_headline: Warning: Don't use with both GoPro and Phantom Wi-Fi systems engaged togther. Lost control.
review_body:
They didn't warn me about this problem: I tried using my quadcopter with my GoPro camera's Wi-Fi turned on. I wanted to monitor the camera on my iPad. The Phantom quadcopter went out of control and crashed into my neighbor's arm giving him a rather deep cut. I tried flying again, and the Phantom quadcopter went out of control and flew away. I searched in the direction it went using my iPad to try and get a signal from the GoPro Wi-Fi, but I never found it. It may have flown far away; I don't know where it went. I lost both camera and quadcopter and my neighbor is mad at me.

There is no warning on the Phantom box. No operating manual came with the product. I used the operating instructions I found on the dji company web site. There is no warning on that web site that I can see. After I lost my camera and quadcopter, I did find a small warning on the B&H Photo web site.

The B&H Photo web site warning says: Warning: Never use the DJI Phantom Quadcopter with your GoPro camera when both devices have their Wi-Fi systems turned on. The DJI Phantom's Wi-Fi and the GoPro camera's Wi-Fi run on the same frequency, so if you use them together when both Wi-Fi systems are engaged, the DJI Phantom's transmitter will lose the ability to communicate with the DJI Phantom Quadcopter. Whenever this happens, you will not be able to tell the Phantom where to fly. This may result in loss of property or damage to your equipment.

It would be a nice product if they sent proper operating instructions and warnings.

product_title: Sanyo Universal 2-Position Quick Charger Set with 2 AA Eneloop NiMH Batteries
review_body:
I purchased this charger on Amazon. It was shipped from Adorama Camera. Picture and description matched Sanyo 2-cell charger NC-MDR02NU, and I was very surprised when I received SEC-TDN02N.

These two chargers are much different. MDR02 can charge AA and AAA, and TDN02 can charge only AA. About half batteries I use are AAA, so TDN02 charger is a waste of money for me.

I went to Sanyo website to check if TDN02 is a Smart Charger, and was surprised again, because this charger is not listed there! Is it real SANYO product?

If someone doesn't know why smart charger is better, it is because it can detect when battery is full to stop charging, as oppose the other chargers rely on charging time only. If battery was not fully discharged, the time based charger will overcharge battery. This will overheat battery, which shortens the battery live substantially or can render it dead. Heat during charge cycle is worst enemy of NiMH batteries. Overcharge also is main cause for what people call memory effect.

Also it isn't clear to me if this charger can charge individual battery as MDR02. Google search returned me very little about TDN02, and I think it can't, but I can't say for sure, as I didn't open retail package. I will try return it, and if I fail, I add more info here.

I own many chargers. I have NC-MDR02NU among them, which I definitely recommend and would give 5 stars, but since the one I got isn't, I give it only 1.

product_title: Foscam FI8904W Outdoor Wireless/Wired IP Camera with 15 - 20 Meter Night Vision and 2.8mm Lens (50° Viewing Angle) - Silver
review_headline: Overheats, Sends Garbled Images, Drops Out of Wireless AND Wired Networks
review_body:
Well, I'm not sure how there are so many good reviews about this product, but my experience with it has been terrible. I ordered two of these, and ended up returning both because they simply don't work outside when the outdoor temp is >70 degrees F. Both cameras started sending garbled images (portions of the image out of place or scrambled), corrupted images (images that can't be opened at all), and psychedelic green/purple images when the temperature outside warms up. These garbled/psychedelic images appeared both in the camera's built-in viewing website and in email/FTP motion detection alerts. Eventually the cameras would simply drop off the network until the outdoor temperature cooled down at night.

I had these cameras connected using a Cat 6 Ethernet cable - not wifi. I tried connecting to two different routers, tried different Ethernet cables, and different electrical outlets. I tested the electricity from my outdoor outlet and from the power brick that came with the camera - they were all fine. I tried storing the power brick and other connections in a water-resistant container with a desiccant pack to buffer against humidity fluctuations and prevent condensation. Nothing made any difference. The cameras worked fine when left inside, but as soon as they were mounted outside, they would drop out mid-day when the temperature increased above 70F. These cameras were NOT mounted in direct sunlight. Maybe I just got two lemons, but at this point I think I'm done trying. I guess I'll just save up for a more expensive/more reputable brand of camera.

review_body:
Initially, these binoculars seemed like a good birding bino. They have a very wide field of view and close focus. The image is bright and crisp, true color, low distortion. Long eye relief, waterproof and fog proof. All at a reasonable price due to being made in China.
I got these along with the Vortex harness. The connectors (small straps with eyelets and D rings) don't fit the slots on the bino! Vortex's elegant solution is to include small tie wraps instead. This isn't a problem with the Vortex Razors, which are made in Japan.
A bigger disappointment is the focus mechanism. It takes 1.7 turns to go from end to end, which is excessive. After six weeks of breaking in, the gear has developed slop and slap. Very annoying in tracking birds. I now have to send them in for adjustment. If I had it to do over again I'd pass on these bins. I'm done buying any optics made in China; it's not called Chintzy for nothing. Be skeptical of marketing hype and reviews of initial impressions since it can fool you if you trust it.

review_body:
So, long story, my beloved s95 ended up in the washing machine. Don't ask.

I looked around for another s95 -- they now cost *more* than they did when they came out, presumably because the demand is still high enough to warrant it. Not surprising really... it's still one of the few remaining cameras at it's price point that will shoot RAW and provides manual controls.

What to do? I read the reviews of the s100 and 110.

I needed/wanted a fairly basic camera that would produce nice shots and give me manual controls when I wanted them. I didn't need the GPS (people really use that?) or a touch screen. Based on the comparison reviews here on Amazon, I took a chance on the s100.

I've had a very favorable experience so far.

It does everything my s95 did, I leave the GPS switched off so the battery lasts 300+ shots, and the ergonomics are a slight improvement. The changes to the buttons a few reviews mentioned were incidental to me. Easy to grok, easy to work with. The sensor is producing nice clear shots and the improvement in pixels has improved the quality of the macro shots I enjoy. I'm not keen on the quality of the flash images (still learning to improve that) but the low light shots are pretty good.

I would say that, after a month of daily use, I'm glad I made this decision. Based on my experience so far, I would say that the reviews which gave the s100 a slight edge of the s95 were accurate.

review_body:
CAUTION: Decent flash, but doesn't play real well with Nikon camera.

I have a Nikon D800 and a Nikkor 60mm closeup lens which I wanted to use with this inexpensive flash. Unfortunately, the hot-shoe attachment does not provide any information to the camera body about the existence of the flash or how it's configured, so the camera sets up the exposure as if there is no flash present. (The hot shoe's single pair of contacts allow the camera to fire the flash, but nothing more.) Yes, it's possible to manually configure the flash in the camera's flash settings, but this is cumbersome since you have to do it every time you change the flash's options. Another option is to run the flash continually like a flashlight, so that the camera's light meter measures it's output. I thought I would settle for that, until I found that this exhausted 4 new AA batteries in about 5 minutes.

Also, the included lens-mounting rings do not include one which fits the filter threads on my closeup lens, although one of the rings sort of snaps over the front of the lens tube well enough to hold it in place.

One other tiny note: if you don't retract the hot-shoe lock ring 100%, the hot shoe will not unlock from the camera body. I initially thought it might detach if only loosened, but there is a locking pin in addition to the friction lock.

Other than these issues, the flash seems well made, and it provides good lighting. For me, the lack of control feedback was a deal-killer, but the price is good and maybe it will work well enough for you in spite of this limitation.
