product_title: Expoimaging Rogue FlashBender Kit, with Bounce Card / Flag, Large Positionable Reflector & Small Positionable Reflector
review_body: i am a professional photographer and i purchased these for circumstances when i need to move quickly and shoot a lot of variety in low-light situations.  these flash benders made an enormous difference in lighting quality -- better than just bouncing the flash as it puts so much more light up into the subject's eyes.  i used the middle size most as it was more manageable on camera than the large but also more versatile for 'bending' the light exactly how i wanted than the small. definitely recommend this product.  have also used it some for location lighting with flashes on stands -- their small size and flat style allow me to keep in my bag to be prepared for any situation.

product_title: 3:2 Swi-View LCDVF LCD Viewfinder for Canon 60D, T3i, any other 3:2 3" LCD Cameras by Carry Speed
review_body:
This looks like an pretty good item, but I wanted to warn Canon T3i users as the description says it works with that.

The T3i has a viewfinder than is closed. You open the viewfinder, swivel 180 degrees, and snap it back into itself. Now it is just like any other camera. To protect it and put it away, you swivel it 180 degrees and snap back in.

Here's the problems. If you mount the metal frame, it's adhesive. if you try and \\"put away\\" the viewfinder it will no longer work, you'll have to leave it in its
open\\" position with the viewfinder exposed.

I thought I could get around this by purchasing the metal mounting hardware that mounts to the bottom of camera. This would work very well, but if you have a battery grip on your camera liek mine, forget it. It won't work.

I am rating this high as I can see it would work well with other cameras, just not the Canon T3i (600d) series.

product_title: Kodak Playsport Zx5 Video Camera
review_body:
In looking over all the reviews I still decided to purchase this camera, but wanted to see it first hand so I ended up going to Best Buy. I was worried that all the reviews were true and that the entire package would be a problematic nightmare.

Suffice to say only a small part of that came true. The first camera I purchased took horrible photos. I sent them to Kodak for verification and they said the images looked ok to them. I decided that while still under the grace period of returns, to do just that and head back to swap out for another. I am glad I did because the camera takes better pictures and the video features work very well.

To prove that it worked so well I gave the camera to my 8 yr old son in the pool. In fact I simply dropped it in the pool and told him to dive for it. He dove for it and after a few quick lessons he was off and running taking pictures and underwater video. The pictures were mush clearer and the underwater video came out amazing. The audio worked underwater and the camera functions were very easy to use, even for my 6 yr old daughter.

There did seem to be low light photo image issues but nothing that was super bothering. This is more of an underwater video system that works well in wet, and high moisture environments. It's very user friendly, with 4 settings for special effects and super easy software that loaded right up on my Mac. The Share button is a simple push button away and ready to offer you the chance to get your images to the internet.

So, read up all you want on the specifics of the unit and come back here for the truth about the camera basics. Had I not had to return the first camera this review would have gotten 5 stars. As it stands I'm pleased with my purchase and will update the review as I work through future photographic and video events.

I used the camera today - June 11th at cooking contest I entered along with pool time with the family right after the cook off. The camera worked perfectly in video mode and took a great video of my son playing in the pool. the pictures I took were equally as nice but I had to really focus on keeping the camera still at time to make sure I go a good shot. Underwater images were actually pretty nice and the kids really liked getting their picture taken under water.ly in video mode and took a great video of my son playing in the pool. the pictures I took were equally as nice but I had to really focus on keeping the camera still at time to make sure I go a good shot. Underwater images were actually pretty nice and the kids really liked getting their picture taken under water.

product_title: Polaroid PoGo Instant Digital Mobile Printer
review_body: I have been searching for a printer to create a photo guestbook for my wedding next month.  I really wanted to use my polaroid 600 camera, but the cost of prints was just not worth it.  To have enough photos for my guests to even take one picture each was astronomical.  Finding a printer that was both portable AND easy to use was proving to be a challenge...I didn't want to have to lug my laptop AND a printer with me so guests could take pictures using like a photobooth software, and the quality would be crappy at best.  WELL, after some searching, the Pogo printer was the perfect alternative.  I didn't want it to replace an actual photo printer, I just wanted something portable that would print acceptable pictures for my guestbook.  The fact that this can be used with any camera/bluetooth enabled phone AND that it has a sticky back is just amazing gravy.  I've been playing with it, and I found the quality pretty good for the cost.  Bluetooth took about 1 1/2 minutes to send/resize and print, and my digital camera hooked up via usb took less than 30 seconds!  And my camera is very high resolution, so I know it had to resize it a lot.  I took the suggestion of other reviewers and put the blue sheet in every few prints and it seems fine...that is actually the solution to streaky photos that the instructions suggest (and also running a Zink sheet through upside down to clean the ink off of the wheels).  My only concern is that it does seem to run a bit hot when left plugged in, but I'm not overly concerned with that.  I'm also not worried about short battery life as I can leave it plugged in place all night so it shouldn't be a problem.  Honestly, considering the alternatives to something like this (say, the Fuji camera I looked into) are triple the cost with film (at minimum) AND don't allow for multiple cameras (so easier to share/manage in a party situation), I have to say this is a great product.

product_title: KAEZI 16-Inch Photo Studio Tent In a Box Light Cube - 1 Tent, 2 Light Set, 1 Stand, 1 Case
review_headline: Very Good, but still..Could Be Better
review_body:
I would say, overall so far, I'm very pleased with this photo studio in a box. It assembles very quickly, no instructions needed (nor were any given with my package). The lights seem to be sub-par in my opinion, and they actually start to smell as though they are burning, after only being on for a couple of minutes. I would say the light they provide is ample, yet you could easily benefit from upgrading to a larger set, and I know they creators of this know that, seeing as how they sell an upgraded lighting set for more money.

The blue, red, black and white backdrops are perfect! Yes they arrived folded, so they will have annoying creases in the them, that you will have to iron out, but I really can't think of another way they could have shipped them and still have all of the kit in one box. So that's nothing really to detract from the overall quality of the package, it's just an annoying necessity that you'll have to deal with. The fact that it all rolls up into a carrying pouch is perfect and I can't really imagine how this could be any more functional and at the same time be easy to carry and move around.

So for the money, I'd say you're getting your dollars worth, but what keeps this package from attaining a grade of \\"A+\\", is definitely the lackluster lighting. I fear that they will one day burst into flames, or more likely I'll have to replace the bulbs of the whole lights themselves very soon. But for what you get, you really can't find a better deal for the money, at least none that I've seen, and I researched this quite a lot on Amazon.

Overall Grade and Satisfaction: B++

review_body: I've had this camera for about 2 weeks now. I received it well within the timeframe specified by the shipper. I havent used the camera much but my initial reactions are:    Pros:  1. Very small and sleek: I used to have a canon powershot A95. So this is a welcome change. Fits very easily in my shirt pocket and really lightweight.    2. Picture clarity: This is really good. Took about 30-40 pictures near the lake and experimented with the different scene settings [foliage] - I can see the difference clearly.    Cons:  The LCD screen is quite large [compared to the A95] and is always open. So I get a little worried about fingerprints and smudges. I am trying to find some sort of a cover for this similar to what I have for my iPhone.    I think the lens is wider than that A95, so pictures taken when I am about 10 paces from the subject seems to include a lot of area around the subject. In fact I love that it has a wide-angle lens.    To me, neither of these two \\"cons\\" are a deal-breaker.    I plan to experiment more in the coming weeks, so I will be updating this review in about 3-4 weeks.    Bottomline: If you are looking for an affordable, sleek, lightweight camera with really good results, go for it! I love canon.

product_title: Fujifilm FinePix S3200 14 MP Digital Camera with Fujinon 24x Super Wide Angle Optical Zoom Lens and 3-Inch LCD
review_headline: Great little camera with AWFUL CUSTOMER SERVICE
review_body: Wow, I got this camera yesterday and had a great afternoon and early evening taking pictures of all kinds. I was very happy with my new camera. The features are great and the pictures are excellent. BUT, I had a problem with connecting it to a pc to download my pictures. Yes, I can still take out the card and download them through a card reader but let me finish my story..... I call support after trying multiple usb ports on 4 computers, tried another cord that works fine with another camera.....everything I could possibly think of. So support guy starts at the top of his list and he decides that it has to be a bad connector on the camera so he sends me over to repair for directions on how to get it repaired. They want me send it in for them to determine if it is covered under the 1 year warranty.1st I must pay to ship it to them. If the problem is not covered under warranty,or is deemed wear and tear, I will have to pay the repair fee and return shipping. (to get my brand new camera back). They did say however that if it was covered under warranty they would pay to express ship it back to me(please allow 6-8 weeks.....really....I then asked to speak to a manager and was put on hold for a couple of minutes until \\"someone else\\" came on the line to immediately explain their return policy that has been in place for over 30 years. They couldn't shut up which is where I got really turned off and is the reason I am writing this review. He said I was lucky that the camera still actually worked that most of the calls they get about this situation come from the connector somehow causing the camera to completely not work. He said that cables are overrated and card readers are the way to go so if I just go buy one, then all of my problems will be solved. He continued to belittle me by strongly suggesting that I caused the problem by trying to put the cable in the wrong way, \\" some people don't realize that it only goes in one way\\" Really..... again..., I finally thanked him for his time and politely hung up. I said all of that to say this. I like the camera, but the fact that \\"at least my camera still worked\\" (his words) the second day that I had it didn't give me any warm fuzzies about the overall quality of this camera. They didn't seem to care that the camera was one day old or the fact that I am a \\"first time\\" FUJI customer. Folks, this camera may be a good one at a good price but its not the only one I can assure you. I WILL NEVER BUY ANOTHER FUJI PRODUCT IN MY LIFE...Customer service still means something to me. I would suggest that you keep looking............

product_title: Domke 700-02W F-2 Original Bag (Brown)
review_body: I was fortunate enough to purchase one of the original dozen F-2 bags that were shipped for retail sale by Jim Domke to National Camera Repair on Pennsylvania N.W., Washington, DC., in 1976.     Five of us in the same company bought them on the same day and we all realized immediately that it was the absolutely best camera bag to come onto the photographers equipment market up to that time. And between about 28 photographers....we had tried every type and shape camera bag made up until then.    What was so great about this bag was that after using it for a couple of months, it started to mold itself around not only your equipment, but where it touched your waistline. It was like a form fitted leather driving glove. I used this first bag from 1976 until 1984, five and six days a week, rain, sleet, snow or sunshine.     In my time on the street I probably went through six or eight F-2's.    And...........sitting on a shelf in retirement after those many years of service, is my great old friend, patched with blue jean denim and sewn with a leather repair kit on occasion, is the old workhorse, my first 1976 original Domke Bag made of just plain old butcher apron canvas.    What a bag!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

product_title: Wasabi Power Battery and Charger for Sony NP-F950, NP-F960, NP-F970, NP-F975 (8500mAh)
review_headline: Great Battery at a Great Price
review_body: Before you read too far.  If some of this sounds familiar, I had written a similar review for a battery for my Canon XA10 and did not feel like recreating the wheel so I changed only the information I needed to in order to give my honest opinion on this particular battery.    Now, I have read reviews that say your camera wont be able to communicate with NON OEM batteries and you wont be able to see the battery life still left available - HOGWASH. I have owned Canon GL1's & GL2's, Sony VX2000's & VX2100's and NOW the NEW Canon XA10 and the XF100 and ALL of them work/operate/report and perform Perfectly fine with Wasabi Power Batteries. The Sony NP F570  that came with the camera is a smaller battery does not last very long (maybe 1.5 to 2 hrs) BUT this NPF960 Wasabi Power replacement battery is a MUST have. review_headline: Great Camera for those who don't have time and money to learn DSLR
review_body: I purchased this camera for my road trip to Seattle and Vancouver recently.   The reason of purchasing this camera is (1) I don't have time to learn to use DSLR. If I cannot explore the best feature of DSLR, it will not do me any good. This camera has all the features I want. (2) If I don't have to learn to use DSLR, there is no point to spend almost $1,000 for a decent DSLR.   Most of my photos were taken in good light condition and the quality of those photos were excellent. For the photos in poor light condition, the flash light help. Also, without a manual, it is easy to figure out the settings of the camera after a few tries.      There are something that I want to complain about this camera though:  1. I wish that Canon can have automatic cover for the lens just like other PowerShot series camera. Sometimes it is a little bit annoying to remove the cover when you see something you want to capture and it is passing by.  2. There is a button right below the on-off button which automatically set the camera to the scene and surrounding condition. If you accidentally press this button, it will automatically adjust the zoom and other settings and you cannot change it. I did not realize it until this happened three to four times.   3. The battery runs out fast. It requires recharge about every 300 - 350 photos. So, it is better to take extra battery if you are on a road trip.    I think it is wrong to compare this camera with DSLR camera. They are different types of cameras. I won't expect it to perform as well as a DSLR camera. I have to say that in order to get the best out of a camera (any camera), some basic knowledge and techniques of photography should be needed. We cannot blame the poor photo quality because we shoot pictures randomly in all condition.

product_title: Pandigital Photolink One-Touch PANSCN06 8.5-Inch x11-Inch Photo Scanner
review_body:
Wow! This scanner exceeded my expectations for such a small and inexpensive gadget. Set up was pretty easy. Initially, I hooked the scanner up through my PC so that I could immediately see the images and get a good idea of any quirks I'd need to manage. Once I got the hang of it, I disconnected it from the PC and made myself comfortable as I went through envelope after envelope of family photos.

Overall, the first batch of scans were hassle free. Yes, you do need to pay attention to the photo as it feeds through to be sure it doesn't end up crooked. Because I was scanning photos of a variety of sizes, I didn't want to keep nudging the guide around, so I used my index finger as the guide. Scans are fast. At the 300dpi setting, the scanner was ready to take the next photo within 10-15 seconds. At the 600dpi setting it was generally double. (Makes sense, huh?)

Having read the reviews here and seeing that a lot of people reported white lines on their scans, I was super careful with my photos. I was sure to keep a lint free cloth on my lap and I wiped each photo on that cloth just before feeding through the scanner. Generally, I'd scan somewhere between 30-40 photos before taking out the canned air and giving the scanner a little *poof*. I used the included swab about every 100 photos.

While I had zero problems with white lines running through the images, I do have a small portion of the edge of the scans that is slightly lighter than the rest of the image. This was the case from the first photo scanned, so I know it isn't my fault for wearing the darn thing out. I ran the calibration card through right away, and the light edge is still there, although it is generally more noticeable on scans of photos where the image background was lighter to begin with. I played around with the scans to see if I could figure out what was causing it, and it seems that the lightened edge is at whichever end of the photograph gets the 'exit push' from the scanner. It would seem that perhaps this has something to do with the ejection of the photograph, and this may be why some people have reported better luck when using the clear sleeve. For the most part, the light edge didn't bother me, especially since so many of the older photos had a white border anyway. I'm scanning photos just to share with family and archive things for personal use. If I had a photo where I didn't want to impact a certain part of the photo, I'd try to turn the photo when scanning so that the lightened edge was at a part of the photo that was less important. Really, the edge wasn't that noticeable in most of my images, so it wasn't enough for me to care all that much .. but was enough for me to knock a star off my rating.

Really, we're talking about a feed-scanner for under $100 that is speedy and does a bang-up job for your personal archive project. review_body:
Lowepro Passport Sling is a rather small shoulder bag, ideal for travelers, commuters and other casual shooters. It is not large enough to hold a professional dSLR with a grip attached. It is very useful with a smaller camera, such as micro four-thirds cameras, as you can carry a camera, an extra lens, a flash and personal items... It's also useful with compact cameras, such as Canon Powershot lines.

I also find it useful as a lens bag. When I shoot weddings, engagement photos, etc., I carry a professional dSLR on a strap and not in this case. But this case can carry one zoom and one or two prime lenses, and one flash unit. With this bag, I can exchange lens quickly while standing. So this is not a bad setup---it's just that my camera won't fit in this the padded compartment of this bag. Should they make the bag bigger? Well, a bit bigger to hold 3 SLR lenses with more room, but any larger would diminish the value of this design.

The unpadded part of this bag is tall enough to hold a regular size wine bottle (750ml). Does it hold 40oz beer? I don't drunk that stuff so I don't know that, and don't want to know, for that matter.

What this bag does not fit? That's iPad. Unless you remove the padded compartments altogether, this bag has absolutely no space for iPad.

So, this is a good for daily commuter and walk-around bag (with a micro four thirds camera), and when I have a commercial or wedding assignment, I use it to carry lenses with my dSLR with a grip (and a flash bracket, usually).

One thing I want them to change is to make the anti-slip pad on the shoulder strap much larger. I don't know why they made it such a small pad. It does help but could be better.

product_title: Panasonic Lumix DMC-FH1 12.1 MP Digital Camera with 5x Optical Image Stabilized Zoom and 2.7-Inch LCD (Black)
review_body: Received product from Amazon quickly and looked forward to testing it out before an upcoming vacation. After charging the battery, reading the manual, formatting some SDHC cards, and playing around with the modes and menus, I tried it out. As the title says, I immediately received either \\"system error (zoom)\\" or \\"please turn camera off and on again\\" errors when I atempted to zoom (just out of the box so no drops or sand, etc.). The zoom functionality worked maybe three times out of dozens and dozens of attempts (and won't work period at this point). The lens does move (not stuck in any position) and the camera will take a picture. It just won't zoom, which makes it the equivalent of a disposable. I contacted Panasonic's customer service dept. after registering the product and they told me to reset the camera and retry, which I did to no avail (several times). Further, they advised sending it to their customer service center in Texas for potential replacement with a reconditioned model (if under warranty - which it better be since I got it a week ago - and the aforementioned reset didn't work). I guess a reconditioned is the best they'll do. Of course, I don't have a time frame of when the reconditioned model will arrive (will be mailing it to them shortly), so I may need to purchase another camera before I leave. Don't know if this is a known issue with this model, but needless to say I'm not too happy. I'll update the review if I get a camera that works.    Revised review: Returned via Amazon's 30 day policy and received a new, working, model (much better than the refurbed option via Panasonic). Anyway, I used the camera pretty extensively and tried many of its functions. It isn't the greatest in low light (but you can improve things by playing around with the settings), and there are some issues with clarity/stabilization even with the OIS on. That said, it delivered some really good images and fits easily into any pocket (and well into a small Case Logic soft case also available on Amazon). Considering price, convenience, number of features, and solid image quality overall (and some images much better than that), I'd definitely recommend it (especially if you want something small to carry on your travels).

review_body: I started out with the 110 and then to 35mm. Then, several years ago the digital cameras and finally to the SRL digital cameras. I received this from Amazon and was shocked that it takes better pictures than my SRL that costs a lot more. Plus, it's smaller and seems more sturdy. I now take more pictures because it fits in my pocket, but I know I'm taking as good or better shots than everybody around me with the big cameras.      Ricoh did everything right with this camera and you will not be disappointed. Just to make sure I was not being deceived by the LCD, I had about 35-40 pictures developed at the local Wal-Mart and even though the quality of the one hr processing was substandard the pictures turned out good. Imagine how much better they'll be if processed with higher standards. I love my Ricoh GR digital III.    (edit) 2011 I have since gone back to my original 4 starts rating. The picture quality is just goo good, for such a small camera and the shutter speed is fast. Wish I could take better pictures with the manual settings. I just have to work with it a little more to get it. I now take this everywhere.     (edit) 2010 I now have knocked it down to 3 stars. Wish I could give a 3.5 rating because I would. product_title: Datacolor DC S3X100 Spyder 3 Express
review_body:
After installing the software, you plug in the device and after the USB drivers initialize you proceed to run the Spyder 3 Express software. Well, the drivers would not initialize properly in my Windows XP SP3 system with all the latest patches.

I uninstalled the drivers and re-plugged the device with the same result. The system reports a problem, says it can't initialize the drivers and gives an error number of 37, a standard Windows message.

Completely uninstalling with deep removal software and re-installation yielded the same results.

I even downloaded the latest software/drivers from Datacolor and re-installed after a complete uninstallation -- still not working.

I've been in the computer industry for 35 years as a software engineer, systems analyst, MSFT beta tester, design engineer and computer scientist. I only spent 2-3 hours fiddling with this package but I don't think it deserves more effort.

It's a poor design. Rather than generate a standard color configuration file readable by other software, it generates it's own file, and requires that you run a program in the background all the time. It leaves yet another icon in your systray, and if you stop the background program, your calibration isn't honored and the correction disappears.

Even though the background program is small and does't use many CPU cycles, it's another layer of complication added to your computer, which may already have more than enough complications.

I didn't test this but the program requires strict registration using a product key, so there may be no way you can use it to correct all your computers by moving the device from one to another. You might need to buy a Spyder for each of your computers. I never got far enough to register my copy via the Internet and so didn't attempt to try it on another computer.

Not using standard color configuration files and requiring a constant background utility is show-stopping enough for me. Add to that the fragility of the software with its inability to initialize on a standard XP SP3 computer and you get a package better left to die.

Fortunately, I bought this through Amazon and they stand behind their products so returning the item was far simpler than using it. One star for Spyder3Express, but five stars for Amazon.oftware with its inability to initialize on a standard XP SP3 computer and you get a package better left to die. Fortunately, I bought this through Amazon and they stand behind their products so returning the item was far simpler than using it. One star for Spyder3Express, but five stars for Amazon.

product_title: Celestron 21063 AstroMaster 90 AZ Refractor Telescope
review_headline: This is an excellent starter telescope
review_body: I bought this telescope last Christmas for my family. I have one daughter, age 7. I did a lot of research around the Internet and this product appeared to be a good starter telescope at the right price. (Incidentally, I paid $69.99 on amazon just before Christmas last year, so clearly prices on electronics change as much as airfares!) We are VERY satisfied. It's perfect for families just beginning to explore the stars/planets/moon with their young ones. It also was easy to assemble. Those who've criticized the parts for being less than perfect are probably right -- but then again, they probably want to be buying a telescope in the $100-$200 range or higher. The parts are fine. Sturdy enough for family use. The tripod works well. We live in Northwest Ohio where our clearest nights tend to be early fall and during extremely cold January/February. So, indeed, our biggest challenge has been recognizing a clear night when we have one. If you're doing this for the first time, work toward finding the moon first. Once I was able to master getting the moon into view, I was able to work on trying to see a planet. Tonight we saw Jupiter and four of its moons! We even saw a ring around Jupiter. Seeing the stars is harder with this unit, though. But we are thrilled enough to see parts of our own solar system. product_title: Fotodiox Pro 40"x60" 5-in-1 Collapsible Reflector Kit with stand
review_body: After struggling for an hour to connect the arm, I realized that the   clip on the far end of the arm can be slipped off. You can pull out the   plug at the end of the tube. Make sure you have the finger strength to fully  retract the clip.    1. Attach the fixed clip that will be closest to the stand to the edge of the reflector by  angling in one side and slipping in the other. let the clip seat properly. You  may need to move the fabric a bit for the clip to get a good grip.    2. Extend the sections of the arm so that the end of the arm extends just to the other   edge of the reflector.     3. Take the clip that you removed from the arm and attach it to the frame at the spot  where the end of the arm is positioned. You can now position the arm (by adjusting its length)  so that it can go through the clip.     4. Before you tighten everything, adjust the sections of the arm so that you have plenty of tubing to insert into the lightstand clamp; having extra tubing extending through the clamp  will give you something to grab and some leverage if you need to make adjustments to height  or the angle that the arm is holding once it has to bear the weight of the reflector.     5. Tighten up all the parts of the arm to make it rigid.    6. Replace the plug (or lose it).    7. Struggle to get the arm with the reflector on it onto the lightstand.        Notes:     Pay attention as to where you put the first clip -- in some situations you may  want the arm high up on the reflector. The arm goes directly across the reflector, not   on an angle.    When setting up the rig, position a leg of the light stand so it falls  directly under the arm. This will help to prevent the stand from tipping -- but  is no substitute for sandbags (which should be used even in the studio). If you don't want to carry around sandbags, two full 2 liter Coke bottles tied together weigh 9lbs./4kg. There's also the Reliance Fold-A-Carrier Water Carrier - 5 Gallon= 50lbs.    The clamp that holds the arm to the lightstand isn't very good but does the job. Make sure you  know how it works before you make your attachments to the reflector because once the arm is  on, it can be a bit clumsy to manipulate.    PS: If you can't get the reflector to collapse so it fits in the bag, search google using  \\"folding a photo reflector\\". There are a few videos that show how it's done.

product_title: Kodak EasyShare P750 7-inch Digital Picture Frame
review_body: I bought this picture frame for my mom. I needed something that is simple to use and \\"just works\\".  We like the frame itself. It is modern and compact (small overall size comparing to picture area). I like the way it automatically rotates pictures when the frame is rotated. The only problem that doing that, it is easy to press the buttons on the back of the frame. If it happens, my mom gets confused what to do next (i.e. how to return to slide mode). Also, the buttons on the back, and particularly the d-pad, are difficult for her to use. Fortunately, there is also a remote with visible and better buttons.  When it comes to hardware, I particularly appreciate the large internal 2GB memory. But not just memory. While the copy process is very slow, it does wonders to space utilization. I guess it must be resizing the pictures to match the frame resolution. Anyway, my estimate is that the frame can fit about 10,000 pictures, regardless of their original total size.  The weak part of the frame is the software. The menus are not very intuitive. One cannot use or manage internal memory when external one is connected. I still don't know what the search command does. However, my main complain and the sole reason I took 2 stars off my rating is the picture order. And not only because the picture order selection is hidden deep in the Tools menu.  When viewing pictures, the base order I like to use is by date taken. The frame offers 3 choices: random, by name, and by date. Random is good, but not for me now. By name is not useful for me, as my collection includes pictures from multiple cameras, with different naming conventions. By date should be the choice. BUT IT DOESN'T WORK!!!  I selected order by date and I was puzzled why the pictures come out in seemingly random order. Finally, I think I found it. My picture collection was copied from a computer. I did a lot of editing on the computer, including picture rotation, labeling, etc. Apparently, the frame uses \\"last modified\\"timestamp, not \\"picture taken\\" one. Any time I touch the picture on the computer (e.g. to rotate it), \\"last modified\\" timestamp changes. This causes the frame to show the pictures in semi-random order. It wouldn't be a problem had the pictures come directly from a (Kodak) camera, but I expect the frame to be a bit more universal. My only hope is that Kodak will issue a frame software update.

product_title: Nikon D7000 16.2 Megapixel Digital SLR Camera with 18-105mm  Lens (Black)
review_body: I had a D300S and a D700.  I never could develop a liking for the D300s.  It felt bulky and the video was just poor.  With nothing but FX lenses in my collection, I wanted a lightweight DX camera that I could just grab and go with one of my FX lenses on it.  After handling the D7000, I knew that it would easily replace the D300s without any loss in picture quality (a gain, instead) but with a loss of about 150 grams of dead weight.  The D7000 is, to me anyway, a lightweight camera that provides images that are nearly the same quality as I get from the D700.  Of course, the D700 is full-frame and that generally provides better and deeper image quality.  Nevertheless, when I compared pictures taken at the same focal length, same f=stop, same shutter speed, and same ISO using a D700 and a D7000, I had a hard time telling the difference from a small 100% crop from the image.  The extra 4 megapixels make a huge difference with Nikon's EXPEED 2 processor.  I've already placed in a few photo contests locally with pictures taken with the D7000.  The images are that high quality.    In short, if you are deciding between a D300s and a D7000, the decision is a no-brainer.  The D300s isn't worth the price difference.  I consider the D7000 to be an upgrade of both the D90 and the D300s.

There's some more stuff about nominal voltages, etc. ...again, not a battery guy; but you guess you're paying $30 for a battery that's $150 on newegg. I wouldn't predict the highest quality cells and I will not run the risk of a battery crapping out on me due to connection failure from improper voltage.     Looks like a good strong battery, even the back connectors are on par with those of a genuine Canon brand battery. Still, I urge you to check your batteries and make sure they're the same as advertised. There's tons of sellers on here giving out these knock off brand decoded batteries, not saying they're all bad, just urging ppl to be careful. product_title: Macally iCamDVR2 Securityman Internet Monitoring System and Video Recording
review_headline: Poor camera quality; internet setup issues
review_body: Skip to the bottom for short version.    I did lots of research before buying.  I wanted multiple cameras and didn't mind hiding them myself.  This product posted more technical data than any other, and the Tech Support guys were very helpful answering questions even before I purchased their product.  I only found 3 reviews and they weren't very good, but I was willing to take a chance, especially with the very reasonable price.    The first problem is very poor image quality from the cameras.  Whether I hook them up to my PC through iCamDVR or directly to my television, they produce an image that is nearly unusable with good indoor lighting.  These cameras require outdoor lighting or something like it to produce a reasonable image.     Also, the wireless signal from one camera interfered with the other, creating moving lines across the screen if both were plugged in.  I could live with this flaw if it were the only.    I decided to return the cameras, but not before tinkering with the iCamDVR.  To test image quality, I hooked up a DVD player.  Image quality on the PC through iCamDVR was very good.  I also tried viewing remotely through my Mac laptop, which runs Windows XP SP2 (You must have windows to host or view remotely).  After enabling all Active X controls, I was able to remotely download the software from PC to Mac, but I was never able to get past a pixel error to view the camera remotely.  The Tech Support guys are troubleshooting that now, and if they figure out the problem, I will buy an iCamDVR without the cameras.  I still may have another problem with remote viewing, in that the Tech guys were unable to ping my computer (I remoted in from inside my house, which is different than from outside).  I'm using a wireless router and thought I had all the port forwarding setup, but it's not working.  I'm not too worried though, because the Tech Support guys are very helpful and I think we'll figure it out.  Nonetheless, setting up this system is harder than Ianticipated.  I have average computer knowledge, but I've had to learn about dynamic IP address versus static IP address, port forwarding on my router, and other topics I never before needed to learn.      I wish that viewing remotely only required the IP address and password, so that all you needed was a web browser.  Instead, you have to install software on the remote viewing computer.  Therefore, you will be unable to view remotely from many computers (public computers, Macs, any place where you don't want to or can't install software).      Therefore:  ----------    Amazon - Delivery and support:  Great.  Return policy is outstanding.    SecurityMan (iCamDVR) Tech Support - Very helpful, although we haven't yet resolved hosting / remote viewing issues.    Cameras - Very low image quality.  Requirement for strong light makes these better for outdoors.    iCamDVR - Complicated setup for web hosting and remote viewing.  Depending on your Internet Service Provider (ISP) and router, yours may be complicated.  If I gain confidence that Tech Support knows why I couldn't view remotely, I'll by an iCamDVR without the cameras and use with some other cameras.  I'll update my review later.

product_title: Digital Holster Harness
review_headline: Good but not what it should be
review_body: I use this harness to mount a Tamrac 5765 on the chest. This is a vastly superior way to carry a small kit while walking. It allows convenient access for lens, memory card, battery and filter changes, and makes the weight all but invisible. Standing, sitting, walking, climbing, it seldom gets in the way, and is protected from damage and theft.    This is essentially two mid size shoulder straps with metal clasps on each end, padding and extra adjustability. They can be used singly when traveling, or used as suspenders for an accessory belt. It is a definite improvement over using two full size shoulder straps or a small binocular harness for the same purpose.    As a harness it lacks a piece to connect the straps together where they cross at your upper back. As a result, the bag tilts from side to side, the straps are hard to put on, and the straps are less secure on the shoulders. I also carry a tripod in a holster on my back, but I inevitably get tangled in all the straps.    The system also has no provision for accessory mounts for things like a filter pouch, cell phone holder etc. These things can be jury-rigged, but this should not be necessary.    Materials and manufacturing choices consider environmental impact.

product_title: Canon SX30IS 14.1MP Digital Camera with 35x Wide Angle Optical Image Stabilized Zoom and 2.7 Inch Wide LCD (OLD MODEL)
review_headline: Amazing camera! Well worth the wait!!!
review_body:
I scouted the camera's release back in September and have been waiting impatiently for it's arrival in early October! I finally got it last week and couldn't be more pleased! I've taken well over 2000 pics and at least 20 videos so far. Can't seem to put it down (literally- i've yet to use a tripod, even at 35 and 140x zooms)! I have shaky hands, so I was pleasantly surprised at the quality in any shooting situation! The zoom seems to be the most reviewed feature, but this thing is far from done there! It has a million features from fully automated shooting to complete manual functionality! Tons of effects and modes (check Canon's site). I had looked at several DSLR cameras, and even tested a few out, and for beginner to intermediate usage this camera is gonna be tough to beat! Especially with that price tag. Here are some of the features that appealed to me: 14.1 MP, 35x wide angle zoom, 720p HD video, TV, AV , Manual mode (especially this- complete control of aperture, shutter, and focus), all the common photo effects, 4.5 stop Image Stabilization. If you're looking for a professional quality camera, but aren't ready for DSLR pricing this is the camera to own! You won't be disappointed!!

UPDATE 10/26/10:
I have taken well over 4000 pics now. Still loving the overall performance and quality. I don't own previous versions of this camera so I can't compare it to the other models.
I sent about 50 shots in to be printed turned out amazing on 4x6 and 5x7. 8x10's to follow soon!
Anybody interested in lens accessories, i found a link on another review for this site:
[...]
They have some great options for all three versions of this camera (as well as some other brands). I just ordered the 58mm filter adapter and the Hoya HMC Circular Polarizer (6 coats) 58mm. should be here this week. i'll update on those. should help a lot with my landscape shots!

product_title: Looxcie Wearable Bluetooth Camcorder System, Android Compatible (Black)
review_body:
The Android app for Looxcie (without which you can't really use the device) is infuriatingly unpolished:

(1) it does not use Android Intents for sending email or uploading videos to Youtube (ie rather than using the Android-provided facilities for this they implemented their own; for example they require your Gmail password; the only way around that is to create a separate Gmail account just for the Looxcie app)

(2) the UI for browsing the circular video buffer has many issues: it is sluggish, the position slider is too inaccurate to easily select a scene within the 4 hours of recorded video, when you click \\"create new clip\\" the position jumps so if you had carefully navigated to the beginning of an interesting scene you have to start over again)

(3) when uploading the video fails, retrying means that the app downloads the clip yet again over Bluetooth

(4) when you create a new clip and give it a title, the title is not reflected in the file name on the flash disk presented to a connected computer

This would all be tolerable if the app were open source or at least the Bluetooth protocol documented -- as it stands, Looxcie officially says that they have no intention of opening up the product but instead intend to keep it a completely closed system.

Regarding the hardware: there is no motion stabilization and no wind protection for the microphone. This means when you take a movie while bicycling, you can all but forget about the sound and watching the video clip is bound to make you seasick. It also appears that the Looxcie has a hard time keeping up with rapid changes of the pictures -- you'll see the image shearing.

This will keep moisture from getting into the housing and fogging up the inside of the glass.     Also, Rain-x on the outside of the glass to keep it clear during and after a rain.

product_title: Lowepro Pro Trekker 300 AW Camera Backpack (Mica/Black)
review_headline: Well built, ergo, and back friendly
review_body:
I recently purchased the 300mm F2.8 lens. Therefore needed another backpack in addition to my classic trekker Lowerpro. After reading many reviews, I settled on this bag. I am glad I did because -

1. It is built strong. I can tell by the quality, and from experience with other Lowepro bags, this ones a very strong bag. The zip is strong and covered.
2. I easily packed in 5D MII, 300mm f2.8, 24-105 f4, 17-35 f2.8, 1.4X TC, 85mm f1.8, 50mm f1.8, and 1 flash 580 EX II in the camera compartment.
I packed a 13 inch laptop and an ipad in the computer section without the computer pouch.
3. There's a seperate fairly large waist pouch which attaches to the bag. It can easily hold spare cables, batteries, memory cards, etc.
4. There's a shoulder adjustment chart provided. After some adjustment, I didn't find the load on my back as unbearable. I find this backpack to be comfortable.
5. There are compartments at the side for putting in things like sunglasses, passport etc.
6. A better way to carry tripod as there is provision to securely carry your tripod.

A few caveats -
a. The empty bag itself weighs quite a fair bit.
b. The strong zip are hard to pull which to me is good but can be a pain if you want to open it in a hurry
c. Some other reviewer mentioned the hydration is an extra optional accessory. For me this is not an issue.
d. It's on the pricier side

All in all, this bag is probably going to last me a very long time and serve me well. I love it for whatever period of time I have used it thus far.

product_title: Fujifilm FinePix Real 3D W3 Digital Camera with 3.5-Inch LCD (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body: We bought a 3DTV last month and have become 3D addicts. We needed to add to our growing 3D collection and while we had high expectations of this camera, we were apprehensive. Since getting it in the mail yesterday, I have had a really difficult time putting it down. If you have 3D skeptics and scoffers in your life or you just want to add to your currently limited 3D options, I highly recommmend this camera.     A few things I want to cover from reviews that I have read:    We were excited to review the pictures we took on the nice-sized LCD display in full 3D without the use of glasses and we were not disappointed! This is, in my opinion, the biggest WOW of the camera. The size of the screen is equivalent to the display on the iPod Touch and while, yes, you need to look at the screen from the right angle, the 3D JUMPS out of the camera. Showing off your 3D photos from your camera is sure to leave people astonished and trying to grab the images.     My experience with battery life is similar to what I've been reading...I definitely suggest ordering a backup.     Macro shots...there have been mixed reviews on this. My experience, at first, was disappointment. I immediately wanted to take up close shots of everything, but the crosstalk or \\"ghosting\\" was at an eye-straining level. However, upon using the advanced 3D settings and a couple of tries, I find the Macro shots to really impress! I find myself gathering up things to shoot and with a little trial and error, I'm already (one day later) close to having this mastered.     I agree that the best shots are taken from further away. Taking pictures from above your subject really shows off the 3D and the depth of your pictures. I took a shot of a tall vase from above and when I showed it to someone, they said it looked like the vase was sitting on the LCD screen.     On the TV, I have not been extremely impressed, but I am hoping it will take some learning as well. The convergence seems to differ too much from the camera to the tv. That said, I took some shots of a sculpture park in my city while it was snowing and the depth is impressive. It looks like snow is coming out of my tv screen.     I have only played around with the video so far...it's gonna take some practice. A lot of crosstalk as of yet, but I anticipate that once I learn to effectively utilize it, it will be a fun feature as well.     I'm looking forward to ordering prints and I'm planning on getting a 3D digital frame to showcase the amazing shots I've taken.     If you are a 3D fanatic and enthusiast, I really think the Fujifilm FinePix Real 3D W3 cameran is sure to please!

They quickly replaced it and when this one was set up everything work perfectly. The Camera connects and records to the WirelessSpace no problem and it is separated from any other network so only people with access to the wireless signal can get to the camera. Its a great little system and comes in for less that 500 for the whole setup. Considering every other system we looked at was in the thousands of dollars range I would say this is a Great solution for our needs and just might be the solution for you. review_body: Purchased this item from a local retailer. I had some expectations based purely on the Sony brand. I took it home and did a side-by-side comparison with a 3 year old Canon Powershot point-and-shoot camera in video mode, and a 2-1/2 year old Aiptek 720HD flash video recorder. The Sony DCR-SX44 was by far the worse performing. Considering that the Sony only had to beat out a 3 year old camera and 2+ year old low-end video recorder, both of which were in the same price range when purchased, I was disappointed with its performance. I recorded with them all in the same setting -- low light indoor environment. The canon and aiptek produced relatively sharp video. The Sony produced a blurry video, way below acceptable threshold for me. The Sony did record the best audio, and the image stabilization seemed good to me. I tested the playback on a small screen, a window on a pc monitor, so that the test would not unfairly bias the results in favor of the higher definition of the other recorders. Still, even on a small screen, the Sony image quality was by far the worst. In general, I still like many Sony products, and this won't stop me from trying other products from them.

product_title: Sigma 85mm f/1.4 EX DG HSM Large Aperture Medium Telephoto Prime Lens
review_headline: A Sigma that rivals the Canon 85 1.4!
review_body: I am a pro wedding photographer who shoots primarily with zooms. I use prime lenses more as specialty lenses when I want to narrow depth of field or in extreme darkness. I own the Canon 85 1.8, itself an excellent lens, and rented a Canon 85 1.2L, a fabled Canon staple. The Sigma is actually better than the 85 1.8 at large apertures and rivals the Canon 85L in almost all respects. Compared to the Canon 85L, the Sigma is slightly more compact and lightweight. It's build is similar to my Canon 35 1.4L. More importantly, the Sigma focuses faster on all of my cameras--5D, 5DII, and the 50D. The Canon L has the advantage of being weather sealed and accepted by Canon Professional Services for pros who are members. The Canon 85L is also unique in that it opens to 1.2 rather than just 1.4.     The Sigma autofocuses faster than the Canon L and almost as fast as the Canon 85 1.8. There have been reports of this lens hunting, having seizures, and making squeaking noises. If your copy of the Sigma does any of these things, return it immediately as you definitely have a dud copy. Mine rarely ever hunts, the autofocus is smooth, quiet, and accurate. The lens is tack sharp even at 1.4--as sharp as the Canon 85L at wide apertures and with similar color and contrast. Like with 85 1.2L, the depth of field wide open is razor thin and requires precise precision in where to put the point of sharpest focus. The faster focus of the Sigma does help in attaining accurate focus quickly.    In summary, I feel Sigma got it right with this lens. It is truly an alternative to the 85L at half the cost with similar image quality and actually faster focus. The Sigma does have a different bokeh than the Canon L. Not necessarily better or worse, just different. The Canon 85L may be slightly better to tame restless backgrounds with smooth bokeh than the Sigma but the difference is small. The Sigma then offers a more compact and faster focusing alternative to the pricey 85 1.2L for both the pro and advanced amateur photographer.

review_headline: Best lens for Full-Frame camera period!
review_body: Let me start the review by saying that I personally like to change my photo gear very often, and I have gone through most of the L / EF lenses that Canon has, in addition to a few nikon bodies/lenses. With so many positive reviews said about 85LII, I thought this lens is a must-have after moving to 5DII and selling my 7D camera. And I'm glad I did. There are many disadvantages to this lens, as most of the have been previously mentioned. I am a former user of 85mm f/1.8 USM lens, so I can compare the two.   Let me start with the CONS first:   - Heavy and bulky - This lens weights more than the \\"Brick\\" 24-70L  - Rear element is very close to the lens body, meaning it's on the same level. It makes it swapping lenses in a hurry quickly virtually impossible without a fear of damaging it.   - AF....Yes, the good old Auto-Focus is still slow. There's so much glass to move inside, that it looks like it's pushing it's best, but still not fast enough to capture a moving subject. Although, after enough practice, I was even able to shoot a ballroom dance competition with it :) Who knows?!  - CA. Just like the 85mm f/1.8, CA levels are still high, although much better (less purple fringing) than on the f/1.8 version.   Now, after mentioning the important CONS, and trying to persuade you not to buy the lens, let me tell you about the PROS:   - Shallow depth of field. Yes, this lens has the most dreamy bokeh I've ever seen. It's a magical effect that no other lens can match. (That is considering you've had enough time to play around with the AF and learn how to get your images in focus @ f/1.2. Believe me, this is not an easy task to do and requires some practice).   - AF in low light. Although the motor itself is slow, the lens can focus in candle-light. I've tried it myself, and it's amazing how it doesn't require much light to focus.   - Color saturation is one of the best I've seen. f/1.8 doesn't come close with shots out of the camera.     All in all, this might be the best lens I've ever owned. Given it's CONS, I am still fascinated by the images it produces. It made me a much better photographer (yes, I admit it:)! And it looks like every image straight out of the camera is a keeper. I've changed my gear around, sold various lenses, bought more lenses, but 85LII always stays in my bag or on the camera. This lens is a keeper!

review_headline: A slightly above Average Rating of a slightly above Average quality Grip

The other reason I call this grip average is due to its lack of weather protection. I have read that the Canon grips are weather protected. That is a huge factor for someone who may have to shoot in the rain, snow or sand....

Considering all of these factors, I am still looking at buying a new Zeikos grip for my 7D. So as you can see, for me the Pros far outweigh the Cons, but for others it may make more sense to go Canon.

product_title: 58mm Snap-On Universal Lens Cap
review_headline: A comparison of three different inexpensive 58mm lens caps
review_body: I purchased three different inexpensive 58mm caps from Amazon at the same time: (1) this cap, (2) Fotodiox Inner pinch Lens Cap with Cap Keeper, 58mm and (3) the Zeikos ZE-LC58 58mm Plastic Snap On Lens Cap (Black). All arrived relatively quickly.     This lens cap, although a little thicker than a flexible press-on, works well with my DSLR manufacturer's 58mm filter-size lenses. It has a larger gripping surface than the original caps provided with those lenses, and so stays in place. Its tether is easy to connect to the triangular metal rings of my DSLR, and it's relatively long so that it's no problem connecting even with long lenses. It hangs significantly below the camera when removed from the lens. The clamping mechanism has more travel than my original lens caps. It works both directly on the lenses and on attached filters. Two minor issues (1) as the tether is made of string, it can occasionally catch under the clamping mechanism if its not free to hang, and (2) the clamping mechanism, at least on my copy, is a bit harder to squeeze than the cap on my DSLR manufacturer's lens and some competitors, so it requires a bit more pressure to install or remove.     Bottom Line: If you need a tether pass on the tether-less Zeikos ZE-LC58 58mm Plastic Snap On Lens Cap. The Universal is a nice cap and I would consider buying it again.  It has a sturdy grip and long enough tether to work with 58mm filter-size telephotos.  However, the Fotodiox Inner pinch Lens Cap is possibly a better choice if you have larger fingers and may have trouble squeezing a tighter pinch mechanism. That cap's  pinch mechanism is somewhat easier to use. However, I was able to use both caps comfortably.      Just remember that a tethered cap stays with the camera not with the lens. Thus, it's advisable to leave an extra 58mm cap in your camera bag for those times you remove a 58mm filter-size lens for one with a different filter-size thread.

I wasn't able to get more than 30 minutes of battery life with the knock off, even after conditioning the battery. The real one goes for an hour.    As I said, I have not bought this particular product from this seller so maybe it's a real thing. I'm not sure how returns work when you buy outside of Amazon fulfillment, but the advantage of buying through Amazon fulfillment is that the return of my knock off pen was painless. product_title: Panasonic HDC-TM700K Hi-Def Camcorder with Pro Control System & 32GB Internal Flash Memory (Black)
review_headline: TM700K's audio quality and fan noise
review_body: Many reviews on amazon.com (including one of the most \\"helpful\\" ones) have claimed that the camera's major flaw, or one of them, is its fan noise. I don't think those claims really have much merit.      1) When we are recording normal dialogs, everyday activities, street events, music performances, etc., our human ears can hardly discern the faint sound of a tiny fan (unless it's broken in a way it generates loud noise), because the signal to noise ratio is usually way too high.  The dynamic range of TM700K's built-in mic is quite limited.  So if it records normal everyday sound sources at a proper audio level, the sound of TM700K's tiny fan can only be too hard to hear.      2) In a quiet environment where everything is quiet, many reviews seem to assume they can (or should) hear the fan noise.  But I strongly doubt that's really what they believe they have heard or can hear.  Auto audio gain is used when shooting TM700k in auto mode.  In this mode, the so-called fan noise in a quiet setup is mostly what the camera artificially generates.  When everything is quiet, the camera in auto mode thinks the sound source is just too quiet, so it will try to boost the audio level of the non-existent sound source as much as it can. This essentially treats everything as the sound source, and ends up boosting the noise level across the entire otherwise quiet recording.  The net result is that the camera makes a quiet environment noisy.  To our ears, such noise is similar to the sound of a fan.    If you are an experienced photographer, you know that just by boosting ISO, you can make an otherwise dark scene look like well lit in the final photo. Raising ISO boosts a camera's sensitivity to light, while raising audio gain boosts the camera's sensitivity to sound.  With shutter speed and aperture/iris unchanged, extra high ISO adds significant lighting (along with digital noise) to the visual recording, while extra audio gain adds significant audio boost (along with audible noises) to the recorded audio.    The same fan-like noise can be heard on fan-less camcorders and latest DSLR cameras in video mode, such as Canon 5D Mark II. Surely, we can't blame a fan-less camera's built-in fan for the noise, because it does not have a fan.  In those cases, most people can easily figure out the real culprit, which is extra audio gain in auto mode when there is no distinct sound source due to everything being quiet.      3) Of course, the sound from TM700's tiny fan does exist.  But it is so quiet that it can be considered as part of the self noise of TM700's built-in audio processing chain.  Every mic (including the quietest studio mic in the world, Rode NT1A, whose self noise is 5db), and every recording gear/setup using mics, produce a certain amount of self noise (also known as system noise). All the noises will add up in the overall noise of the final audio. And the way the mics are used typically significantly contribute to the overall noise of the recording.    We may suppose that every fan has to be something noisy.  But the reality is: even without a nearby tiny fan, all consumer-grade mics are noisy on their own (at least noisier than professional mics in typical comparable scenarios). And typically, there is no way to re-route the original mic signal to a professional quality amplifier for better processing. As a result, as most must have noticed, video clips from low-end video recorders such as cell phones and cheap cameras tend to be very noisy, regardless where the clips were shot.  In most cases, such noises have nothing to do with a fan. And in the case of TM700K, we just happen to see a fan that some can place the blame entirely on.    Even if we don't agree that the fan noise can be considered as part of the system noise, don't forget there are numerous other noises just like the so-called fan noise in this case. For example, when we breathe, when our lips fast move while speaking, when our heart beats... we generate noises that canbe heard by everyone with no hearing problems.  They are (or can become) much louder than TM700's tiny fan.  A consumer-grade camera is typically used within an arm's length from the shooter. So, no doubt, the shooter contributes to the overall noise in the final audio too.  If we blame the tiny fan for the audio noise of TM700's recording, why shouldn't we blame our breathing, lip moving, heart beating, etc., for the overall audio noise?    A more reasonable claim is to state that the fan adds a little extra noise to the final recording, while admitting the fan noise is just a part of the overall noise and is generally too quiet to discern by our ears.      4) My personal experience:    Since I bought my TM700K last summer (as of 4/2011), I have shot over 4000 clips with this camera, as reported by HD Writer (the software that came with the camera). I have repeatedly produced (near) noise-free sound recordings with my TM700 camcorder in a reasonably quiet environment. I consider my TM700 5.1 mic to be a piece of top-notch recording gear.     I have several professional-grade mics, such as Rode NTG-3/NT4/NT2000 and AT 4053b. They are good for their intended purposes. If used as intended, they can produce broadcast-quality audio recordings. If used improperly, they can feel like most disappointing junk too. For capturing live sound as we would hear it right at the spot of the recording camcorder, TM700K (when used as a 5.1 surround sound mic) is much better than other professional mics I have (including Rode NT4, which is one of the best stereo mics in the world).  I wish I could tear it from the camcorder such that I could use it as a standalone mic along with my high-quality recording gear.    - How do I know a sound clip is (near) noise free?  I use Sennheiser HD-25 II (a pair of high-quality headphones) and get audio signal from a 7.1 sound system that produces near zero audible self noise. Turn up the volume. If I can't hear obvious noise, it's noise-free (at least to my ears).  In theory, certain noises always exist - that's for sure.  But in practice, what really matters is whether we can hear them, or whether we can record audio in a way that we can't hear them.      5) How to get (near) noise-free sound recordings with TM700K?    First and foremost, you must switch away from auto mode (IA). And use manual mode instead. Otherwise, as explained above, the camera will always try to make a quiet environment (including brief quiet intervals during speech pauses) appear to be noisy, just like a still camera in auto mode will always try to make a dark scene appear well lit in the final photo.      Here's what you most likely have to do to get near noise-free audio from TM700K:    a) Dig into the menu to adjust the mic level down (-9db to -15db works for me most time)    b) Turn on low cut filter when you hear undesirable rumbling sounds - unless that's what you intend to record (so, for an example, in the case of recording a piano play, don't use this filter).    c) Do your recording in an environment where the sound source is significantly louder than other sounds (noises).    d) If your sound source is quieter than, or about as loud/quiet as, the overall noise, you can i) change the surround mic setting, in the hope that other mic types (such as zoom mic) will have stronger audio signal along the axis of the camera's focusing; or ii) move your camera closer to the sound source (you can't move the mic without moving the camera).  Keep in mind though: if the sound source can't stand out in the recording environment, or if you just can't make it stand out, your options to record clear audio with TM700's built-in mic will be very limited, and you will end up having noisy recordings no matter what. The only remedy is to not use your TM700 for audio recording purposes (or use it just as a low-quality backup).      6) Keep this in mind: professional audio work is almost never done using an on-camera mic (whether built-in mics or an external mic mounted on camera), no matter how good the mic is (a really good mic can cost 1000s of $$$).  A news crew may appear to use on-camera mics all the time, but that's for the purpose of capturing ambient sounds (a.k.a., ambient noises), plus giving them a handy fallback just in case their off-camera audio system fails.      7) As far as audio recording is concerned, TM700's major drawbacks include:     a) the mic has relatively poor dynamic range so it's very easy to have audio clippings    b) there is no built-in quality limiter against audio clippings.    c) there is no way to adjust audio level on the fly - Panasonic should have added an audio-level icon when this camera is used in manual mode.  It does allow you to see the audio level, but unfortunately you just can't adjust it without stopping recording first.        == Overall conclusion ==    TM700 is capable of producing (near) noise-free 5.1 live sound recordings.    However,  in most recording scenarios, it's up to the shooter to use the camera in a proper way to make that happen, or understand limitations of the built-in mic and know when that will not happen.  Hopefully, my review is helpful in getting better audio out of this fantastic little camera.

I bought the A700 camera just because it's rooted in Minolta Konica engineering (and because I can use my existing Minolta lenses without buying more lenses).      But, Sony took photography technology more seriously than I thought.  I am very please with the A700 camera, now I'm very please with this lense.    Sharpness: normally worst at max zoom.  But at 400mm I took a picture of a bird about 30 feet away, the cropped image was as razor sharp as similar image was taken with a good 50mm lense 3 feet away.    Autofocus is really fast and quiet, it focused so fast and quiet that I thought it didn't do anything, but everything was always in focus as I spanned the camera around.  Thanks to the SSM motor (SSM stands for SuperSonic Motor).  Having the focusing motor in the lense can reduce the strain on the focusing motor residing in the camera body.    If I have to complain about this lense, it would be its weight.  It's almost 4 lbs.  Adding your camera's weight on top of that you can't hold your camera steadily for long ! product_title: Panasonic HDC-TM700K Hi-Def Camcorder with Pro Control System & 32GB Internal Flash Memory (Black)
review_headline: Lots of weaknesses, doesn't beat competition in any area !
review_body: First of all I have been using this camera for about 2 weeks. I have only used it in 1080 60p mode since that is the only reason to buy this camera, its closest competitors have higher data rates in every other mode. My experience level is high, on a professional level.     I have encountered several issues that probably will result in returning the camera. Based on professional and consumer reviews I took the risk with this     camera despite it's current incompatibility with most consumer editing platforms. I thought if the image quality and low light performance are outstanding(as some have reported) it would be worth the hassle of transcoding etc.    Below are my findings.    1. Automatic white balance and the preset modes are totally unacceptable/unusable. In automatic mode it shifts noticeably worse than any camera I have ever used, In preset mode I could not find satisfactory setting for indoor lighting situations.  If you don't know what white balance is just suffice it to say that you will get unnatural/greenish skin tones and other color problems. Colors  will not be consistent and may change during a scene.    2. This camera has been praised for its low light capabilities. My results have been mediocre...When the zoom is on maximum wide and you shot with the iris fully open you can get acceptable results but once you zoom in and the aperture closes to 2.8 you are done. So if you are shooting a fairly well lit sporting or social event and cannot use additional lighting and need to use the zoom your results will be poor. I realize all camcorders have smaller apertures with zoom. For me this camcorder is a dog in low light    3. 1080 60p video is incompatible with most editing software.      4. I have only shot with an external mic so I cannot comment on the microphone/noise issue that many have reported. I used the Sennheiser mke400 and have been happy with the results given the price and size of the microphone.      5. Battery life is really bad.      My conclusion:     The video quality is good(but doesn't outclass the competition) but the low light performance is mediocre and the white balance very poor.       Given the need to transcode when using it's highest data rate.      And the lesser quality lCD relative to the competition(330k pixels vs 900k)      And the battery life is beyond pathetic. I did have luck with the aftermarket wasabi batteries sold here on Amazon.      And the risk of Audio problems many have reported.       Clearly this is an upgrade over any non hd camcorder (not in low light)    but has too many disadvantages and no area where it is clearly superior to the current competition.    I prefer the Sony CX550 or the Canon HF S21 in that order     (despite what camcorderinfo.com says)

product_title: Square Perfect Professional 3 Strobe Studio Flash & Softbox Set Photography Kit
review_headline: Good quality stuff for the price.
review_body:
I can't complain one bit about the strobes in this kit. The umbrellas were good too, would have liked a few more inches on radius but this will do fine. The soft boxes looked like trash or cheap until you put them together then they are totally functional and stout. I will leave mine put together all the time but it would be nice to have an easier way to fold them down for transport. The stands were of good quality and works just fine. The battery in the remote trigger (on the camera side) was dead on arrival but I did a search and found a package of five batteries for around $5 so I'm sure it will work fine then. The remote receiver uses two AAA batteries as well. The strobes will all work as slaves to a speedlight if you use manual mode which does not put out the pre-flash for such as red eye reduction, etc. Otherwise the strobes will sync with the pre-flash and not the flash itself and the shutter will snap after the strobes flash. Not a big deal as it's a flash problem not a strobe issue. The cases are nice as well. I do wish that the strobe caps were deep enough to keep the modeling lights in the strobe unit instead of having to take them out each time for transport and before you are able to put the cap on. The barn doors and snoots, filters, etc do a pretty good job as well. Medium quality for what it is.

I would highly recommend this kit to any starting photographer and/or semi-pro wanting a good strobe kit without spending thousands of dollars. A power strip included in this kit with a 12 foot extension would only enhance this kit.

product_title: Canon EF-S Focusing Screen for Canon EOS 40D Digital SLR Camera
review_headline: More benefits than just manual focus
review_body: I adapt Contax lenses to my 60D, and when using them with the Ef-A screen, not only was focus difficult to acquire, but metering was extremely irritating: Photos would overexpose at apertures faster than f/2.8 and underexpose at apertures slower than f/4. After switching the screens (an easy process), metering was perfectly consistent from f/2 to f/22, only overexposing a third of a stop at f/1.4.    For anyone shooting with adapted lenses, I cannot more highly recommend this.    Note that this screen can only display the depth of field of about an f/1.8 lens, and the visible bokeh appears as a hexagon at apertures larger than f/2. It's not a problem for focusing an f/1.4 lens, because images shimmer slightly when barely out of focus, almost like microprisms, but you will get more blur than what you see at f/1.4. In addition, for all lenses, the defocus blur isn't evenly lit, but instead speckled. Not a problem, per se, but it isn't exactly pleasing to look at.

I called Parrot support and they said they would be happy to fix it if I send it to them at my expense each way. That would have cost me about $75. The AR Drone seems really cool and is a great idea, but Parrot is apparently just not quite ready in its development of this product. Maybe in a few years I'll try again, but probably not. My Blade CX2 helicopter lifts my Kodak Playsport HD camera just fine, so I'll stick with that for aerial shots.  As usual, Amazon ROCKS in getting this thing to me and getting it back to them. I don't return many things I buy from Amazon, but it sure is nice to know that if I need to, they are so awesome in taking care of their customers.

product_title: Shoot Great Video with your Canon DSLR Camera (DVD)
review_headline: Really helpful, even if you know quite a bit about post-processing still images
review_body:
For many years I've been using Photoshop to process still images, and assumed that in processing video I would use the same tweaks for white balance, exposure, etc.

Video coming from the Canon dslrs is quite compressed, so every editing step we take in post-processing degrades the output. I learned how to get better results by optimizing my choice of subject locale and placement, use of best camera settings, and use of accessories such as tripods and microphones geared for video. Studio lighting is discussed as well.

I own another Blue Crane video, for my 580ex and 430ex Canon Speedlights, and found that one equally helpful.

Isabel

product_title: Sony Alpha NEX NEX5K Digital Camera with Interchangeable Lens
review_body:
I've shot with both DSLRs and rangefinders for the past 7 years, and I bought this hoping that it would be an easier camera to carry around when I just need to snap a few quick pictures. I've read generally positive reviews and thought I'd give it a try.

It's been a mixed bag from three days of shooting. The camera itself is not meant to be a replacement for a DSLR, or a point and shoot, or a rangefinder. It is not as fast as a DSLR, not nearly small enough to put in your pocket (although the 16mm lens might let you do it), and does not give you manual freedom or \\"connectedness\\" like a rangefinder.

The tactile feedback is very limited, and yes, the menu diving is annoying. The options in the menu are inconsistent depending on which camera mode you're on, and some options (like raw shooting) are absent when shooting certain modes like hand-held twilight, panorama, etc. I suppose this makes sense in terms of processing, however the camera doesn't explain that you need to be in another mode first in order to change these settings.

The video quality is fairly good. You have almost no control of the recording, however. Everything is automatic - you can tap the shutter to \\"refocus\\" the camera, but to me this just sends the camera on a wild AF hunt that blurs the video. The intelligent auto also works well for someone who just wants the camera to do all the work. The other modes, panorama, twilight, and the preset \\"styles\\" all work pretty good. Saves me the time of stitching pictures together!

The raw files from this camera are decent - but never on par with my a700, and certainly not on par with my m8 or m9. Most of this is due to the lens, I believe. The kit lens is very prone to all sorts of distortion, and never takes pictures that are exceptionally sharp. And another issue with the raw files is that they're incompatible with photo editing software currently available. (Doesn't work in LR3, Aperture, photoshop, etc) They can only be viewed on sony's software. Eventually the format will be added, but for now you're stuck with sony's proprietary software unless you want to convert these files to adobe DNG.

With all of that said, for $700 you do get value for what you pay for. The camera does take pictures that are far superior to any prosumer point and shoot, and slightly edges out my friend's panasonic GF1. The video is pretty nice for such a tiny camera, and toting it around is a lot easier than carrying a DSLR or a rangefinder. I really liked the tilt screen that reminded me of my old hasselblad. I can recommend this camera if you're looking for an upgrade to your point and shoot, but I can't recommend it as a replacement for a normal DSLR or rangefinder. The tactile feedback, speed, and manual controls simply aren't there.ware.
